Owner thinks the whole interface doesn't work: if the agent requests access, going to a weird settings page to approve doesn't work. Approvals should be IN the context of the agent or the task being done, not a settings page. ACCEPTANCE: the orphaned approvals settings section is removed; approval prompts surface in-context (in the agent/task that needs them). LANDED 0.2.313 (5f8931f3) — the orphaned Settings Approvals section, nav and wiring are removed; revoking a permission confirms in-context via runOwnerApprovedMutation. NOTE: this is the change that left scripts/chrome-journeys.ts driving a deleted section — see CAP-FB-20260827-MAIN-GATES-RED-02."
- id: CAP-FB-20260826-SYSTEM-PROMPT-01
  severity: P2
  status: merged
  summary: "Update the built-in default system prompt to be more accurate to the types of tasks it can do (now that the toolset grew to 130 tools). Also: the agent should ALWAYS search for the tool first — we have a search/list-tools (query_tools) capability; give more examples of search-then-execute, WITHOUT bloating the system prompt context. ACCEPTANCE: the default system prompt reflects the real toolset, instructs search-then-execute with query_tools examples, and stays context-bounded. LANDED 0.2.312 (d7ed500e) — the default system prompt instructs search-then-execute and carries accurate tool signatures."
- id: CAP-FB-20260826-HEADER-HOME-01
  severity: P3
  status: merged
  summary: "In the settings panel, clicking the 'Chrome agent platform' header should take you back to the homepage. Small UX affordance; pairs with BACK-STACK-01. LANDED 0.2.296 (c8730513) — the Settings brand click goes Home."
- id: CAP-FB-20260826-PERMISSIONS-SIMPLIFY-01
  severity: P0
  status: merged
  summary: "Owner (frustrated, P0): the permission system is a MESS. (1) The sorting-hat demo failed with 'Tab grouping write operations are pending owner tab-management permission enrollment in Settings' EVEN THOUGH all permissions are enabled — there are TWO confusing layers (the chrome API permission AND the separate expiring browser-control GRANT) and the owner can't tell which one to grant. (2) 'It should be asking me in context' — when a tool needs a permission/grant, the approval must surface IN the agent/task context, not send the owner to a Settings page. (3) Settings UI can't REMOVE a permission; the 'needs permission' security label never surfaces where to manage it. GOAL (owner's words): 'make it super simple and easy to use and understand.' REDESIGN: (a) ONE coherent mental model — when a tool needs something, an approval surfaces in-context ('This agent wants to group tabs — Allow?') and one click grants what's needed; (b) diagnose why the demo said 'pending enrollment' despite enabled permissions (which layer failed — is the grant expiring/not-set, is tabGroups separate from tabs and un-granted, or a real detection bug?); (c) Settings becomes a clear inventory — every permission with a plain-English label + what it enables + a working add/remove toggle, and 'needs permission' labels link to the exact control; (d) the in-context approval is the primary path, Settings is the management/inventory path. ACCEPTANCE: the sorting-hat demo works after a single in-context approval; every permission is add/removable in Settings with a plain-English label; no 'pending enrollment' dead-ends. LANDED 0.2.303 (0856225f) + 0.2.313 (5f8931f3) — in-context approval cards for tool permission/grant denials; one click grants exactly the needed scope and retries; deny is sticky; the Settings dead-end is gone. The tabGroups half of the sorting-hat failure was a genuinely undeclared permission, fixed at 0.2.290."
- id: CAP-FB-20260826-BROWSER-SINGLE-DRIVER-01
  severity: P1
  status: merged
  summary: "Owner requirement (2026-08-26): with many NTPs/surfaces open, ONLY ONE may issue browser commands at a time. Today the grantMutex serializes the grant-check+mutation per-tool in the SW realm, but nothing arbitrates WHICH surface drives — multiple NTPs can interleave destructive commands from different agents. DESIGN: a SW-owned, durable, expiring BROWSER-CONTROL SESSION LEASE — a single holder keyed by surface/run; a surface must hold the lease to issue destructive browser commands; a competing surface gets an honest 'another surface is driving the browser' result (or a bounded queue); released on task end / surface close / expiry. In the worker architecture the lease authority stays in the SW and each agent worker requests the lease before driving the browser (recorded in docs/AGENT-EXECUTION-ARCHITECTURE.md). ACCEPTANCE: two NTPs drive concurrently → exactly one succeeds, the other is honestly told why; the lease survives the issuing surface closing (expiry-based release); no deadlock on lease release. LANDED 0.2.310 (a7612031, b8896f0d, 95521139) — a SW-owned, durable, expiring single-driver lease. Both the worker and the interactive paths go through withGrantLock; the check is DESTRUCTIVE-only so capture_screenshot stays an ungated read."
- id: CAP-FB-20260826-AGENT-WORKERS-01
  severity: P0
  status: merged
  summary: "Owner DECISION (2026-08-26): adopt the per-agent SHARED WORKER execution architecture (docs/AGENT-EXECUTION-ARCHITECTURE.md). Each agent (background/named/site) = its own shared worker ({name: agentId}), hosted by the single offscreen document (reason WORKERS — the SW cannot create workers directly), bootstrapped through the SW (alarms wake SW → SW ensures offscreen host + worker alive → dispatch). MessagePorts passed to CLIENTS (NTP/sidepanel) via a SW-validated handshake so the UI holds a live port and keeps the worker alive 'as much as possible'. BroadcastChannel (cap:agent:<id>) for state. SW stays the authority for routing/auth/grant-lock/redaction/storage. PHASES: P1 foundation (offscreen host bootstrap + agent-worker shared-worker shell + SW connect/port handshake + alive-set reconciliation + documented pattern) → P2 migrate the agent-do run loop into the worker (tool exec, provider calls, durable-run interaction from the worker context) → P3 durability mapping (run progress/logs survive worker death via durable-runs/OPFS) → P4 UI ports everywhere + background agents fully on workers. Acceptance per phase; P1 KATs: bootstrap, port handshake, keep-alive across host/client death, reconcile-on-wake. LANDED — all four phases: P1 0.2.308 (d0060d28), P2 0.2.309 (e7bf6b81, 90d32754), P3 (1e0588c4), P4 0.2.310 (a7612031). Each agent runs in its own shared worker with authority staying in the SW."

title: [CAP-FB-20260827-MAIN-GATES-RED-02] Main is red again: the journey suite drives a deleted Settings section
description:
## [CAP-FB-20260827-MAIN-GATES-RED-02] Main is red again: the journey suite drives a deleted Settings section
- Feedback: 2026-08-27 — found by running the gates during a documentation reconciliation, not by reading trackers. `npm run test:chrome` reports **26/127** on clean `origin/main@139b6f92` (`0.2.319`) with no local changes
- Updated: 2026-08-27 22:40 UTC
- Status: DONE
- Priority: P0
- Owner: claude-opus-5 implementer session
- Workspace: active (local path private)
- Branch: working tree on `origin/main`
- Base: `139b6f92`
- Candidate: `9f02f9fc` (0.2.320)
- Shipping: `origin/main@9f02f9fc` (0.2.320, pushed 2026-08-28)
- Acceptance: `npm run test:chrome` reaches 127/127 (or an honestly re-baselined count) on a clean profile. Each of the three failures is resolved at the layer that actually broke — the deleted-section drive is repointed at the in-context approval path so the deny/restart coverage it carried is **preserved, not deleted**; the capability-count assertion is derived from `CAPABILITIES` rather than hard-coded; and the `debugger` assertion is left failing until Q17 is decided, then made to match the decision. No assertion is weakened to make the suite pass
- Review: **author review 2026-08-27 with the falsification gates** (the review rule changed the same day — no second model is available; see AGENTS.md "Review without a second model"). The gates caught a real defect in my own change: see the History entry below
- Gates: Chrome journeys **127/127** · unit **1779/0** · security suite **PASS** · build clean · changelog in sync · gallery drift clean · tasks schema clean
- Blockers: —
- Next: closed. The remaining follow-up is generic — keep applying the falsification gate to every future assertion change
- Recover: `npm run test:chrome 2>&1 | grep -E "^FAIL|journey failure" | head`
- History:
  - 2026-08-28 00:30 UTC — **the falsification gate immediately caught a defect in my own fix, which is the whole argument for it.** Under the new rule every changed assertion must be shown going RED against the unfixed product. Two were checked. **(a) The debugger removal guard passed:** re-adding `"debugger"` to the manifest turned `T12 GUARD` red (13 passed / 1 failed), restoring it turned it green — so the guard genuinely protects the ten deleted tests. **(b) The capability assertion FAILED its falsification and had to be rewritten.** I had replaced the rotted literal `length === 7` with `capState0.length === CAPABILITIES.length`. Adding a phantom capability to `CAPABILITIES` and re-running left the journey at **127/127** — the check still passed. It was tautological: Settings renders its rows straight from `CAPABILITIES`, so both sides of the comparison move together and the count half can never fail. My "fix" was weaker than the hard-coded literal it replaced, and a plain reading of the diff would not have shown that. Rewritten to assert what is actually falsifiable — that the extension boots with zero capabilities granted, and that every capability this suite goes on to DRIVE is present by id. Falsified properly: renaming `sidePanel` to `sidePanelRENAMED` takes the suite to **125/127** with that exact check FAIL; restoring returns **127/127**.
  - 2026-08-27 21:15 UTC — opened with reproduction on clean main. **(1) The abort, and the reason the number is 26.** `scripts/chrome-journeys.ts:749` `resolveNextApproval` clicks `.nav-item[data-section="approvals"]` and throws `pending owner approval did not render in exact Settings`. `0.2.313` (`5f8931f3`) deliberately deleted that Settings section — approvals moved in-context, which was the right product change — but the journey was never repointed, so the throw takes the remaining 100 checks with it. The suite is reporting far worse than the product is, and that gap is itself the danger: a red number nobody trusts is a gate nobody reads. **(2) `manifest: debugger absent everywhere` fails honestly.** `0.2.286` (`38641974`) re-declared `"debugger"` in `optional_permissions` for the allowlisted CDP tools, reversing its deliberate removal at `c5ccb2d0`. The assertion is correct and the posture changed under it; this is an owner decision (Q17), not a test defect. **(3) `permissions: all seven capabilities start ungranted` fails.** `extension/lib/capabilities.js` now defines **18** capabilities, up from 7 across the `0.2.278`–`0.2.290` tool waves; the assertion hard-codes `length === 7`.
  - 2026-08-27 22:40 UTC — **all three fixed; the full suite is green (127/127, 1779/0, security PASS).** Deliberately NOT by relaxing assertions: **(1)** the approvals drive was repointed onto the product's real contract. `management.resolve-approval` is still gated on `context.principal === "owner-options"`, so resolving still demands the Settings surface; the Settings control now completes in ONE click through its native `confirmActionDialog`, driven with a genuine CDP click, matching what `runOwnerApprovedMutation` actually does. The two DOM-scraping approval assertions moved onto the **payload**, which is strictly stronger than scraping one rendering of it — the row must be singular, expose exactly `action,approvalId,at,targetRef`, carry a 32-char opaque `targetRef`, and leak no asset id, digest or raw target. The embedded-iframe deny check now evaluates inside the Settings frame's OWN execution context, because calling another frame's `chrome.runtime` from the parent realm does not adopt that frame's principal — so it now genuinely proves the embedded Settings surface is an owner principal, which the old version did not. **(2)** `debugger` removed per the owner decision (Q17): the optional permission, the four CDP tools, the capability row, the Settings label. Browser tools 130 → 126, capability table 159 → 155; the user-scripts half of T12 is untouched. A removal guard was ADDED (`tests/chrome-tools-t12.test.ts`) asserting absence from the manifest, the toolset, the scoped toolset, `BROWSER_TOOL_NAMES`, the capability table and the Settings capability list — deleting 10 tests without leaving a guard would have been the quiet way to lose this. **(3)** the capability count now reads `CAPABILITIES.length` from the product's own table instead of the literal `7`, so the next tool tranche cannot rot it.
  - 2026-08-27 21:15 UTC — **process finding, recorded because the defect is the symptom.** This is the second instance of the identical class: `CAP-FB-20260825-MAIN-GATES-RED-01` was opened on 08-25 for a journey suite left behind by a shipped change, fixed, and the same thing happened again within two days. The full-suite-green rule in `AGENTS.md` is not being applied at the moment work lands. Consequence: **no task merged since 2026-08-25 can legitimately be `DONE`**, since `DONE` requires the journey suite green at that tip — several entries claim it against a gate that was not actually green.

## [CAP-FB-20260824-TASK-AGENT-BOUNDARY-01] @mention task vanished from the list and became the agent's conversation — MERGED

- Feedback: 2026-08-24 — product owner: creating a task that @mentions an agent made it disappear from the task list and strand the owner in the agent's view; a task should stay a task that talks TO agents, not become the agent's conversation.
- Status: MERGED
- Priority: P0
- Shipping: `origin/main@b2742c3eefc525250904a48591319cf5251ddd55` (0.2.248)
- Root cause: the composer mention branch called openAgentSurface → currentThreadId=null → DIRECT agent routes (agent.delegate/named-agent.run/background-agent.run) journaled to the agent's own store and never created a thread (dates to unified picker 38ae7ae, not the recent thread fixes).
- Fix: mention = delegation directive ON the hub task; the thread is kept and the mention passed; conversation.js routes mentions via agent.run (the thread route); agent.run dispatches to the delegation handlers WITH threadId; all three routes carry threadId into durable admission/resume args so the outbox commits the terminal INTO the thread (crash-safe, idempotent by executionId); resume replays restore threadId; pre-admission refusals commit an error terminal (never stuck running). Agent sandbox semantics untouched.
- Review: PASS (Gemini 661a8805), 1511/1511.
- History:
  - 2026-08-24 22:25 UTC — LANDED at 0.2.248. Mentioned tasks now persist to the list, reopen as [user, assistant], follow-ups continue the same thread, and the agent's result returns into the task thread.

## [CAP-FB-20260829-MAIN-GATES-RED-03] Journey suite red on main after the install-granted permission change
- Feedback: 2026-08-29 — found by running the suite on `origin/main`
- Updated: 2026-08-29 UTC
- Status: DONE
- Priority: P0

- Workspace: main
- Branch: main
- Base: `2c84f2fa`
- Candidate: —
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: `npm run test:chrome` green at the tip, with the permission checks asserting the CURRENT install-granted model rather than deleted
- Review: author review 2026-08-29 with the falsification gate cleared
- Gates: journeys 120/120; unit 2243/0; build, tracker schema, gallery, vocabulary green
- Blockers: —
- Next: —
- Recover: `git grep -n "install-granted, not optional" -- scripts/chrome-journeys.ts`
- History:
  - 2026-08-29 — **fixed: 78/127 → 120/120.** Two of the three causes were product bugs the suite had correctly caught, not test drift.
    **(1) Test drift.** The product moved to 36 permanent install-granted permissions plus `host_permissions: ["<all_urls>"]`; the suite still drove `.grant-perm` / `.revoke-perm` controls that no longer exist. The 11 permission checks were rewritten as 4 that describe the real model: the manifest's install-granted shape, every capability granted at install (read from the worker's authoritative map rather than a DOM scrape that carried no ids), the Settings panel being a read-only diagnostic with zero controls, and `capability.revoke` still requiring owner approval. The enrollment and screenshot checks flipped from asserting a headless denial to asserting the now-reachable success path; refusal is still covered by the wrong-origin, expired-grant and post-revoke probes. `audioCapture`/`videoCapture` report not-granted under headless, so the panel check deliberately asserts read-only-ness rather than universal grantedness — otherwise it would fail for an environment reason.
    **(2) Product bug — every site-agent delete failed.** `unregisterOriginScripts` treated a per-origin host permission that `contains()` still reports as a teardown failure. Under `<all_urls>` that permission is permanent and `permissions.remove` cannot touch it, so deletion always returned `"host permission still present after remove"` despite having removed the scripts and cleared memory. Per-origin host revocation is now recognised as NOT APPLICABLE in that model, and the delete/retry routes no longer gate success on it. Their fallback error also claimed `"OPFS clear failed"` when clearing had succeeded; it now says what actually happened.
    **(3) Product bug — a revoke that could never succeed destroyed state first.** Every `capability.revoke` branch does its dependent teardown before removing the permission (scripting tombstones every enrolled origin so a running bridge is rejected from that instant). That ordering is right when revocation is possible, but a required manifest permission can never be removed — Chrome answers `"You cannot remove required permissions."` — so the operation took the origins' authority with it on the way to a guaranteed failure. `isRequiredCapability()` now refuses in `capabilities.js` before any branch runs. The journey asserts the corrected property directly: **a refused revoke tombstones NOTHING.**
    **Falsification:** removing the guard restores the destructive path and drives "a refused revoke tombstones NOTHING" RED (117/120); restoring returns 120/120. The delete fix was verified by observing the exact error string disappear from the route response between runs.

## [CAP-FB-20260829-SILENT-PROVIDER-RUN-01] WITHDRAWN — the provider gate does report itself; the harness was reading the wrong DOM

- Review: n/a

- Next: nothing. The one genuine observation that came out of it is tracked separately as `CAP-FB-20260829-PROVIDER-SET-NO-BASEURL-01`
- Recover: `git log --oneline --all --grep=SILENT-PROVIDER-RUN-01`
- History:
  - 2026-08-29 — **WITHDRAWN. The claim was false and the fault was in my measurement, not the product.** I reported that a keyed provider without host access produced "no assistant message, no error, no status, no approval card". It produces a correct, styled error bubble with a remediation action. Re-measured reading the conversation through its shadow root: with a valid base URL the transcript says *"the configured provider's exact origin is not granted / grant the exact provider origin in Settings, then run this task again"* with a **Fix in Settings** control, and `runConversationTurn` sets `state: "waiting-for-permission"` before it. My probe sampled `document.body.innerText.slice(-260)` — the composer area — and counted `message-bubble` elements in the light DOM, so it could not see anything the conversation had rendered inside `<agent-conversation>`'s shadow root. It reported silence because it was looking somewhere silent. The harness has been fixed to read the bubbles themselves; a harness that can report "nothing happened" when something did is worse than no harness, which is the same class of defect as `CAP-FB-20260829-FIXED-DEBUG-PORTS-01`. **The "Fix in Settings" routing is also deliberate, not a shortfall:** `runConversationTurn` documents that calling `chrome.permissions.request` after the asynchronous provider lookup is rejected by Chrome as not being a user gesture, so Settings is the only surface that can genuinely request it. That is a considered design, and the AGENTS.md rule it appeared to violate is in fact satisfied — the failure names the exact origin and offers the remedy.

PAUL'S DIRECTIVE (verbatim): "Harness: I need tools in the browser to be available to the harness (like claude) and then have it called and messaged back to Chrome over a protocol inside this app (not via MCP). One example: group my tabs - should be able to get the tabs from chrome an then move them into grouos... theis means we need to proxy the tool calls from harness to chrome client"

ARCHITECTURE (coord's brief): declare browser tools to the harness session (signatures in prompt/protocol); when the harness calls one it sends `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"…","method":"browser/call_tool","params":{"name":"…","args":{…}}}` over the EXISTING WebSocket/native connection; `extension/lib/acp-runner.js` receives it, dispatches to `browserToolset()` (list_tabs, group_tabs, …), and returns the JSON result on the same channel. **NO MCP**: no MCP SDK, no external HTTP server.

CANONICAL DRIVE: "group my tabs" — harness calls list_tabs, computes the grouping, calls group_tabs({tabIds, title, color}), Chrome executes chrome.tabs.group; verified in a browser.

ACCEPTANCE: unit tests for the dispatch + an end-to-end drive that really groups tabs.

comments.text:
chrome-agent-platform-2amt: the harness can call CAP's browser tools over the app's own protocol

PAUL'S DIRECTIVE: "I need tools in the browser to be available to the harness (like claude) and then
have it called and messaged back to Chrome over a protocol inside this app (not via MCP). One example:
group my tabs … this means we need to proxy the tool calls from harness to chrome client."

WHAT EXISTS NOW, and none of it is MCP (no MCP SDK, no HTTP endpoint, no mcpServers):
  * scripts/acp-bridge.ts declares the catalogue to the harness ONCE per session — prepended to the
    session's first prompt — with the exact envelope to emit:
      {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"…","method":"browser/call_tool","params":{"name":…,"args":{…}}}
    and the relay is unchanged: the bridge already forwards adapter lines to the browser socket
    verbatim, so an agent→client request arrives where it should with no new transport.
  * extension/lib/acp-client.js handles that method in _handleAgentRequest (where permission requests
    already land), reports it to the turn listener as a tool event, and answers on the SAME id.
  * extension/lib/browser-tools.js gains runBrowserToolCall(name, args): the catalogue, the zod
    validation and the tool bodies are the EXISTING browserToolset() — list_tabs, group_tabs,
    ungroup_tabs and the rest. The GRANTS STAY INSIDE THE TOOLS, so this adds reach, not authority: a
    harness call is refused exactly where a model call would be.
  * unknown tool / invalid arguments / a throwing tool come back as a JSON {error,…} a harness can
    correct rather than a protocol error or an unhandled throw.

THE ANTI-DRIFT GUARD: tests/browser-tool-proxy.test.ts compares BROWSER_TOOL_DECLARATIONS with
Object.keys(browserToolset()) in BOTH directions, so a tool cannot be declared without existing and
cannot exist without being declared — and asserts the declaration block introduces no mcpServers and
no http(s) URL, which is Paul's "not via MCP" as a test rather than a comment.

TESTS (6/6): the both-directions declaration guard; the once-per-session injection (second prompt
untouched, a different session decorated, non-prompt frames verbatim); the dispatcher's three error
paths; the GRANT property (an ungranted call is refused by the tool itself and no tab count leaks);

title: The collapsed sidebar cuts its own chips off: the rail re-styles every row type except the harness rows (117px chips in a 40px rail, 90px cut)
description:
OWNER REPORT (Paul, 2026-09-23, verbatim): "icons are there however when that sidebar they are in is closed, they get cut off."

FILED AS ITS OWN BEAD, not on l3ts. l3ts was "the one-click agent buttons had no marks, a collapsed side panel squashed them" and it landed the MARKS (they are there — the owner says so) plus the side-panel geometry. This is a different defect in a different surface: the NTP's own collapsible task sidebar, whose rail re-styles every row type when it collapses EXCEPT the harness rows, so the chips stay full-width pills inside a 40px content box. l3ts is closed and its subject (marks exist) is satisfied; re-opening it for a rule that was never written would blur what it fixed. discovered-from l3ts; same family as qzae (a collapsed-panel rule that was pinned but never fired).

MEASURED IN THE BUILT EXTENSION (real browser, CDP, geometry not appearance) — collapsed rail = 60px, content 40px:
- BEFORE: each harness chip 117x29, visible 27x29, ratio 0.231, cutRight 90px, outside the rail by 89px. Clippers: div#side-harness (overflow hidden auto, 10..49) <- section.side-section.side-harness (overflow clip, 10..49) <- aside#side.side.collapsed (overflow clip, 0..60).
- WHAT IS CUT: the CHIP (mark + label pill), truncated mid-pill; the mark itself was intact at ratio 1.0 (16x16 fully visible). So the owner's "icons cut off" is the chip being chopped right after its icon — the identity survived only by luck of the 8px padding.
- AFTER: chip 34x34, ratio 1.0, cutRight 0, outsideRailBy 0, mark 16x16 ratio 1.0, label display:none (hidden by rule, not clipped), title + aria-label carry the full name, glyphs still distinct (pi / C / X).

CAUSE: `.side.collapsed` re-styles .thread-item, .agent-item, .foot-btn, .new-task, .side-label-row — and had no rule for the harness rows at all, leaving `.harness-list`'s 12px inline padding and the chips' full-width mark+label layout inside the 40px rail.

FIX (branch fix/panel-collapse-clipped-mark @ 1f64a7b3, version bump c0b8a92e = 0.3.475): collapsed harness rows become icon-only like the rest of the rail — `.side.collapsed .harness-list { flex-direction: column; flex-wrap: nowrap; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 4px 0 8px; }`, `.side.collapsed .harness-list button { inline-size: 34px; block-size: 34px; padding: 0; justify-content: center; gap: 0; }`, `.side.collapsed .harness-list .hq-label { display: none; }`, plus `btn.title = name` so the full name stays reachable on hover once the label is hidden (the convention the rail's task rows already use).

WHY THE WIDTH HARNESS DID NOT CATCH IT, which is the instrument part of this bead: a clipped element still has a bounding box, so the existing checks ("every harness button carries a mark", markW >= 12) pass on a chip that is 90px cut off. scripts/constrained-width-layout.ts now measures the missing observable — every icon's box intersected with ALL its clipping ancestors (visible ratio, side cut) — for the collapsed rail at 1400px and 900px, plus an identity check (the marks must not collapse to one repeated glyph) and a per-width non-vacuity guard. 16 new checks: 49 -> 65.

MUTANTS (all run; the two surprises are statements about the checks and are recorded, not hidden):
1. collapsed rules removed -> RED: 117x29 / ratio 0.231 / cutRight 90 / outsideRailBy 89. The reported defect is caught.
2. label hidden but the 34x34 chip rule removed -> GREEN. Hiding the label is what ends the cut (the chip then sizes to the mark); the 34x34 rule is uniformity with the rail's other icon rows, NOT the load-bearing part. Stated plainly rather than claimed as necessary.
3. harness section hidden when collapsed -> RED at the non-vacuity guard (chips 0x0), so an absent rail cannot pass.
4. the three named marks given one glyph -> RED at "the marks distinguish the harnesses" ({"glyphs":["Z","Z","Z"]}). Two earlier attempts at this mutant were wrong and are recorded: mutating the fallback glyph changed nothing (pi/claude-code/codex are in the named map), and one mutant produced invalid code — a broken mutant proves nothing.

GATES: npm run test:width 65 passed / 0 failed; npm run test:changed 5 passed / 0 failed; npm test GREEN (serial phase 17 files, parallel phase 478 files in 50s). Heavy-gate slot taken for every browser run (the probe announced its holder; test:width is registry class "named", so it does not take the turn itself). No --no-verify.

EVIDENCE: the harness's own geometry.json (rail section) per run, /tmp/pc-*.log for the matrix, and the before/after tables in this comment.

A durable run record exists for it, the provider receives the 5 requests it expects (search_tools ×4 + text), and the journey gate can pass the keyless/cookie block on an idle box. The check that fails today is the probe's own shortfall assertion, so a fix must make it pass WITHOUT weakening that assertion or the "no durable run record" phase reporting.

comments.text:
REPRODUCTION ATTEMPTED AND REFUSED — INCONCLUSIVE, plus a bounded STATIC reading offered as two candidate mechanisms and the measurement that would separate them. Nothing here is a diagnosis and nothing here is a reproduction.

REPRODUCTION: npm run test:chrome on a clean checkout of CURRENT MAIN 5e5fd815 (build:production rc=0, check:dist clean) exited 75 after the gate's full 601229 ms quiet-window bound. CAP_ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL {"load1":32.42,"load5":28.32,"load15":20.36,"cores":32,"loadPerCore":1.013125,"compilers":6,"compilerNames":["esbuild"],"measurable":true,"activeCompilers":3}. Samples across the wait never approached the threshold (0.47, 0.72, 0.64, 0.74, 1.13, 1.29, 0.99, 0.84, 0.67, 0.61, 0.66, 1.09, 0.96, 0.90, then 1.01 at refusal), and dnop's active count named 3 genuinely compiling esbuild processes, so this was real build activity rather than parked services. NOT RETRIED: this bead's claim is about an idle box (its own evidence reads load/core=0.19) and load15 is 20.36, so a window is not imminent; a retry now either refuses again or produces a 132/370 indistinguishable from load, which is the misattribution 9t1p was filed to stop. So the question "did 35o1 or a later landing already fix the enqueue?" REMAINS OPEN and is not answered by source reading. Evidence: ~/cap-evidence/jnwb-repro/{main-5e5fd815.log,driver.log}.

STATIC READING of runScriptedToolProbe (scripts/chrome-journeys.ts:525-570 at 5e5fd815), offered as two candidates because both are consistent with the observed "0 of 5 requests, phase no durable run record" and I cannot separate them without a run:

CANDIDATE A — the two driver steps that start the run have their RESULTS DISCARDED.
    await typeInto(cdp, ntpSession, "#task-input", task);
    await clickSel(cdp, ntpSession, "#run-task");
Neither return value is read. typeInto returns false when clickSel cannot resolve a point, and clickSel returns false when boxOf yields null — so a typing failure or a missed Run click presents EXACTLY as the reported symptom: the provider receives 0 requests, no durable run record is created, and the probe waits its full 120 s before reporting a shortfall that names the provider rather than the step that never happened. Note these still use the retired composer ids; they resolve because boxOf (:367-380) carries the compat mapping to [data-composer-input]/[data-composer-send], but that mapping is DOCUMENT-WIDE, so it resolves to whichever composer comes first in document order — and ntp.html carries two (#composer at :1026, #thread-composer at :1233). The probe does click #home first, so the hub composer should be the target; whether it is visible and hittable at that moment is exactly what a discarded return value would hide. This is the same class as 9t1p fixed for the timeout loop and as qdjn fixed for the per-width guards: a silent failure reporting as a different, more confusing failure.

CANDIDATE B — the probe's agent.run never gets dispatched because a PRIOR run in the same block is still in flight. The comment immediately above the cookie-probe call site (:~4060) says: "Leaving the run paused here is what hung the suite (the next agent.run queued behind it until the CDP evaluate timed out), so the card is ALWAYS settled before moving on." So this block has a known history of a paused run blocking the next enqueue. If the settling step did not complete, the probe's run would queue and never start — producing the same 0-of-5 and the same absent durable record.

WHAT WOULD SEPARATE THEM, in one quiet-window run: capture the return values of the two driver steps and the in-flight run set at probe start. If typeInto/clickSel return false, it is A. If both return true and a prior executionId is still non-terminal when the probe types, it is B. Both observations are cheap and neither weakens the shortfall assertion, which must stay exactly as strict as it is.

A FIX I AM PROPOSING AND DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPING: assert the two discarded return values so a failed step is named at the step instead of surfacing 120 s later as a provider shortfall. It is low-risk, changes nothing when the steps succeed, and is the same shape as 9t1p's three-outcomes change. I am not shipping it because I cannot verify it — any change to this gate needs a quiet-window drive to prove it did not move the 132/370 for an unrelated reason, and coord's ordering is reproduce first. Shipping an unverifiable change to the strongest gate is the thing I have declined all session.

NO ATTRIBUTION IS MADE. Per cap-astra's caution, which I am adopting as the standard for this bead: a quiet sample is a control, not a cause, and "0 requests / no durable record" is an observed CHECKPOINT, not a root cause. Both candidates above are consistent with the observation and neither is established.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
STATIC ROOT-CAUSE CANDIDATE, found before being re-tasked to 32yz. Releasing the claim; this is where I stopped and what is measured. NOT driven in a browser, so it is a candidate, not a confirmed cause.

THE MECHANISM: boxOf() (scripts/chrome-journeys.ts) returns getBoundingClientRect() UNFILTERED, so a HIDDEN element yields {x:0,y:0} rather than null. clickSel() then dispatches a real mouse click at the viewport origin and RETURNS TRUE. typeInto() proceeds to type into whatever has focus (nothing). So the probe's three input steps — clickSel('#home'), typeInto('#task-input', task), clickSel('#run-task') — can all report success while nothing was clicked and no run was ever enqueued. That is exactly jnwb's signature: 0 of 5 provider requests, phase 'no durable run record', and the full 136 s wait.

EXECUTABLE REPRODUCTION (no browser; source-extracts the REAL helpers with new Function and drives them against a fake CDP, the house pattern from tests/journey-cdp-timeout.test.ts). Script retained at /tmp/jnwb-probe.mjs:
  boxOf(hidden element)  = {"x":0,"y":0}
  clickSel(hidden)       = true   -> dispatched at ["0,0","0,0"]
  boxOf(absent element)  = null
  clickSel(absent)       = false
The ABSENT case is handled; the HIDDEN case is not. A zero-rect click fails identically however long you wait, which matches the bead's own note that a 7m29s run and an 8m run both died at the same place — i.e. not a timing race at this level.

TWO WAYS THE HUB COMPOSER CAN BE NON-INTERACTABLE THERE, both measured statically: (1) extension/ntp/ntp.html:1194 declares #thread-view as a class="view-overlay" that can cover the hub; (2) ntp.html carries TWO agent-composer elements (#composer at :1033 and #thread-composer at :1240), so the probe's UNSCOPED '#task-input' resolves via boxOf's compat mapping to whichever [data-composer-input] comes first in document order rather than to the hub's. AgentComposer is light DOM (static shadow() { return false; }), so both hooks are reachable to document.querySelector — which is why this resolves to the wrong element rather than failing loudly.

PROPOSED FIX SHAPE (not implemented): make boxOf FAIL CLOSED on a zero/degenerate rect and on an element that is not hit-testable at its own centre point, returning null so clickSel reports false exactly as the absent case already does; and scope the probe's composer selectors to the hub host so two composers cannot resolve ambiguously. The falsification is cheap and inverted — the MUTANT is today's behaviour: restore the unfiltered rect and the reproduction above returns true at 0,0 again.

WHAT I DID NOT DO, stated plainly: no npm run test:chrome drive. The box measured load 19.23 (30.58 five-minute) on 32 cores while I was on this, and the journey gate is load-sensitive by its own registry declaration — 9t1p exists because a run under load produces a verdict about the box, not the tree. So the driven half of this bead is OWED, and the static finding above must not be read as confirming the 132/370 cause until someone drives it in a quiet window. Also unverified: whether making boxOf strict lets the keyless/cookie block REACH its checks, or merely fails earlier with a better message — jnwb's acceptance requires the former, and that distinction needs the driven run to settle.

title: MAIN IS RED at cc2711fa: muc's components.js refactor regressed diay's segmented-control scroll-into-view (scrollIntoView called 0 times, test expects exactly once) — npm test exits 1 for every lane
description:
FOUND while gating an unrelated change (chrome-agent-platform-qdjn). npm test exits 1 on unmodified origin/main @ cc2711fa with three failures, none of them in the gating lane's files. This bead is the one with a decisive attribution; the other two failures are listed at the end.

WHY THIS IS P1 AND NOT A LANE PROBLEM: npm test is the pre-push gate for every lane. Right now every lane that runs it gets these three reds and has to decide whether they caused them. I nearly had to; I verified at a pristine checkout instead. A red main makes every lane's gate verdict ambiguous, which is how a real regression gets waved through as "someone else's".

THE REGRESSION, MEASURED.
  At cc2711fa (muc, current main tip):
    npm run test:file -- tests/components.test.ts
    segmented-control scrolls the activated tab into view (chrome-agent-platform-diay) ... FAILED (1ms)
    segmented-control scrolls the attribute-selected tab into view on render (chrome-agent-platform-diay) ... FAILED (934µs)
    FAILED | 54 passed | 2 failed (2s)
    Assertion, verbatim from tests/components.test.ts:1147:
      error: Error: click: the activated tab must be scrolled into view exactly once, got 0

  At 61e4fdab (the commit immediately before muc), same worktree, only extension/shared/components.js + docs/components.js + tests/components.test.ts checked out at that revision:
    npm run test:file -- tests/components.test.ts -> exit 0, GREEN.

So the break is localized to muc's edit of those files, and muc did NOT touch tests/components.test.ts. Its changed-file list is docs/components.html (+9), docs/components.js (+130), extension/ntp/ntp.js (+175), extension/shared/components.js (+130), plus release/tracker bookkeeping. The test asserts on components.js, which muc refactored for the agent-picker row unification.

WHAT REGRESSED, IN PRODUCT TERMS: bead chrome-agent-platform-diay was "Providers tabs at 360px: active tab can scroll out of view", and it landed at c80b8abc — TWO COMMITS BEFORE muc. Its fix made the segmented control scroll the activated tab into view. That behavior is now gone: scrollIntoView is called zero times where the fix required exactly once. So this is not a stale test asserting an old shape; it is a shipped accessibility/usability fix at a narrow width being silently undone by an unrelated component refactor. The test is correctly red and the product is wrong.

THIS IS THE COUPLING RULE, TEXTBOOK: AGENTS.md — "File-disjointness is not suite-greenness. Two lanes whose diffs touch disjoint files can still break each other through a watcher... Neither lane alone can see the break; only the union gated together can." muc and diay share no file. muc changed a component; diay's test watches that component. Only a full-suite run at the union sees it.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. npm run test:file -- tests/components.test.ts green at the tip, with both diay checks passing because the behavior is restored — NOT by editing or deleting the assertions. The test is right; weakening it would re-break the owner-visible fix at narrow widths.
2. The restored behavior driven in a real browser at the narrow width diay cared about (360px / the segmented control's container), not only in the unit test, since the unit test observes a scrollIntoView call count rather than the rendered result.
3. Determine whether the agent-picker row unification and the segmented-control scroll behavior can both hold, or whether muc's refactor needs to carry diay's scroll wiring forward. The likely shape: the refactor replaced or re-parented the element that owned the scroll-into-view call.

EVIDENCE: /tmp logs are transient; the durable copies are ~/cap-evidence/qdjn-falsification/ (the qdjn work) and the pristine worktree /home/paulkinlan/worktrees/cap-pristine-cc2711fa at cc2711fa with a clean tree. Reproduce with: git worktree add <path> cc2711fa && npm ci && deno install && npm run build:production && npm run test:file -- tests/components.test.ts. The build step is REQUIRED first — running the test before it fails with TS2307 Cannot find module extension/dist/shared/diff-core.bundle.js, which is an environmental failure and not this bug (I hit that myself and had to re-run).

THE OTHER TWO FAILURES ON MAIN, listed so nobody re-derives them:
- tests/agent-header-rename-reload.test.ts => "7zf0: real-browser rename-then-reload updates thread header and history state" FAILED (3s). VERIFIED pre-existing: it fails at pristine cc2711fa in a clean worktree. NOT ATTRIBUTED. Two candidate causes, both unproven: muc changed extension/ntp/ntp.js by +175 lines and this test drives the NTP thread header; or it is load-sensitive (it is a real-browser test and the box was at 0.37-0.47 load/core while I ran it). Distinguishing those needs a run in a quiet window, which I did not have.
- Both diay checks above, which are this bead's subject.
So npm test at cc2711fa is 3 failures across 2 files, and the full-suite tallies I measured were: serial phase (16 files) GREEN, parallel phase (476 files) FAILED, 492 files total.

NOT CLAIMED: I did not run the browser journeys, so I cannot say whether the narrow-width tab behavior is visibly broken for the owner today — only that the unit assertion observing scrollIntoView is red and was green two commits ago.
close_reason:
LANDED — repaired by 1941f9f2 (fix/main-red-after-muc-landing, v0.3.464) while this bead was in flight; the attribution and the fix crossed. Verified empirically at origin/main 7b6ab342, not taken from the report.

MEASURED AT 7b6ab342 IN A CLEAN WORKTREE (build:production first — running these before the build fails with TS2307 on extension/dist/shared/diff-core.bundle.js, which is environmental and not this bug):
  npm run test:file -- tests/components.test.ts -> 56 passed / 0 failed, exit 0 (was 54 passed / 2 failed, exit 1 at cc2711fa). Both diay checks now pass by name: "segmented-control scrolls the activated tab into view (chrome-agent-platform-diay) ... ok" and "segmented-control scrolls the attribute-selected tab into view on render (chrome-agent-platform-diay) ... ok".
  npm run test:file -- tests/agent-header-rename-reload.test.ts -> 2 passed / 0 failed, exit 0 (was FAILED (3s) at cc2711fa; 1941f9f2 also migrated it to the <agent-picker> summary rows).
  npm test -> serial phase GREEN + parallel phase (476 files) GREEN, 492 files total, wall 225s, exit 0.

THE RESTORATION IS REAL BEHAVIOR, NOT A WEAKENED ASSERTION — checked rather than assumed, because the acceptance for this bead was explicitly "restore the behaviour, do NOT edit or delete diay's assertions". git show 1941f9f2 -- extension/shared/components.js adds 18 lines including the method definition `_scrollSelectedIntoView() {` with `b.scrollIntoView?.({ block: "nearest", inline: "nearest" })` and two call sites `this._scrollSelectedIntoView();`. tests/components.test.ts is NOT in that commit's changed-file list, so the assertion at :1147 ("the activated tab must be scrolled into view exactly once") is untouched and now passes on restored behavior. That is the outcome the acceptance asked for.

WHAT THIS BEAD ESTABLISHED AND SHOULD KEEP ON RECORD: at cc2711fa, muc's refactor of extension/shared/components.js (+130) dropped the scrollIntoView call that diay's fix at c80b8abc had added, without touching components.test.ts — so the two lanes shared no file and only a full-suite run at the union could see it. RESIDUAL, still open and NOT closed by this: the narrow-width behavior should also be driven in a real browser, since the unit test observes a scrollIntoView CALL COUNT rather than the rendered result. The call count being restored is strong evidence the behavior is back, but bead diay's original complaint was visual (the active tab scrolling out of view at 360px) and nobody has re-driven that width since. Filed as a note here rather than a new bead; if the desk wants it driven, scripts/constrained-width-layout.ts at 260/300/400px is the existing instrument and qdjn's branch just made its per-width checks non-vacuous.

1. I bound cap/mcp-harness-tools' intended_delta to SIX COMMIT SUBJECTS. Subjects are history; the net diff is content. They do not — they were added by 44cb7f2d and dropped by 441f900c, and they do not appear in the net diff at all, because added-then-removed inside a branch nets to zero. Verified independently rather than accepted: git diff --stat d0f01545..9d40cfec is 9 files, 241 insertions, 16 deletions, of which the functional content is scripts/acp-bridge.ts +40 (PI_MCP_CONFIG_MODE=exclusive and the spawn env carrying it), tests/acp-bridge-mcp-isolation.test.ts +96 (rule and wiring pinned as two separate layers), docs/MCP-SUPPORT-DESIGN.md +83 (what was measured as NOT built). This is the same error class as trusting a test's NAME for its coverage — item 1 in this repo's own test-honesty canon.

2. I overstated the shim hazard. I wrote that a naive merge "could re-introduce files main removed". For an ordinary three-way merge that is WRONG: base has the file, main deletes it, the branch does not modify it, so the merge preserves the deletion — no conflict, no resurrection. MEASURED: git diff --name-status 38e3418d <tip> -- browser-shim-node.js browser-shim-process.js returns EMPTY for all three branches; zero shim files modified anywhere.

The residual hazard is real but narrower, differently shaped, and only on two of the four branches: a MODIFY/MODIFY CONFLICT ON build.mjs. So build.mjs conflicts, the branch side points at three files that no longer exist, and resolving it by taking the branch side or union-restoring yields a build that imports missing modules. That is a LOUD build failure, not a silent resurrection — materially smaller than what I first wrote. Desk action: take main's side for the shim wiring and the branch's side for the bundle-budget change; they are in different regions, so it is a line-level resolution, not a choice between versions. feat/harness-ui is EXEMPT: 10 files changed, no build consumer among them, so it carries the inert shim files and nothing that references them. cap/mcp-harness-tools is exempt by base.

title: The post-commit hook carried a second copy of the changelog filter that did not know the internal: marker, so it published three internal notes as release entries and burned a version on one
description:
FILED AFTER THE FIX because no bead existed for it: the branch cap/whatsnew-449 and its review findings were tracked only in a branch name and an intercom thread. The fix is on cap/whatsnew-hook-sync @ e247cf3832d9b94aa0e6aa2801bd292fc2f5d6ae, branched off a1365f60.

DEFECT. scripts/bump-version.mjs carried its own copy of the six filter regexes plus isUserFacingEntry, justified in a comment as "so the standalone script functions in scratch temporary test mirrors without relying on outside module resolution". The two copies agreed until extension/options/changelog-filter.js gained the `internal:` marker (INTERNAL_MARKER_RE :33, isInternalEntry :42, returning false at :48). The duplicate had no isInternalEntry, so it scored a marked note USER-FACING. scripts/git-hooks/post-commit:19 calls `node scripts/bump-version.mjs patch --skip-if-no-note --message "$MSG"` on EVERY commit, and :111's bail is `if (cleanNote && !isUserFacingEntry(cleanNote))` — so for a marked note the bail did not fire and the hook took the PUBLISH path.

MEASURED CONSEQUENCE, not a drift table. On that branch, CHANGELOG.md line 4 read:
    ## [0.3.452] — 2026-09-22
    - internal: the changelog gate now allows a stated-internal note instead of forcing a user-facing sentence
The hook published the marker's OWN commit as a release entry and consumed 0.3.452 for it — six version strings across package.json, package-lock.json, extension/manifest.json and extension/lib/bundled-inventory-data.js moved 0.3.451 -> 0.3.452 for a note the marker exists to suppress. A second and third `internal:` line sat at 0.3.448 and 0.3.446, but those are NOT this defect — see the distinction below, which is the part a reviewer or a future lane is most likely to get wrong.

THE DISTINCTION THAT MATTERS. Only 0.3.452 was hook output. A post-commit hook can only PREPEND an entry for the commit it runs on; it cannot rewrite entries four versions back. The `internal:` markers on 0.3.448 and 0.3.446 were hand-applied by the copy-rewrite commits 2b321a77 and 51346e12 and are THE FEATURE WORKING: they hide a rationale correction and a measurements commit from the readable five while keeping them under Show all, and changelog-filter.js names both as its motivating cases. Deleting them would re-expose "correct the F1 rationale to what was actually measured" and "the measurements behind the constrained-width fix" to readers. I was instructed to remove all three, checked the diff first, and removed one.

FIX. bump-version.mjs imports isUserFacingEntry from extension/options/changelog-filter.js, exactly as scripts/check-changelog.mjs:9 already did; the duplicate and its six regexes are deleted. A second copy of a rule is how two gates drift apart.

THE CONSTRAINT THAT HAD TO BE PRESERVED. The standalone rationale was real: FOUR scratch mirrors spawn this script from a temp dir (tests/bump-version-sanitize.test.ts 1, tests/named-agents-provider.test.ts 3) and none copied the filter, so a bare import would have made the script die on module resolution in all four and read as a bump failure. All four mirrors now carry extension/options/changelog-filter.js. Verified only two copies of the filter existed repo-wide (grep for the regex names across scripts/, extension/, tests/), so the sync is complete.

UNDO. Six version strings reverted 0.3.452 -> 0.3.451 (the faithful undo — the bump should never have happened) and the 0.3.452 block removed from CHANGELOG.md; extension/CHANGELOG.md is gitignored and regenerates. check:changelog-order reports 871 entries, unique + descending, latest 0.3.451 — exactly one fewer than the 872 measured before the fix. LANDING NOTE: this branch's commits consumed 0.3.449-0.3.452 while main independently consumed through 0.3.456, so landing must take main's side on the version surfaces and let the hook assign the next free number. Do not renumber by hand; the hook owns version assignment.

FALSIFICATION, three ways.
1. THROUGH THE REAL HOOK ON A REAL COMMIT: the fix commit's own subject starts with `internal:`, and the hook printed "[bump-version] commit note ... does not pass user-facing filter — NOT bumping version", consuming nothing. Version stayed 0.3.451, no entry written.
2. UNIT, BOTH HALVES: an `internal:` note with --skip-if-no-note must exit 0, consume no version (stays 1.2.3), write no entry, and print the same loud notice bookkeeping gets; a user-facing note must still bump to 1.2.4 and still publish, so syncing the filter is not the same as disabling the hook. 6 passed / 0 failed.
3. PRE-FIX DIFFERENTIAL: with a1365f60's duplicate restored, 5 passed / 1 failed, and the one that reddened is the internal-note test with "a marked-internal note must not consume a version", actual 1.2.4 vs expected 1.2.3 — the burned version, named. The user-facing test stayed green.

TWO NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS FIXED IN THE SAME PASS. partitionChangelog's docstring claimed each recent entry carries "how many internal bullets it hides", but it pushes {version, date, bullets: visible} with no count field and the UI receives only {recent, rest}; the claim is removed rather than a count added, because nothing consumes one. And the marker's comment said "deliberate and explicit, never inferred" without naming the cost, so both residual risks are now in the code: a bullet that should be marked and is not still passes if it reads as user-facing (the marker suppresses, its absence never accuses), and the marker can hide real user-facing copy with nothing objecting (silent by construction, since the point of the marker is that nobody has to justify it).

GATES at e247cf38: npm test serial 16 files GREEN 174s + parallel 471 files GREEN 47s, 487 files total, exit 0, zero failures; check:changelog 0; check:changelog-order 0; build 0; check:dist clean. All four mirror tests and both new tests verified by name inside the suite.

RELATED: 4zp3 (the jargon filter does not cover the internal words that actually leak — the same filter, the other direction), p7k4 (leaked joiner punctuation), y6z6 (sanitizeEntry joiner leak), bge5 (changelog.test.ts red on the jargon filter). This bead is the hook-side duplicate; those are filter-coverage beads.

Qwen corrected comparison, independent cap-k3/Opus content challenge and cap-astra synthesis confirm currentmain913d7e80 retains the shared filter/import and primary source/test blobs; parsed metadata differs only in root releases. Original bead carries author post-landing verification; no new runtime PASS or invented original independent verdict is claimed. title: journey abort at 132/370 is an unanswered service-worker round trip reported as fleet load — assert the probe's expectations and measure the box on an evaluate timeout
description:
Found measuring chrome-agent-platform-muc on the union tree (muc + dnop + 0lj3). Full evidence in the chrome-agent-platform-qk7p comment of 2026-09-23; this bead is the fix.

WHAT IS BROKEN (precise, source-referenced):
1. scripts/chrome-journeys.ts:512-530, runScriptedToolProbe: the wait loop 'while (provider.requests.length < expectRequests && Date.now() - t0 < 120000)' exits SILENTLY on timeout — it never asserts that the provider received the requests it expected. The probe then returns a partial result, the caller's check fails on a confusing payload, and the failure surfaces one step later as a timeout about something else. (Same class as the seed-nothing fixtures: a probe that found nothing, letting the failure land elsewhere.)

title: Serialise load-sensitive gates through one declared fleet-wide slot, announced, and report INCONCLUSIVE naming the holder
description:
Coord 2026-09-22, option (a). The measurement that made this a design question: with chrome-agent-platform-dnop fixed, chrome-journeys STARTED and reached 132/370 before aborting on 'cdp evaluate exceeded the budget under fleet load' at load/core 0.13 — a box quiet by every measure the quiet-window gate has could not complete 370 round-trips. More threshold tuning cannot fix that; there is no threshold left to loosen.

THE GAP THIS CLOSES (source, verified):
- chrome-slots.ts is a bounded SEMAPHORE (CAP_CHROME_MAX_CONCURRENT, default 4) and it is a MEMORY bound, not a correctness one.
- launchChrome's acquireLaunchScope treats the two scopes as mutually exclusive: with canonicalLock (or lockPath) it acquires the flock and takes NO slot (slot: -1); otherwise it takes one of 4 slots and NO flock.
- So a journey holding the canonical lock does NOT exclude a KAT batch's up-to-4 browsers: journeys and KATs can run concurrently by construction. The canonical lock only excludes other canonical-lock users (journeys, the security custody supervisor).
- The KAT runner is serial WITHIN a run, but several lanes each run their own KAT batch, and each KAT browser takes a slot.

DESIGN OF RECORD (the shape coord asked for):
1. ONE declared fleet-wide slot for load-sensitive gates: a flock on /tmp/cap-heavy-gate.lock, held for the gate's lifetime, release = close the holder's stdin (the crash-safe pattern the canonical lock already uses, so a killed lane leaves no held slot — the kernel drops it).
2. ANNOUNCED: the holder writes an atomic sidecar (/tmp/cap-heavy-gate.holder.json) with gate name, harness/npm script, pid, started-at, cwd. A refusing lane reads it and NAMES the holder, so 'who has the machine' is answerable without asking a human.
3. BOUNDED + INCONCLUSIVE: the wait is bounded (CAP_HEAVY_GATE_BOUND_MS, default 20 min, the canonical lock's contract). A lane that cannot get the slot reports the ENVIRONMENTAL verdict — exit 75 with the existing CAP_ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL marker carrying {"reason":"heavy-gate-slot-busy","holder":{...}} — never a product red, never a silent skip, never a green.
4. NO INTERFERENCE: measure and wait, or refuse. The module never kills, renames, re nices or otherwise touches another lane's processes (the same DO-NOT as quiet-window.ts, with the same source-scan guard).
5. ORDERING: acquire the slot FIRST, then wait for the quiet window. Holding the slot means no other heavy gate can start while we measure, so the quiet predicate then measures only non-gate load.
6. WIRED (this change): chrome-journeys.ts (the 370-check gate) and scripts/kat-runner.ts (one slot for the whole serial batch). FOLLOW-UP, listed not hidden: the other gate-class entries in scripts/lib/harness-registry.ts (a11y, components, width, security injection, the security custody supervisor's own lock on fd 9) — the custody chain's exclusivity already exists and must not be double-locked without reading its protocol.

ACCEPTANCE / MUTANTS:
- two concurrent heavy gates: exactly ONE holds; the other's bounded wait expires and its refusal NAMES the first (gate + pid from the sidecar). Falsification, mandatory: with the slot disabled/pointed at a private path, BOTH hold — the test must be able to fail, otherwise it pins nothing.
- crash safety: a holder SIGKILLed mid-hold leaves no held slot; the next acquirer gets it within the bound.
- announcement: the sidecar is written only by the holder and is removed/refreshed on release; a refusal never invents a holder.
- the DO-NOT source scan passes over the new module.
- end to end: with the slot held by another process, chrome-journeys exits 75 with the holder named and does NOT start a browser.

HONEST LIMITS, stated: the slot serialises GATES against each other. It does not stop another lane's compiler from spiking mid-run — that remains the quiet-window predicate's job (and the qk7p classification's), and a transient spike can still kill a journey mid-run. This closes gate-vs-gate competition, which is the part that is ours to fix.

Evidence: /tmp/muc-journeys3.log (the 132/370 abort at load/core 0.13, with the gate's own 'box quiet after 10068 ms' line above it).

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
CANDIDATE PUSHED — branch cap/nweh-cookie-redaction @ 6525c3ce, STACKED on 835bff08 (the selector repair, bead im52). Ordering is NOT symmetric: this fix is only measurable on top of that one, because without the selector repair the suite times out before reaching the cookie section. 835bff08 can land alone; this cannot land first. Worktree /home/paulkinlan/worktrees/cap-security-suite, 1 file changed (scripts/security-suite.ts), no product code.

I built on the reviewer's reproduction rather than re-deriving it, and both halves are confirmed by reading the code. They are worse together than separately: the fixture returned zero rows on a fresh profile and Array.isArray([]) is true, so the check passed with nothing to redact; and cookieModelContent was JSON.stringify of already-serialized content strings, so every inner quote came back escaped and /"value"/ could never match the text it inspected. Either alone weakens the check; together they made it structurally incapable of failing. The production mapper is correct — metadata only — so this was purely an instrument that could not see a leak.

FIX, following this bead's acceptance item by item:
- seed and assert a NONEMPTY matching synthetic-cookie metadata row: chrome.cookies.set (the same API the tool reads) for a non-httpOnly nweh_probe cookie on 127.0.0.1 with a per-run sentinel, seeded before the run; new check (a) asserts the seeded row reached list_cookies as metadata.
- inspect the DECODED executeEnvelope result for own value keys: a bounded recursive walk (ownKeyPaths) over cookiesEnv.result, not a grep over a stringified blob, plus both spellings (bare and escaped) in the raw model text as a backstop.
- assert the synthetic value is absent from the model transcript: check (c) scans EVERY message of EVERY provider request in the probe run, not just the last tool message — a leak in message four of nine would have passed the narrower version.
- pristine passes and the real browser-tools value:c.value mutation fails SPECIFICALLY on redaction: measured, below.
- the provider capability / terminal-run check is kept unchanged.
- the sentinel never enters evidence: if (c) fires the detail carries an occurrence count, not the transcript. A redaction check that prints the value it was watching for has moved the leak rather than closed it.
No real user secret was used at any point; the value is a per-run synthetic sentinel.

FALSIFICATION, as a differential rather than just a red (evidence ~/cap-evidence/nweh-falsification/{mutant-run.log,restore-run.log,mutant-build.log,restore-build.log}):
  MUTANT — extension/lib/browser-tools.js mapper returns value: c.value, rebuilt:
    RESULT: 19 passed, 2 failed. The two failures are exactly the redaction checks:
      FAIL: cookies: list_cookies returns no value field (metadata only) — in the model's own context — {"decodedValueKeys":...}
      FAIL: cookies: the seeded synthetic value reaches NO message the provider received — {"sentinel":"nweh_synthetic_..."}
    The two that stayed GREEN: "the redaction probe run executed list_cookies for real (capability granted, envelope settled, run terminal)" and "the probe fixture was NON-EMPTY". So the redaction assertions are the ones doing the work; the plumbing is not what reddened. That is the differential this bead's acceptance asked for.
  RESTORE — mapper reverted, rebuilt: RESULT: 21 passed, 0 failed.
  PRISTINE at this sha: RESULT: 21 passed, 0 failed, receipt {"result":"PASS","exit":0,"timedOut":false,"termSent":false,"residue":[],"cleaned":true}, runId 72e9f4e6e938d4e8.
The suite is now 21 checks: the 19 restored by the selector repair, minus the one weak cookie check, plus three.

OPERATIONAL NOTE, recorded because it cost a run and it is my error not the harness's: my first attempt at the pristine run was launched while a flock -n check in the same command batch was reporting the lock HELD — the two raced and the launch proceeded regardless, so the statement I had just sent ("checked FREE before launching") was false for that attempt. I killed it, and the kill crashed the supervisor in teardown: readProcIdentity (scripts/security-suite-custody.mjs:61) read /proc/<pid>/stat for a child that had already exited and threw an uncaught ENOENT, so the run left NO receipt at all. That is a real robustness defect in the custody chain, filed separately, and it is the same shape as everything else tonight: a failure that erases its own evidence. The clean re-run waited for LOCK-FREE-CONFIRMED before launching and produced the receipts above.

title: The security gate reported a section it never ran: providerRequests [] and both cookie-redaction checks absent from the transcript, on a gate whose subject is credential leakage — masked by an exit-124 timeout
description:
Distinct from the selector migration (chrome-agent-platform-4vfj), which is the CAUSE. This bead is the DEFECT CLASS and the classification rule that let it hide, and it is filed separately because the sentence that matters is not about selectors.

THE SENTENCE: a gate inside test:all reported a section it never ran. providerRequests:[] proves no model turn started, so this was not a check that ran and passed quietly — it was a check that did not exist. And the checks that did not exist were the COOKIE-REDACTION ones, on a gate whose whole subject is credential and cookie leakage. That is not a neutral gap.

MEASURED BEFORE, on unmodified origin/main @ c80b8abc (fresh detached worktree; npm ci + deno install + npm run build:production all rc=0; canonical lock verified free with flock -n before launch and released cleanly — receipt residue [], cleaned true, groupSurvived false, killSent false):

  npm run test:security
  CAP_SECURITY_RESULT {"result":"FAIL","scenario":"production","exit":124,"timedOut":true,"termSent":true,"killSent":false,"cleaned":true}
  wall 23:36:46 -> 23:38:46 BST = 120 s = PRODUCTION_TIMEOUT_MS (scripts/security-suite-custody.mjs:31)
  runner.log: 16 PASS, then
  FAIL: script.run: a model-initiated run_script (real provider path) pauses on the approval card with the source shown and the script un-run
        — {"setProvider":"openai-compatible","composer":false,"card":null,"lastRunAt":null,"providerRequests":[],"overflow":0,"threadText":""}
  Evidence: /home/paulkinlan/.local/state/chrome-agent-platform/security-suite/ab2a08c3ee28a5c5/

The suite reached 17 of its 19 checks. The two it never reached:
  cookies: the redaction probe run executed list_cookies for real (capability granted, envelope settled, run terminal)
  cookies: list_cookies returns no value field (metadata only) — in the model's own context

WHY IT HID — THE CLASSIFICATION RULE THAT MASKED IT. The receipt's headline was exit 124 / timedOut:true. This repo's own canon (AGENTS.md, "Test honesty", observer rule 5) says a timeout is INCONCLUSIVE and an environmental verdict is never a product red. That rule is correct in general, and here it completed the masking: the FAIL was printed to runner.log roughly 100 seconds BEFORE the supervisor sent TERM, but anyone reading the receipt saw a timeout and moved on. One failure mode hiding another, with our own discipline doing the hiding.

THE RULE THIS BEAD ASKS THE PLAYBOOK TO ADOPT (coord's wording, confirmed by these timestamps rather than by argument): **a timeout is environmental only if nothing failed before it. A timeout that follows a failed assertion is a failure, and the assertion is what you report.** Operationally: on any receipt with timedOut:true, read runner.log for FAIL lines before classifying the run as environmental.

WHY IT ALSO HUNG (arithmetic, not a second defect). The suite spent its whole 120 s budget in polling loops waiting on a run that could never start: the 20-try composer loop at 250 ms, then the 60-try approval-card loop at 500 ms, then section 7's own waits. A hang that is retries multiplied by waits against a precondition that can never become true is worth recognising by shape — it is not a slow machine.

MEASURED AFTER the four-selector repair (chrome-agent-platform-4vfj, stacked candidate cap/4vfj-security-suite @ 835bff08):
  CAP_SECURITY_RESULT {"result":"PASS","exit":0,"timedOut":false,"termSent":false,"killSent":false,"residue":[],"cleaned":true}
  wall 23:48:19 -> 23:48:34 BST = 15 s (was 120 s + TERM)
  runner.log: RESULT: 19 passed, 0 failed — including the run_script approval-card check and BOTH cookie-redaction checks
  Evidence: /home/paulkinlan/.local/state/chrome-agent-platform/security-suite/490692ad190a9a68/
exit 0 was not accepted as proof on either side; both transcripts were read and the PASS/FAIL lines counted (17-of-19 before, 19-of-19 after).

ACCEPTANCE:
1. npm run test:security reaches all 19 checks and reports 19/0 with exit 0 and timedOut:false. DONE on the candidate, awaiting landing.
2. The classification rule above is written into the playbook / AGENTS.md observer rules, so the next exit-124 is read for a preceding FAIL before it is called environmental. NOT DONE — this is the durable half and it is the reason this bead exists separately from 4vfj.
3. A gate that cannot reach a section says so. The suite printed its FAIL and then hung; nothing in the receipt distinguished "ran 19, failed 1" from "ran 17, timed out". Consider carrying a reached/total count in CAP_SECURITY_RESULT so a truncated run is legible from the receipt alone. NOT DONE, and it is a judgement call for the owner — the cheapest version is a checkedCount/expectedCount pair in the result JSON.

RELATED: chrome-agent-platform-4vfj (the migration and its guard — the cause), chrome-agent-platform-cwy2 (the same class in sidebar-parity: a harness that ran zero of its checks while its registry row still asserted a verdict), chrome-agent-platform-nco2 (subset gates that cannot see cross-cutting guards).

description:
MEASURED on unmodified origin/main @ a3e35928 (worktree /home/paulkinlan/worktrees/cap-sidebar-parity after npm ci + deno install + npm run build:production; transcript /tmp/cap-a11y-baseline.log):

  npm run test:a11y  ->  exit=1
  FAIL: slash palette is an accessible textbox-with-popup (haspopup + expanded + controls) - {"popupId":"popup-1","activeId":"cmp-1-opt-1","popupHidden":false}
  FAIL: slash palette names the highlighted option as the active descendant - {"popupId":"popup-1","activeId":"cmp-1-opt-1","popupHidden":false}
  slash palette attrs -> {}
  FAIL: at palette is an accessible textbox-with-popup (haspopup + expanded + controls) - {"popupId":"popup-1","activeId":null,"popupHidden":true}

a11y-audit.ts is class "gate", npm "test:a11y" (scripts/lib/harness-registry.ts:71) and runs inside test:all. It carries no expectedRed (expectedRed is kat-only), so a GATE IN test:all IS RED ON MAIN TODAY and no bead owned it.

MECHANISM (measured, read-only CDP probe on the loaded hub):
  document.querySelector('agent-composer textarea#task-input') -> false   (the selector the four checks read)
  document.querySelector('#composer [data-composer-input]')    -> true
  the textarea's real id is "composer-input"; its role attribute is null with the palette closed
The palette itself DID open and highlight an option (popupHidden:false, activeId cmp-1-opt-1), so the product is doing something. But paletteCombobox() reads every asserted attribute off `document.querySelector('agent-composer textarea#task-input')` with optional chaining (scripts/a11y-audit.ts:399, 406-414, 442): a null element yields null for role / aria-haspopup / aria-expanded / aria-activedescendant, so `attrs` comes back {} and the four checks CANNOT PASS regardless of product behaviour. The guard that should have named this - `if (!t) throw new Error('no composer textarea')` at :399 - does not surface: the run continued to the checks, so the throw is being swallowed by the cdp.evl helper. Two instrument defects: a stale selector, and a guard whose failure is silent.

LABELLED HONESTLY: what is verified is (a) the gate is red on main, (b) the asserted element does not exist, (c) the checks read attributes off it with ?. so they are unpassable. NOT verified: whether the WAI-ARIA 1.2 combobox contract (CAP-FB-20260830-SLASH-PALETTE-COMBOBOX-01) also has a REAL product defect underneath. That question can only be answered by re-running after the selector is repaired.

CORRECTION TO MY FIRST REPORT, then the sweep and the fix shape (coord asked for both verbatim). I told coord three files. The real number on origin/main tip d0f01545 is 35 files, ~150 sites. I under-reported because I only listed what I had personally hit; the grep is below and is reproducible in one command.

THIS IS AN ANNOUNCED MIGRATION THAT WAS NEVER COMPLETED, not a set of independent stale selectors. Bead chrome-agent-platform-sndb deliberately removed the fixed ids and pinned the removal in tests/agent-composer-unique-ids.test.ts, which asserts (1) AgentComposer must NOT hardcode <textarea id="task-input"> or <button id="run-task">, (2) it MUST expose [data-composer-input] and [data-composer-send], (3) focusInput() resolves via [data-composer-input], (4) NTP and sidepanel declare distinct composer host ids. The reason was real: #composer and #thread-composer share one document, so getElementById('task-input') silently resolved to the hub composer while the user was in the thread view and input went to a hidden element. The product half landed and is unit-pinned. The harness half did not: only 9 files in the whole repo mention the stable hooks (git grep -ln 'data-composer-input|data-composer-send' -- scripts cap-evidence tests): chrome-journeys.ts, sidebar-parity.ts (as of cwy2), lib/harness-registry.ts, 4 cap-evidence one-offs, and 2 tests. b5q4 told the fleet to use the stable hooks on 2026-09-18 and named the drift; nothing swept.

REPRO: git grep -n 'task-input|run-task' -- scripts cap-evidence tests | grep -v data-composer

GATES INSIDE test:all (highest severity, in this order):
- scripts/a11y-audit.ts:399,406,442 — 'agent-composer textarea#task-input'. MEASURED RED TODAY: 4 combobox checks fail, exit 1 (/tmp/cap-a11y-baseline.log on unmodified a3e35928). Silent mechanism: :406 reads t?.getAttribute(...) so a null element yields null for role/haspopup/expanded/activedescendant and attrs comes back {} — the checks cannot pass, and the failure reads as a product ARIA defect. The guard that should name it, 'if (!t) throw new Error("no composer textarea")' at :399, never surfaces (the run continued to the checks), so cdp.evl is swallowing the page exception — that swallow is its own defect.
- scripts/security-suite.ts:339,347,417,426 — centerOf('#task-input') / '#run-task', and centerOf at :201 is a plain document.querySelector with NO fallback. STATIC FINDING, NOT RUN (running it takes the canonical Chrome lock and would queue every other lane's browser gate behind me, so I did not). Mechanism, each link verified by reading plus the live probe: #task-input is absent -> clickAt returns false -> the 20-try loop leaves composer=false -> the typing and Run click inside 'if (composer)' never happen -> the check at :361 'script.run: a model-initiated run_script pauses on the approval card' includes composer in its condition, so it FAILS LOUDLY. Worth saying twice: this one is loud because composer is in the assertion. That is the pattern the other 34 files should copy, and it is why I am not claiming a silent pass here.
- scripts/component-gallery-smoke.ts:200,216,217 — c.querySelector('#task-input'), and :217 also probes '#run-task, .run'. Not run; classify before fixing.
- scripts/chrome-journeys.ts — 38 sites, most routed through boxOf() at :367-380 which DOES carry the compat mapping (#task-input -> [data-composer-input], #run-task -> [data-composer-send]). Two read it directly with no fallback: :2688 comp?.querySelector('#task-input') and :2721 document.querySelector('agent-composer #task-input')?.value ?? ''. Both use ?. / ?? so they read null or empty string and the checks around them can pass on nothing. That is the silent shape inside the suite's strongest gate.

KATs (run by test:kat, also a gate): kat-local-files.ts 7, kat-thinking-trace.ts 4, kat-composer-slash-commands.ts 3, kat-composer-grow.ts 3, kat-tool-call-clarity.ts 3, kat-mic-state.ts 3, kat-webmcp-honest-errors.ts 2, kat-patch-asset.ts 2, kat-bundled-execute.ts 2, kat-progress-inline.ts 1, kat-mcp-tool-injection.ts 1.
NAMED harnesses: agent-access-journeys.ts 11 (registry says 81/7), webmcp-acceptance.ts 8, ui-integration.ts 4, run-status-lifecycle.ts 4, read-page-host-grant-acceptance.ts 4, system-prompts-integration.ts 3, tool-call-evidence.ts 2, page-actions-journey.ts 2, live-run-evidence.ts 2, live-every-tab.ts 2, keyless-first-result.ts 2, mic-transcript-smoke.ts 1.
ONE-OFFS: cap-evidence/sndb-composer-unique-evidence.ts 15, cap-evidence/h638-open-trace.ts 4.
TESTS TO AUDIT (may be pins asserting absence, which are correct, or fixtures which are stale): durable-runs.test.ts 3, first-run-onboarding-composition.test.ts 1, components.test.ts 1, sw-route-modularization.test.ts 1, sw-dispatch-authority-census.test.ts 1.

FIX SHAPE — the composer is addressed by a stable hook or it is not addressed at all:
1. ONE resolver, not 35 patches. scripts/lib/composer-target.ts exporting the scoped selectors and a helper that takes the composer HOST id (ntp.html has two: #composer and #thread-composer, so a bare document-wide [data-composer-input] is wrong for the same reason the fixed ids were). Every harness imports it; no selector literal for the composer survives outside it.
2. A STATIC GUARD that pins the RULE, not today's instances: fail if 'task-input' or 'run-task' appears as a selector anywhere in scripts/, cap-evidence/ or tests/ outside the resolver and the sndb pin. Per this repo's own canon a rule-pin owes a second mutant that ADDS a fresh instance, so the guard is proven to cover the rule rather than the current 150 sites. Without this the migration silently un-completes again the next time someone writes a harness.
3. An absent composer must be LOUD and NAMED. Delete the ?. / ?? reads that turn a missing element into null, an empty string or {}: they are what made a11y-audit's red look like a product ARIA defect and what lets chrome-journeys:2688/2721 pass on nothing. Fix the cdp.evl swallow so a page-side throw surfaces. security-suite.ts:361 including composer in its assertion is the model.
4. Migrate in severity order and MEASURE each harness after its step rather than assuming: a11y-audit (red today) -> chrome-journeys' two direct reads -> security-suite -> component-gallery-smoke -> the KATs -> the named harnesses -> cap-evidence one-offs -> audit the 5 test files.
