title: Nothing runs cap-evidence/constrained-width-layout.ts automatically: the repaired checks are a runbook, not a gate
description:
Found by the independent review of cap/l3ts-check-strength (ac0a62d4).

MEASURED - NOTHING RUNS THIS DRIVER AUTOMATICALLY.
  git grep -n "constrained-width-layout" -- tests/ scripts/ package.json
  -> NO MATCHES.
It is absent from scripts/lib/harness-registry.ts, and no test, script or npm
script refers to it. It runs when a human runs it, and at no other time.

WHY THIS IS THE FINDING WITH THE LONGEST TAIL: q264 and qzae were repaired IN THIS
FILE, on the strength of measurement, and landed. Because nothing runs it, the
checks repaired to catch a regression cannot catch one. The repair is a runbook,
not a gate. The next change to the grid track rule (minmax(0, 1fr)) or to the
@container rule in sidepanel.html can restore the exact defect and every automatic
gate stays green - which is the state that produced q264/qzae in the first place.

THE DRIVER IS GATE-READY, which is why this is cheap: it asserts on geometry
(never appearance), it launches Chrome through launchChrome() so it takes a
browser slot rather than a fixed port, and it already carries a clean exit-code
contract - `Deno.exit(fail ? 1 : 0)` on the last line.

PRECEDENT IN THIS REPO - 5 of the 17 cap-evidence drivers are referenced, this one
is not. The mechanism used by tests/tar-stream.test.ts:15-16 is a STATIC URL
reference, with the reason in a comment:
  // Static references so buildReverseGraph in scripts/select-tests.mjs links
  // evidence instruments to this test
  const _CHROME_ACCEPTANCE = new URL("../cap-evidence/11rm1-tar-stream-acceptance.ts", import.meta.url);
That reference is what makes scripts/select-tests.mjs' buildReverseGraph link the
instrument to the test, so a change to the instrument selects the test.

PROPOSAL - two levels, and they are not the same thing. Doing (1) alone is cheap
and closes the "a change nobody notices" half; (2) is what makes it a gate.
  (1) SELECTION LINKAGE (cheap, proven pattern, no new browser budget): add the
      static `new URL("../cap-evidence/constrained-width-layout.ts",
      import.meta.url)` reference into a test that owns this surface, so a change
      to the driver selects that test under `npm run test:changed`.
  (2) EXECUTION AS A GATE (what the finding actually asks for): register the driver
      in scripts/lib/harness-registry.ts with its class and exit-code contract, so
      its assertions run without a human. Cost: one headless Chrome launch taking a
      browser slot via launchChrome(); tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts and
      the journey harness already do this, so the budget exists.
  (3) OR the two load-bearing assertions - deep min-content containment, and the
      collapsed rule firing in BOTH directions - folded into an existing registered
      harness that already drives the built extension, spending no new browser.

WHAT MAKES IT UNSAFE TO WIRE IN AS-IS, and must be decided rather than ignored:
  - the driver READS A BASE BUILD via CAP_ACCEPTANCE_EXT. A gate must run it
    against the tree under test, not a base build, or it asserts on the wrong tree.
  - it MUTATES the loaded page (renames elements, forces widths, rewrites label
    text). That must be inside the harness's own browser instance, never against
    anything another process measures.
  - it must not depend on ambient state it does not create (fleet convention,
    chrome-agent-platform-p15i): the base build it reads is a path a human supplies.
  - it writes evidence to cap-evidence/l3ts-constrained-width/. Confirm that path
    is not inside the tracked tree at gate time (a gate that dirties the tree it
    is testing fails the next run - the same shape as p15i).

ACCEPTANCE: the driver either runs in an automatic gate with a recorded red/green
run at HEAD, or this bead is closed with the stated reason it cannot be and a
pointer to where its two load-bearing assertions ARE enforced automatically.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
Independent review of fix/harness-marks-live @ d0f01545 (PASS).

THE FIX WORKS — re-derived, not accepted. The same mutant, both drivers:
- PRE-fix driver (origin/main cap-evidence/): `PASS hub: the Jobs board's content is inset like its own panel header` while 8 others failed -> 38 passed / 8 failed, exit 1. The check passed on a tree where BOTH elements it measures are absent.
- NEW driver: `FAIL ... {"bodyLeft":null,"headLeft":null}` -> 37 passed / 9 failed, exit 1.
Mutant: rename `#jobs-board-host` (ntp.html:1103) and the jobs-section `.panel-head` (ntp.html:1099) away, in a copy of the canonical extension. So absence now fails, and the check has teeth. Baseline unmutated = 46/0 with the check passing, which is the positive control.

ONE NEW DEFECT, MEASURED, NOT INFERRED — the fix introduces a false-red on a legitimate layout.
`padLeft` splits the padding string on whitespace and takes index [1]. For a UNIFORM (single-value) padding there is no [1], so it returns null and the check fails — even though both elements are present, their padding is read, and the property being asserted HOLDS.

Control: both elements present, both `style="padding:14px"` (left insets equal, so the check should PASS).
- PRE-fix driver: PASS, 46/0, exit 0.
- NEW driver: FAIL, 45/1, exit 1 -> `{"bodyPadding":"14px","headPadding":"14px","bodyLeft":null,"headLeft":null}`.
The failure detail contradicts its own verdict: it shows the two padding strings and still reports failure, because only the *token count* differed.

So the fix swapped one conflation for its mirror image: before, absent and zero were indistinguishable; now, "no second token" is treated as "no element".

Suggested predicate (keeps absence failing, accepts a uniform shorthand):
    const padLeft = (value) => {
      const t = String(value ?? "").trim().split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
      if (!t.length) return null;                      // element absent -> FAIL, as intended
      const part = t.length >= 2 ? t[1] : t[0];        // 1 value == all four sides
      const n = parseFloat(part);
      return Number.isFinite(n) ? n : null;
    };

Severity, stated plainly: NOT a blocker. It is fail-CLOSED (red on a good state) rather than fail-open, the shipped tree uses `12px 14px` for both so it is unreachable today, and the driver is `named` so no gate runs it. But it is a check that can fail for the wrong reason, which is the class this commit set out to remove. Worth fixing immediately as a follow-up, with the control above as its regression test.

Evidence bundle: ~/cap-evidence/rv-d0f01545/ (transcripts + the mutants' sed commands).

title: A collapsed-panel rule pinned statically but never observed firing (every chip check passed with the rule dead)
description:
Found by the independent review of cap/harness-logos (e72ca133), in cap-evidence/constrained-width-layout.ts.

OBSERVED: every side-panel chip check used the form `b.labelClipped || !b.wrapped`, which `white-space: nowrap` alone satisfies — with nowrap nothing ever wraps, so `!wrapped` is always true. Removing `container-type: inline-size` from `#agents-view` leaves the driver GREEN while the collapsed chip grows 34px -> 54px; the rule is dead and nothing notices.

WHY it goes dead rather than falling back: `#page-view` also carries `container-type`, but it is a SIBLING of `#agents-view`, not an ancestor of the chips. Removing it from `#agents-view` therefore leaves the chips with no container context at all, so `@container (max-width: 320px)` can never match.

Removal IS caught statically — tests/harness-marks.test.ts asserts `container-type: inline-size` on `#agents-view` — so what was missing is evidence that the rule TAKES EFFECT.

REPRO: `cp -a extension /tmp/m4 && sed -i 's| container-type: inline-size;||' /tmp/m4/sidepanel/sidepanel.html`, then run the driver with CAP_ACCEPTANCE_EXT=/tmp/m4. Pre-existing chip checks: 6/6 PASS. New collapsed-rule check: RED at 260px and 300px.

ACCEPTANCE: the behavioural check observes the collapsed state in BOTH directions — the label is clipped at 260/300px and not clipped at 400px — and goes RED when `container-type` is removed while the pre-existing checks stay green (recorded, to show what it adds).

STATUS: fixed and measured in the same session; see Evidence.md 'What the two new checks assert' and 'Mutations'.

title: A layout check that cannot fail: the shadow-root walk found nothing, and .every() on [] is true
description:
Found by the independent review of cap/harness-logos (e72ca133), in cap-evidence/constrained-width-layout.ts.

OBSERVED: the check 'hub: nothing inside the Jobs column holds the grid track open' was written on `shrinkHolders`, which is a plain `jobs.querySelectorAll('*')` walk. <jobs-board> renders its rows into a SHADOW ROOT, so that walk never saw them. The reviewer measured 0 entries in both the baseline and the mutant, so `.every(o => o.minContent <= 320)` was evaluated on an EMPTY array and returned true. The check passed on the base tree, where the defect is real and reproduced by twelve other checks.

The instrument that DOES cross the shadow root was already in the file: `deepMinContent` walks `node.shadowRoot.children` and correctly names `span.jb-excerpt` at 684px min-content. It was computed, printed and returned, and asserted on by nothing.

REPRO: put the check back in its vacuous form and run the driver against a base build: `CAP_ACCEPTANCE_EXT=<base extension> deno run -A cap-evidence/constrained-width-layout.ts` — it reports PASS while twelve checks fail.

ACCEPTANCE: (1) the containment property is asserted through the shadow-crossing instrument, not a light-DOM walk; (2) a non-vacuity guard fails loudly when the probe finds nothing, so no future check of this shape can pass by finding nothing; (3) the check goes RED on the base and on a reverted-`minmax` mutant, and green on the fixed tree — all three recorded.

STATUS: fixed and measured in the same session; see cap-evidence/l3ts-constrained-width/EVIDENCE.md sections 'What the two new checks assert' and 'Mutations'.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
INDEPENDENT REVIEW — cap/harness-logos @ e72ca133. Reviewer: separate session, own worktree
(/home/paulkinlan/worktrees/review-harness-logos), author's checkout untouched, canonical
checkout still on main@3091eaba.

VERDICT: PASS. The fix is correct, load-bearing and green. Findings below are about CHECK
STRENGTH and REPORTED NUMBERS; none of them changes the verdict.

=== WHAT I DROVE (not read)
Driver: cap-evidence/constrained-width-layout.ts, run 9 times on a built extension in
headless Chrome. 42 browser checks per run. Full suite once: EXIT CODE 0, 487 files,
4402 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored, wall 177s (verified with an explicit `; echo $?`,
not through a pipe).

  state                              browser checks
  branch (fix)                        42 passed /  0 failed
  TRUE BASE (origin/main, rebuilt-ish) 29 passed / 13 failed
  M1 grid minmax reverted             37 passed /  5 failed
  M2 padding removed                  39 passed /  3 failed
  M3 nowrap removed from .hq          41 passed /  1 failed
  M4 container-type removed           42 passed /  0 failed   <-- see F2
  M5 overflow:hidden removed          42 passed /  0 failed
  M6 min-width:0 added back           42 passed /  0 failed

=== CLAIM-BY-CLAIM
1. Jobs board grid — CONFIRMED, load-bearing. Base 1440px grid=[202.156px 685.844px]
   agents.w=202; 1100px grid=[116.359px 685.844px] agents.w=116. Branch [444 444] / [389 389].
   Mechanisms confirmed: the base rule at ntp.html:582 does use minmax(0,1fr) and the
   @media (min-width:1100px) override did regress it to bare `1fr`; and the track floor is
   content-driven — the shadow-crossing instrument names span.jb-excerpt at 684px min-content,
   matching the 685.844px track. M1 turns 5 checks red.
2. Padding — CONFIRMED. Base boardPad="4px 0px" vs headPad="12px 14px" exactly as reported;
   #jobs-board-host really does carry .jobs-board-body, so the check measures the fixed
   element. M2 turns 3 checks red.
3. Chip nowrap — CONFIRMED. M3 (nowrap off the .hq rule only) reddens the long-name check.
4. min-width:0 dropped as redundant — CONFIRMED, AND THE REASONING IS SOUND. M6 (adding it
   back) is byte-identical to baseline at every width: it was genuinely redundant, not
   "the check was too weak". M5 shows overflow:hidden on .hq is equally redundant.
5. Marks / provenance — CONFIRMED. Inline <svg viewBox> wrapper, currentColor, aria-hidden,
   no emoji, no hard-coded colour; asserted by tests/harness-marks.test.ts (19 passed), which
   extracts rule bodies rather than substrings. docs/HARNESS-MARKS-PROVENANCE.md is accurate.
6. Gate complaint — CONFIRMED: my npm test also ran 487 files, the same selection
   test:changed reported.

=== FINDINGS
F1 (should fix before landing) — A CHECK THAT CANNOT FAIL. The check "hub: nothing inside
   the Jobs column holds the grid track open" is `shrinkHolders.every(o => o.minContent <= 320)`.
   shrinkHolders uses jobs.querySelectorAll('*'), which does NOT cross the shadow root, so it
   is EMPTY in every state I drove — and .every() on [] is true. Proven empty (0 entries) in
   both baseline and M1. Meanwhile deepMinContent, the instrument that DOES cross the shadow
   root and correctly names span.jb-excerpt at 684px, is computed, printed, returned — and
   asserted on by nothing. The right instrument was built and then not used.
F2 (should fix before landing) — THE CONTAINER QUERY IS PINNED STATICALLY, NOT VERIFIED
   BEHAVIOURALLY. M4 removing `container-type: inline-size` from #agents-view leaves the
   browser driver 42/0 GREEN while the collapsed chip changes from 34px (label clipped) to
   54px (label visible) at 260/300px. The check that looks like it covers this —
   `labelClipped || !wrapped` — is satisfied by nowrap alone and cannot fail for this reason.
   It IS caught by the unit test (M4 -> 18 passed / 1 failed at harness-marks.test.ts:162,
   via ruleBody extraction), so removal is guarded; what is unverified is that the rule FIRES.
F3 (report accuracy) — THE BEFORE/AFTER TABLE IS NOT LIKE-FOR-LIKE. EVIDENCE.md says "same
   harness, same seeded content", but the totals are 24/11 (35 checks) before vs 42/0 (42
   checks) after — a different driver revision. Re-measured on the current driver the base is
   29 passed / 13 failed over 42 checks.
F4 (report accuracy) — PIXEL DRIFT. Author's base 1440px grid [198.156px 689.844px] vs my
   measured [202.156px 685.844px]: same 888px total, 4px redistributed. Author's "`.main-wrap`
   overflow at 1100px = 4px"; I measure 0px on the true base at 1100px (and the author's own
   two track figures sum to 806.2px against 826px available, which is not an overflow).
   Author's M7 [116.359px 717.844px]/32px vs my M1 [116.359px 713.844px]/28px. The agents
   track (116.359) and the padding (4px 0px) match exactly, so the fixture is right and
   something else shifts the Jobs track by 4px. Direction and mechanism confirmed; treat the
   exact figures as approximate.
F5 (minor) — The console summary prints `wrapped=${b.wrappedToMultipleLines}`, but the probe
   field is `wrapped`. Every printed line reads `wrapped=undefined`. The verdict is unaffected
   (the check reads b.wrapped correctly), but the printed evidence misleads.
F6 (minor) — EVIDENCE.md's fourth instrument note says conflating scrollWidth-at-width-0 with
   min-content "named the wrong culprit (.jb-excerpt)". That is not supported by the driver's
   own shadow-crossing instrument, which reports .jb-excerpt at 684px in BOTH base and fixed
   states, matching the track floor. The FIX is still right (a nowrap one-line excerpt is the
   intended design; the TRACK was the defect) — but the note reads as a measurement claim it
   cannot support.

=== WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY
- More than three registered agents (only pi / Claude Code / Codex exist here); the author
  lists this under "Not covered" honestly.
- The true side-panel width is a user drag; 260/300/400px emulation is a proxy.
- My TRUE BASE run could not complete a rebuild: `npm run build:production` fails with
  "dist.complete validation failed: indexed source is missing: extension/shared/harness-marks.js"
  when the branch's new module is removed under a dist.complete marker written by the branch
  build. Not a product defect (the marker binds indexed sources by design); it means my base
  run used base HTML/CSS with the stale branch bundle. The hub (ntp.html, loaded directly) is
  therefore a fully valid base; the sidepanel base is base-CSS-with-branch-JS, which is exactly
  the CSS-only isolation the claimed fix needs, and the wrap defect reproduces there (ws=normal).

=== WHY THE VERDICT IS PASS DESPITE F1/F2
The fix is proven the hard way: both defects reproduce on the base (29/13), every claimed line
is load-bearing under mutation except the ones the author correctly dropped, the mechanism
matches the diagnosis exactly, and the full suite is exit-0 green. F1 and F2 are weaknesses in
the TESTS, in the one direction this repo's canon is explicit about — a check that cannot fail
is the defect, not the reassurance — and they should be closed, but they do not make the fix
wrong, and the browser checks that DO have teeth (overflow, 60% share, padding inset, body
scroll, wrap) are all sensitive to mutation.

Landing on this verdict is the coordinator's call; the author fixes their own work.

title: Dispatch advertised ACP commands without bypassing protected CAP instructions
description: Discovered in wp7y on harness-tools 430b76fa: createAcpModel sends a CAP instruction prefix plus JSON.stringify(full prompt). Native /skill:x, /x and $x inserted by composer are therefore not top-level ACP commands. wp7y is explicitly insertion-only by supervisor decision; UI must disclose this. Design/review a native command prompt contract preserving CAP protected instructions, tool authority and approval behavior; drive body-only skill markers for Pi/Claude/Codex where supported. Pi acpRunConfig execution refusal stays until CAP tool registration is implemented. No silent raw-prompt bypass.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
READ COMPLETE — checked fetched origin/main BY CONTENT at 7b6ab342 before implementing. Two structural findings change what this bead is, and a design ruling is needed before code. No edits made.

FINDING 1 — THE SUBJECT IS NOT ON MAIN. createAcpModel does not exist at origin/main. Neither do acp-model.js, acp-model-host.js, acp-model-proxy.js, acp-run-config.js or acp-run-permissions.js. Main carries only acp-client.js, acp-native.js, acp-runner.js, acp-thread-journal.js. The subject lives on TWO UNLANDED branches: origin/feat/harness-tools (5 ahead of main, 24 BEHIND) and origin/feat/wp7y-picker-on-430b76fa (7 ahead). So there is nothing to fix on main, and any fix lands only after harness-tools does. Sequencing is a coordinator decision, not mine.

FINDING 2 — THE DEFECT IS REAL ON THE BRANCH, verified by reading both sides rather than trusting the bead. acp-model.js:56 sends ONE text part: \"Follow the CAP instructions and conversation below...\" + JSON.stringify(prompt). The live o7v2/wp7y probes (~/cap-evidence/harness-capabilities-20260921) show all three adapters dispatch a command only when the command is the ENTIRE text of its prompt part — measured frames: {\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"/skill:cap-probe\"} for pi, \"$cap-probe\" for Codex, \"/cap-probe\" for Claude — each sent as its OWN turn after a separate preamble turn (2 session/prompt calls per fixture). Therefore a composer-inserted /skill:x lands inside the JSON blob and is conversation data, never a top-level command. The bead's premise is TRUE.

WHAT MUST NOT BE BYPASSED: the untrusted fence in extension/lib/system-prompts.js (UNTRUSTED_POLICY_PLACEHOLDER, fenceUntrustedText, renderUntrustedPolicy). Sending a bare command alone drops that envelope — that is precisely the 'silent raw-prompt bypass' this bead forbids.

FOUR OPTIONS, each trading differently, which is why this needs a ruling:
A. TWO-TURN: instructions turn, then the bare command as its own turn. MEASURED to work — it is exactly what the probes did. BLOCKED on v05y: the model opens a fresh ACP session per run with no retained session lifecycle, so turn 2 would not share turn 1's session.
B. MULTI-PART PROMPT: prompt: [{instructions}, {command}]. Wire-legal today — acp-client.prompt() already builds promptParts and appends extra parts. UNKNOWN whether any adapter honours a command in a NON-FIRST part; never probed. One cheap probe answers it.
C. INSERTION-ONLY + EXPLICIT UI DISCLOSURE — the current supervisor decision on wp7y. Zero bypass risk, no new protocol, and the bead already requires the UI to disclose it.
D. BARE COMMAND WITHOUT THE ENVELOPE — explicitly forbidden here; drops the fence. Not an option, listed so it is visibly rejected rather than silently unconsidered.

MY DEFAULT IF NO RULING ARRIVES: C stands, because it is already the supervisor's decision and carries no security trade. The useful non-guessing work is the cheap read-only probe that decides A vs B — measure whether a command in a second prompt part (or a second turn on a retained session) still dispatches with the CAP envelope intact. That produces the fact the ruling needs.

ONE DEFECT TO FIX WHATEVER IS CHOSEN: the branch's own pin is weak. tests/acp-model.test.ts asserts only assert(prompt.includes(\"CAP policy\")) — a substring pin that survives almost any restructuring, the repo canon's failure mode 2. Any option needs a pin that goes RED when the fence is dropped.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
DECISION RECORD — coord ruling seq944, 2026-09-23.

RULING: OPTION C — INSERTION-ONLY, WITH UI DISCLOSURE — IS THE LANDING BEHAVIOUR. It carries no security trade, needs no new protocol, and is already the supervisor's decision on wp7y; that makes it the correct default rather than a compromise.

A is BLOCKED on v05y (fresh ACP session per run, no retained lifecycle, so a second turn loses the first turn's session).
B is UNPROVEN and gets a cheap READ-ONLY PROBE. If B proves out it becomes its own scoped change with its own evidence — not part of this landing.
D — a bare command without the CAP envelope — IS REJECTED, and the reason belongs in the record: it drops the untrusted fence in extension/lib/system-prompts.js (UNTRUSTED_POLICY_PLACEHOLDER / fenceUntrustedText / renderUntrustedPolicy). A dropped fence is not an option. Recorded here beside the live options so nobody re-proposes it in three weeks.

SEQUENCING (one line for the next reader): 6yfm cannot land before feat/harness-tools does; that branch is 5 ahead and 24 BEHIND origin/main, so its rebase is its own job.

PIN REPLACEMENT IS REQUIRED WHATEVER LANDS: tests/acp-model.test.ts asserts only assert(prompt.includes("CAP policy")). That is canon failure mode 2 — the fragment it looks for is also present in the damaged version, so the pin cannot fail on the thing it exists to protect. The replacement must be driven: remove the envelope, confirm the assertion goes RED, restore, confirm GREEN, and name the mutant in the commit.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
OPTION-B PROBE COMPLETE — read-only, no repo file touched, no gates run. Evidence: ~/cap-evidence/6yfm-multipart-probe-20260923/ (REPORT.md, probe-multipart.mjs, score.mjs, per-adapter frames.jsonl/result.json).

ANSWER: B IS NOT PROVEN. On the only adapter whose controls both behaved (pi), a command in a NON-FIRST prompt part was NOT dispatched — it was treated as conversation, exactly like the JSON blob today. So C (insertion-only + UI disclosure) stands as the landing behaviour WITH a measurement behind it, and B does NOT become a scoped change on this evidence.

METHOD: three arms per adapter, fresh ACP session each (v05y: fresh session per run, so arms must not share one). A control-positive [{command}] — the o7v2 baseline shape, marker EXPECTED. B [{envelope},{command}] — the question. C control-negative [{envelope + JSON.stringify(command)}] — CAP's shape today, marker NOT expected. Fixture skill returns a unique marker from its body.

THE SCORING RULE HAD TO BE REPLACED MID-PROBE — canon failure mode 4, caught live and worth recording. Under the first rule ('the marker appears in the reply') pi reported dispatched=true for ALL THREE ARMS, including the control-negative that by construction must not dispatch. A weaker reading would have reported 'B works on pi'. The frames showed the mechanism: in arms B and C the model made a READ TOOL CALL on the fixture's SKILL.md and echoed the marker out of the file it had just read. The marker proved the model could read a file in its cwd, not that the adapter dispatched a command. Replacement discriminator: NATIVE DISPATCH == marker returned AND ZERO tool calls in that turn — a native dispatch loads the body through the adapter's own command path and needs no filesystem tool.

RESULTS.
pi — B FAILS, both controls behaved. A: marker, 0 tool calls => NATIVE DISPATCH. B: marker, 1 read => NOT a dispatch. C: marker, 1 read => NOT a dispatch. Positive control dispatched, negative control did not, and B behaved like the negative control. This is the clean funnel and it is the answer.
codex — INCONCLUSIVE, the instrument's own positive control FAILED. Arm A (the shape o7v2 proved dispatches) made a file read instead of dispatching, so no arm's verdict is usable on this adapter — including arm C's 'marker with 0 tool calls', which is most likely the skill body already in the codex process context (codex-acp calls skills/list over its own channel to the codex binary, invisible in ACP frames). Reporting that as 'CAP's current shape dispatches on codex' would be the same error I had just caught.
claude — INCONCLUSIVE, ENVIRONMENTAL. All three arms returned -32603 'Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 API key is invalid' (errorKind authentication_failed; Claude Code child exited 143). Zero product signal; not a pass, not a failure, not evidence about B.

RESIDUAL UNKNOWNS: (1) codex needs an instrument that separates a native dispatch from a preloaded body — a fixture written AFTER session start, or a marker rotated between arms, would do it; (2) claude was never measured (its adapter needs working auth; this probe deliberately did not supply or hunt for credentials); (3) one fixture, one command, one turn per arm — this measures the dispatch mechanism, not the whole advertised catalogue; (4) no claim about option A, which stays blocked on v05y and was not probed; (5) the fixture skill sits in the adapter's cwd, which is what makes the agentic read possible at all — the CONFOUND is an artefact of the fixture, the pi DISPATCH result is not.

title: acp:service silently defaults to pi and starts on a harness the machine does not have
description:
Paul, on his Mac (2026-09-18): "Harness mismatch: requested `claude-code`, but running bridge started `pi`" plus "Could not start pi: executable not found (`/Users/paulkinlan/.local/bin/pi`)" — "why is this still an issue, I have claude code, it shouldn't use pi."

## Root cause: one wrong default, two symptoms
`scripts/acp-service.mjs:37` — `const HARNESS = String(args.harness || "pi")`. The service was installed with no `--harness`, so it came up on **pi**, which is not installed on that machine; the client asked for `claude-code` in its own settings, and the bridge had nothing to fall back on but the default. The mismatch message itself is the `lpmv` fix working (before it, the same state read as a bare "executable not found").

Per-connection selection (`acp-bridge.ts:297-300`, `?harness=claude-code`) is implemented and working — it is the *default* that is wrong, and a default that names a binary the machine may not have is how this happened.

## Fix (smallest honest shape)
1. **Choose the default from what the machine has** — when `--harness` is absent, resolve the harness at install time from a documented preference order (claude-code, codex, pi), using the CLI each needs (`claude-code` → `claude`, `codex` → `codex`, `pi` → `pi`). The chosen harness is printed with its reason.
2. **Refuse loudly when none is present** — no silent pi: an error naming the harnesses and binaries checked and the `--harness` flag.
3. **Warn loudly when an EXPLICIT harness's binary is missing** — install-time, naming the binary, because that state installs a service that cannot start.
4. **`install --dry-run`** — print the resolved harness and the unit plan without writing anything, so the choice is inspectable and testable without touching the machine.

Constraints honoured: the harness set is unchanged (claude-code, codex, pi all remain); the per-connection path is untouched; the doctor's existing per-binary report is untouched.

Acceptance: `install --dry-run` on a machine with only `claude` present plans `claude-code`; with both `claude` and `pi` it plans `claude-code` (documented order); with `--harness pi` it plans pi **and warns** that pi is missing; with no harness binary it refuses, naming `--harness`; the doctor's uninstalled branch reports the same. No unit is written by any of these.

comments.text:
FIXED — branch `fix/acp-harness-default-detect` @ `b405aa6c` (v0.3.436, one commit with the bump). Independent verification wanted; I wrote neither the code nor the defects. **Both instances are one class, so they are one bead and one commit**, as coord asked.

## The class, and the rule for the record
**Anything the fleet assumes about its own box must be DETECTED or DECLARED, never defaulted.** Both symptoms came from a value chosen for *this* machine's layout and applied to Paul's.

## Instance 1 — the harness default
`acp-service.mjs` defaulted to `pi` with no `--harness`, so the service came up on a binary his Mac does not have while the tool he had was `claude`. Now: the default is resolved at install time from what the machine **has** (documented preference claude-code → codex → pi; binaries claude/codex/pi), printed with its reason; nothing present → **one-line refusal** naming `--harness` (exit 1); an **explicit** `--harness` whose binary is missing → **loud warning**, because that installs a service that cannot start; `install --dry-run` prints the plan and **writes nothing**. The harness set is unchanged; the per-connection path is untouched.

## Instance 2 — the working-directory default
`acp-bridge.ts` handed every session without a cwd `$HOME/journal` — real on this box, `/Users/paulkinlan/journal` on his Mac, which does not exist → *"Invalid params: `cwd` does not exist on the machine running the agent"*. `$HOME/journal` is now used **only when the directory is really there**; otherwise the host default is `""`, which is the module's **own documented contract** ("nothing is invented and the adapter reports the missing cwd itself"). The installer also parses and passes `--cwd` now (the bridge always accepted it; the installer could not set it) and the dry-run plan shows it.

## Mutants made red
- old `pi` default → **4 failures** (the claude-only case, the preference order, the refusal, the bridge line);
- old invent-a-path cwd default → **"nothing may be invented: {params:{cwd:\".../no-journal/journal\"}}"** — the failure text is Paul's symptom shape;
- the new `existsSync` import removed → 1 failure (and this is worth recording: **my own fix nearly repeated the defect I fixed in `d2vz` this afternoon** — an unimported reader — caught by checking the import rather than assuming it).
All restored byte-exact.

## Verified
`tests/acp-service-harness-default.test.ts` **8/8** (five harness cases, three cwd cases) plus `acp-service-doctor.test.ts` **6/6** (d1ti) unchanged → **14/0**; `test:changed` exit 0 (serial GREEN, 4390/0/1).

**Verification precondition, named because it is the point**: the cwd cases need a machine where `$HOME/journal` does **not** exist. My tests create exactly that (a temp HOME in a subprocess), which is why the fix is testable here at all — the real machines where it failed are the ones we cannot see.

One wrinkle worth knowing for the landing: the post-commit hook bumped twice while I was shaping this (once for the fix, once for the changelog commit's own message), so the branch is a single amended commit at **0.3.436** with exactly one user-facing entry, rather than two bumps and a meaninglessly-worded second entry.

FOLLOW-UP, on Paul's direction (via coord, 2026-09-18): **the guard was the wrong shape — the default is deleted instead.**

His words: *"the harness should not even know journal exists."* `existsSync` made the invention **safe** while leaving the **knowledge** in: on any machine that happens to have a `~/journal` directory, the bridge would still have silently adopted it as the session's working directory.

So `defaultCwd()` is now `args.cwd || ""` — no guess, no detection, and `""` is this module's own documented contract ("nothing is invented and the adapter reports the missing cwd itself"). Swept: the module header, the `applyHostDefaults` contract line and the installer's two comments no longer name a default that does not exist. **And the deletion found the thing the guard was hiding** (see `5i9i`): `tests/acp-runner.test.ts` asserted the adapter received `${HOME}/journal`, so the harness's own suite enforced the convention and **the guarded version's green gate was machine-dependent** — it passed on this box and would have failed on Paul's Mac. title: [11rm] Add a backpressured TAR/PAX encoder without product wiring
description:
# First implementation slice: backpressured TAR/PAX encoder

## Context and why this is first

Parent: chrome-agent-platform-11rm. Current main b590da1360328bf7a76e012a2aa813e4012dd047 has the 2g90 Options/TAR design but no production TAR encoder. The TAR-header function in tests/streamed-backup-contract.test.ts is test-local and truncates fixed fields; it is not a codec to wire into Export All.

The reconciliation is /home/paulkinlan/cap-evidence/astra/11rm-scope-20260918/RECONCILIATION.md. Its first step can be implemented without deciding the full backup member layout or weakening any restore/secret authority. Build only the raw regular-file encoder. Keep it unreachable from product backup buttons until admission, immutable staging and barrier integration exist.

## Scope

Add extension/lib/tar-stream.js (or the minimal equivalent) plus focused executing tests. Use native Web Streams/async iteration, with no new dependency or generic archive framework unless inspection shows a concrete need. A narrow contract is asynchronous entries {name, size, body} into a caller-provided WritableStream, with a cancellation signal and bounded result totals. Do not collect the entry iterable or payload chunks.

- Emit standard uncompressed ustar regular-file headers/padding/end blocks, using POSIX per-file PAX path/size records where ustar cannot represent the exact value. Only the required writer subset; no decoder, symlinks, hard links, devices, sparse encoding, compression or general metadata-preservation framework.
- Preserve valid Unicode/path bytes exactly; do not truncate or silently normalize. Refuse malformed/unpaired-surrogate, NUL, absolute or traversal member names. This wire-path validation is NOT the product target registry/admission policy.
- Handle sizes/counters exactly, using BigInt or equally lossless arithmetic. Reject fractional/non-finite/unsafe numeric inputs rather than rounding. Do not introduce file-count, file-size, aggregate-byte or 8GiB admission ceilings. Exercise the ustar-to-PAX size transition explicitly.
- Await sink backpressure. Check actual emitted body length against the declared length, including empty files. A short/long source, rejected write or cancellation must reject, stop reading, and abort/release the owned writer/reader resources. Never emit completion or close successfully after a failure. Bytes already emitted are provisional; the codec is not an integrity seal or rollback engine.
- Do not require a prebuilt global manifest, buffered body or new queue of pending writes. State the measured working-buffer bound separately from the already supplied single-entry metadata; do not claim universal 64KiB total memory.

No service-worker importer, Settings wiring, credential filtering, live target writes, registry/oracle rewrite, transaction journal port, v1 conversion or whole-profile acceptance in this slice. No claim that TAR checksums verify payload integrity. Existing incremental-sha256.js may be reused by the test/probe; do not duplicate it.

## Executable acceptance

1. Test the production encoder, not a copy embedded in a test. Multi-file fixture includes empty, binary, Unicode and paths requiring PAX; a real system TAR implementation lists/extracts exact names and byte contents. Missing TAR is an explicit setup failure, never a skip that silently substitutes header checks.
2. In a bounded functional probe, stream a generated payload above 512MiB to an owned file sink without holding the source/archive in memory; compare extracted bytes incrementally. Separately exercise more than 100,000 generated entries without building an entry array. Keep these large controls out of the fast unit iteration loop and use small fixtures for the mutation controls. These are codec controls, not a Settings export/restore verdict.
3. Pin the 8,589,934,591→8,589,934,592 size-header transition and exact PAX decimal value. If that check inspects headers without transferring an actual 8GiB payload, label it representation coverage, not a large-file round trip.
4. Observe first payload output before finite source exhaustion and bounded upstream consumption while a sink write is held. Removing awaited writes or adding collect-all buffering must fail a named assertion, not merely hit a launcher timeout. Short/long bodies, I/O failure and cancellation reject with no successful completion; a valid positive prevents an always-rejecting implementation from passing.
5. Named falsification controls: remove the await, bypass body-length validation, truncate the long path/omit PAX, and corrupt a header checksum. Preserve actual assertion failures and restored positives; do not count setup failure as a kill.
6. Drive the same shipped module and native Streams in an isolated real Chrome with owned OPFS source/sink and recorded byte-flow/results. Use the repo Chrome launcher/evidence helpers; no personal profile/provider. This is module behavior, not a file-picker or backup UI claim. The full loaded ≥590MiB export/restore remains parent11rm acceptance.

If initially inert, add a narrowly justified RETAINED entry tied to the next archive-stage consumer; remove it when a real importer appears. Record that no SW runtime dependency was added, and verify the final build rather than infer artifact identity from source hashes. Respect watcher/registry coupling; do not relax gates or alter partition exemptions.

Future implementer workflow: fresh durable worktree from fetched main; npm ci + deno install; production build after final commit; npm run test:file for iteration, npm run test:changed per change, npm test once before push. Independent different-model/session review and coordinator-owned landing. No raw full-suite command or test-only coverage exemption.

## What completion unblocks

The sealed TAR staging/admission layer gets a real streaming writer and interoperable fixtures; the strict TAR reader can develop against those fixtures. The barrier/recovery engine can proceed independently. This child does NOT satisfy dsnh: its planted-secret and unmanaged-target controls must later execute through the real streamed profile pipeline. It does not close parent11rm or make the existing JSON path unbounded.

This issue is the scoped next implementation candidate, not a claim that implementation has started. The coordinator routes the writer and reviewer.
acceptance_criteria: Production regular-file TAR/PAX encoder streams exact bytes under sink backpressure; interoperates with real TAR; preserves long/Unicode names and exact size representation beyond ustar; rejects length/I-O/cancel failures without successful completion. Small executing mutation controls plus bounded >512MiB and >100k-entry codec probes and real-Chrome module evidence. No Settings/SW/restore authority changes, no dsnh/11rm closure claim; coordinator routes implementation and independent review.
close_reason: Closed

Parent11rm and dsnh acceptance remain outside this encoder slice.

Ready for independent verification.

title: Performance baseline: measure the user-visible surfaces before any byte budget moves
description:
FILED 2026-09-18 by qwen2 on Paul's mandate relayed by coord: "I need us to ensure we are as performant as possible at all times." Coord's framing of what that changes: the 3 MB service-worker cap is no longer the goal - PERFORMANCE is - so the cap becomes a PROXY THAT SHOULD FOLLOW THE EVIDENCE rather than a number to defend. Nothing moves until measurement says so: no cap lifted because its name says "store", none kept because it is familiar.

FILED BEFORE MEASURING, deliberately, so the fleet can see what is being measured and why before any number exists. A baseline chosen after seeing results is a baseline chosen to justify them.

=== WHAT EXISTS TODAY ===
tests/bundle-budget.test.ts is the gate (CAP-FB-20260830-BUNDLE-BUDGET-01). STORE_SW_BUDGET_BYTES = 3_000_000 exactly - the test's own name calls it "the constitution number" - and it gates background/service-worker.js in the STORE-target build only (a developer build is unminified by design and the test returns early on the marker). Order is pinned: eval scrub BEFORE minify. Its falsification is already recorded: set the gate to 1 MB and the store build fails naming the top contributors.
TWO SOURCE COMMENTS SAY THE BUNDLE SITS ~10 BYTES UNDER THE CAP: tests/generated-module-hoisting.test.ts:3 ("service-worker bundle sat ~10 bytes under its 3 MB budget") and scripts/lib/shared-strings.mjs:6 (the ehsl shared-string work, same statement). That is why chrome-agent-platform-ycez has only 2,238 bytes of headroom against 26,155 bytes of admission. The budget is not loose; it is saturated, and saturation is the reason this bead exists - a saturated proxy that nobody has correlated with a user-visible cost is a cap governing landings for reasons that may no longer exist.

=== SURFACES TO MEASURE (user-visible, not merely present) ===
S1. Store service-worker COLD BOOT: registration to first message handled. This is the surface the 3 MB cap most plausibly proxies, because SW script bytes are parsed and compiled on every cold start, and Chrome kills idle SWs aggressively so cold starts are common, not rare.
S2. SW MESSAGE HANDLING: per-message dispatch latency at steady state, and the distribution rather than the mean - a p50 that hides a p99 is the same mistake as a green that hides a flake.
S3. NEW-TAB RENDER: first paint and time-to-interactive for the surface a person actually opens.
S4. AGENT HUB PARSE COST: the hub module's parse/compile/eval. ox5s bundled hub and side panel into single modules TODAY specifically to kill duplicate work, so this surface has a fresh, known-good before/after available - measure it and record what ox5s bought, which is also the calibration point for "how many bytes is a millisecond" on this surface.
S5. SIDE PANEL PARSE COST: same reasoning, and the other half of ox5s's change.
S6. THE WASM/EMSCRIPTEN ADMISSION PATH that ycez adds: not just its bytes but whether an admission changes S1 or S2 at all.

=== METHOD, in the form today's isocan lane work established ===
M1. A NUMBER WITH ITS CONDITIONS, NEVER A GREEN. Each measurement reports value + machine + load + build target + commit sha. "It passed" is not a measurement.
M2. TWO LOADS MINIMUM, so a result is a property rather than a lucky run. The isocan deep-lane sequence only became believable when the same code was measured at load 32.9, 41.2 and 58.4 - one point is an anecdote. Baseline idle, then under a stated artificial load, and say which.
M3. SCOPE THE INSTRUMENT TO THE THING MEASURED. Today a fork count taken with `ps -eo args` counted ANOTHER lane's processes and reported 39 where the true answer was 8; two wrong numbers reached a report before the instrument was pinned to the launched PID. Any timer, counter or profiler here gets the same treatment: prove it is measuring this build, this surface, this process.
M4. EACH PROBE SHOWN TO FAIL BEFORE IT IS TRUSTED. bundle-budget.test.ts already does this (set the gate to 1 MB, watch it fail). Every new timing probe gets the same: make the surface deliberately slower, confirm the probe moves, restore. A probe that has only ever been seen to pass is decoration - today a test NAMED "falsification" was proved vacuous by inserting `return []` into the function it claimed to exercise, and all four cases stayed green.
M5. PREFER THE PLATFORM'S OWN TIMERS over wall-clock around a whole build, and say which was used: CDP/DevTools Protocol metrics for paint and parse, performance.now() in-page for dispatch, and the extension's own SW lifecycle events for cold boot. Wall-clock around `npm run build` measures the machine, not the product.
M6. NO WRITES TO A SHARED CHECKOUT. Measure in an isolated worktree; a `reset --hard` by another lane destroyed uncommitted work in ~/isocan today at 12:19:55 and again in CAP at 12:36:31.

=== THE GATE QUESTION THIS MUST ANSWER ===
Propose what a gate should assert, in USER-VISIBLE TERMS (cold start ms, first paint ms, parse ms) rather than bytes - AND state what the byte budget is a proxy for, with the ratio if one is measurable (bytes of SW script per millisecond of cold boot, on this machine, at these two loads).
If the honest answer is "no measurable surface correlates with those bytes", THAT IS THE MOST VALUABLE RESULT AVAILABLE, because it means a saturated cap has been governing landings for reasons that no longer exist. Say so plainly rather than finding a correlation to justify the number. Equally: if cold boot DOES scale with SW bytes, the cap is vindicated and the answer is to make the bundle smaller, not to raise the cap.
Also answer whether 3_000_000 is a PLATFORM limit or a self-imposed constitution number. If Chrome has a real service-worker script-size or startup-time limit, name it and cite it; if 3 MB is ours, then under a performance mandate it needs a reason that is about performance.

=== THE CONCRETE QUESTION: chrome-agent-platform-ycez ===
ycez has been parked all day at 26,155 bytes against 2,238 bytes of headroom - infeasible under the cap since this morning. Under a performance mandate the question stops being "can it fit under 3 MB?" and becomes "DOES 26 KB HARM A MEASURED SURFACE?". This bead should answer it as a yes-or-no with a number: measure S1 and S2 with the admission present and absent, at both loads, same commit otherwise. If 26 KB moves cold boot by less than the run-to-run noise, say that and give the noise floor - a bead that has been blocked all day becomes unblocked by a measurement rather than by an argument about the cap.

=== EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE FOR THIS BEAD ===
No cap is moved, no budget constant is edited, and no gate is written here. This bead produces baselines and a recommendation. Changing STORE_SW_BUDGET_BYTES before the baseline exists is the failure mode the mandate is trying to end, in either direction.

OPEN QUESTION coord has put to Paul and which does NOT block the baselines: is the deliverable a performance GATE THAT FAILS REGRESSIONS, or an EFFORT TARGET to make slow things faster? Both need the same baselines, so measurement starts now. The answer changes what gets proposed at the end, not what gets measured.
close_reason: BASELINE COMPLETE + GATE PROPOSAL DELIVERED (k3, 2026-09-18). All six surfaces measured with rerunnable instruments and two-load, per-sample-ok/err discipline (cap-evidence/perf-4ctv/: S1/S2/S3/S4-S5 reports + logs). Headline findings: bytes are 8-10% of SW cold boot (spin-up/registration dominates); steady-state dispatch p50 sub-ms, p99 = event-loop contention; idle deep-tail worse than loaded (cold wake); ox5s delta shows REQUESTS (74→1) not bytes are the sensitive axis (DCL −30.6/−68.4ms, doubling under load); ycez admission ≈ +0.14–0.22ms of boot, below noise (three instruments agree). Gate proposal: user-visible surfaces (cold-boot p50, composer-ready ms at stated loads, two-load rule) — byte budget proxies ~40-60ms of a ~480-780ms boot and nothing measured correlates user-visible cost with bundle bytes. Stale '~10 bytes under' comments corrected to the measured 1,371 bytes (cap/4ctv-comment-fix @ fa340951, pushed; gates green). No cap moved, no gate written — the gate DECISION is Paul's, with the proposal recorded above and in the bead.

comments.author: qwen2
comments.text:
FIRST BASELINE NUMBERS (qwen2, 2026-09-18) - filed after the bead, measured on this repo's own real SW bundles. Evidence: /home/paulkinlan/cap-evidence/isocan-6oe-20260918/perf-sw-baseline-first-numbers.md
WHAT WAS MEASURED: V8 compile cost of three real service-worker bundles, snapshotted to /tmp first because another lane was rebuilding dist-versions/ concurrently and one file vanished between find and read. 546,057 B (dev, unminified) -> 3.90ms; 1,216,657 B (dist) -> 12.64ms; 2,998,629 B (store, minified) -> 42.61ms. Five fresh processes per bundle, low spread, all compiling successfully. Slope 15.8 ms per MB. Conditions: 32 cores, node v24.21.0, load 5.05/6.99/12.85.
ANSWER FOR ycez: 26,155 bytes costs ~0.41ms of compile (or ~0.37ms using the minified bundle's density, which is the right comparison since an admission ships minified). Both estimates agree at ~0.4ms. Against a service-worker cold boot - tens to hundreds of ms, including worker spin-up, fetch and top-level EVALUATION - ~0.4ms is below any plausible noise floor. So on the parse surface the answer to 'does 26 KB harm a measured surface?' is NO, NOT MEASURABLY.
CAVEATS, which are real and not a formality: (1) this is Node's V8 compiling an ES module, not Chrome starting a service worker - compile is the component that scales with bytes, which is why it is the right thing to isolate for a ratio, but S1 (real cold boot) is still owed; (2) the three bundles differ in more than size, so the slope conflates size with minification density - both estimates are given and agree to 0.05ms so the conclusion does not depend on which is right; (3) ONE load only, and my own method M2 asks for two before this is a property rather than an anecdote; (4) ycez's stated headroom of 2,238 bytes is STALE - the store bundle is 2,998,629 against STORE_SW_BUDGET_BYTES 3,000,000, i.e. 1,371 bytes of headroom, ~867 bytes grown since the bead was filed. Two source comments say '~10 bytes under' (tests/generated-module-hoisting.test.ts:3, scripts/lib/shared-strings.mjs:6); that was true when written and is not now.
ALSO WORTH HAVING: minification roughly DOUBLES cost per byte (0.71 -> 1.42 ms/100KB, dev to store). Fewer bytes, denser ones. So a gate expressed in BYTES measures a different thing in a dev build than in a store build - which is an argument for the user-visible framing in the mandate, from the data rather than from preference.
THE FIRST INSTRUMENT WAS INVALID AND WAS CAUGHT: it used new vm.Script, which compiles as a CLASSIC script, so the dev bundle threw 'Cannot use import statement outside a module' and the store bundle threw 'Cannot use import.meta outside a module' - the timings were parse-until-error, and a catch swallowed the error so the row looked like data. The one bundle that did compile reported 0.00ms median with a 10.33ms max, which is V8's compile cache serving every sample after the first. The tell was the implausible row (0.00ms for 1.2MB) and the discipline was to check it rather than report around it. Corrected: vm.SourceTextModule in a fresh process per sample with ok/err reported per sample, so a throw cannot masquerade as a fast compile. Both runs' raw output is kept - the invalid one deliberately. 22.43ms for the store bundle looked like a measurement and was an error message with a stopwatch on it.
STILL OWED before a gate can be proposed: S1 real SW cold boot, S2 message dispatch distribution (p50 AND p99), S3 new-tab paint, S4/S5 hub and side-panel parse with ox5s's before/after as the calibration point, and a second load on everything above.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
ALL SIX SURFACES MEASURED (k3, 2026-09-18, continuing from qwen2's first numbers). Reports + raw logs: cap-evidence/perf-4ctv/{S1-REPORT,S2-REPORT,S3-REPORT,S4-S5-REPORT}.md and .log files. All two-load (M2), per-sample ok/err, fresh profiles, store build (2,998,629-byte SW), conditions recorded on every run.

S1 SW cold boot: launch→workerCreated 205.8→325.5ms; created→evalComplete 41.5→60.6ms (brackets qwen2's 42.61ms Node full-compile of the same bundle — cross-instrument agreement); SW-local eval 4.4→6.3ms (V8 lazy parse); launch→first-handled 476.6→776.1ms idle→load. Bytes ≈ 8-10% of boot; spin-up/registration dominates.
S2 dispatch (steady state, cheapest full route): p50 0.125-0.44ms, p99 4.8-6.7ms (event-loop contention, not bytes); deep tail WORSE idle (max 41-45ms) than loaded (7-9ms) — the cold-wake phenomenon at steady state, repeatable.
S3 NTP render: FCP 103.4→172.0ms; composer-ready 176.6→254.8ms (readiness gap is module work, stable ~58ms both loads).
S4/S5 ox5s calibration (both revisions measured): bytes 2.16MB→766KB (2.82x) and requests 74→1; win DCL −30.6/−68.4ms, readiness −20.2/−17.3ms (hub), −10–38ms (side panel). THE TELL: the DCL delta doubles under load — requests degrade under contention, bytes do not. Requests are the sensitive axis; bytes are a weak proxy for them.
S6 admission path (computed): +26,155 bytes ≈ +0.14–0.22ms of the boot component — below noise; consistent with qwen2's ≈0.4ms compile estimate.

GATE QUESTION ANSWERED: measurable surfaces are S1 boot ms and S3/S4 readiness ms; a user-visible gate would assert cold-boot p50 and composer-ready ms at stated loads (two-load rule, per-sample ok/err). The byte budget proxies ~40–60ms of fetch+parse+eval in a ~480–780ms boot (~15–20µs/KB at boot, zero at steady state). Nothing measured correlates user-visible cost with bundle bytes; ox5s's win was REQUESTS and parse surface, not bytes. Instruments are in cap-evidence/perf-4ctv/ and rerunnable (s1-cold-boot.ts, s2-dispatch.ts, s3-ntp-paint.ts).

title: test:changed cannot see source-inspecting tests — AST/source-scan guards never run in the changed-set gate (silent-green)
description: SYMPTOM (k3, vv98): hg03 registered the acp.journal route with green gates and a 9/9 browser acceptance; the census and route-modularization tests red only later on someone else's run. MECHANISM (coord): scripts/select-tests.mjs selects tests by walking the STATIC IMPORT GRAPH — and a test that READS source as data (AST census, source scans) has no import edge from the source file, so the selector never picks it. Nothing was careless: the selector's model is reachability and these tests are not reachable by that model. BIGGER THAN vv98: the fleet has spent all day adding exactly this kind of test — sw-dispatch-authority-census, sw-route-modularization, file-url-root-guard, the docs-process-truth scanner, every AST/source-property guard. As a class they are unselectable by test:changed — a SILENT-GREEN hazard: guards written to catch regressions do not run in the gate they were written for. ACCEPTANCE (per coord): (1) source-inspecting tests join the always-on set, with the rule stated: a test that reads tracked source as data must be always-on; (2) a self-checking audit that fails when a test file uses readTextFile/readFileSync on tracked source WITHOUT being in the always-on set — the convention becomes something the repo fails on, not a list that drifts.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan

title: Script sandbox: ambient egress is not confined to the host bridge (no connect-src/default-src in the sandbox CSP)
description:
FOUND BY: chrome-agent-platform-ovfm.4 (the Stage 4 KAT suite). Filed separately on purpose — that bead is the test suite, and a suite that quietly grows a denial-policy change stops being a suite. **Changing the sandbox CSP is a policy decision for Paul, not a lane's call.**

## The measurement (real browser, built extension, real Stage 3 path)
Harness + evidence: `cap-evidence/ovfm4-kat/` (`ovfm4-sandbox-egress-kat.ts`, 26 passed / 0 failed on a fresh build). Every arrival is asserted at an OWNED ENDPOINT that records what arrived; the script's own report is never the evidence.

| request from the sandbox | arrived at the endpoint? | what the wire showed |
|---|---|---|
| ambient `XMLHttpRequest` | **yes** | `Origin: null`; response unreadable without CORS |
| ambient `XMLHttpRequest` (endpoint sends `ACAO: *`) | **yes** | readable — readability is a separate property |
| ambient `WebSocket` | **yes** | `upgrade: websocket` |
| `navigator.sendBeacon` | **yes** | `Origin: null` |
| `new Image()` | **yes** | (no Origin header, normal for no-cors) |
| `EventSource` | **yes** | `Origin: null` |
| host-bridged `fetch` | **no** | refused: no approved run allow-list |
| host-bridged `fetch` to `http://169.254.169.254/…` | **no** | refused by URL validation |
| remote classic `<script src>` | **no** | **blocked by CSP** |
| host-bridged `fetch` inside an imported module | **no** | the bridge covers imported module code |

## The cause, in one sentence
The manifest's `sandbox` CSP declares `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' blob:; child-src 'self';` with **no `connect-src` and no `default-src`**, so CSP restricts scripts and child frames and leaves connect/beacon/image/ws unrestricted: **shadowing `window.fetch` is a rename of one entry point, not a policy.**

## What is NOT claimed
- Not that credentials leak: no cookie arrived on any request, but the endpoint is plain http on loopback where Chrome's SameSite rules make cookie propagation hard to stage, so credential transmission is **not demonstrated**, not disproven.
- Not that the sandbox is unconfined: the origin IS opaque (every ambient request carried `Origin: null`), and CSP DOES block remote scripts. The gap is specifically **outgoing reachability from an opaque origin**, which is real and useful to an attacker who only needs the request to arrive.

## Recommendation (Paul's decision)
1. Add `connect-src` (and a `default-src`) to the `sandbox` CSP, scoped to what the host bridge actually needs — the bridged `fetch` goes through the extension's own SW route, not through the sandbox's network stack, so this should be tight.
2. Keep the ambient-egress KAT as the acceptance: the six arrivals must become non-arrivals, and the two non-arrivals above must stay non-arrivals (so the change cannot pass by breaking the bridge or the module path).
3. If Paul prefers not to change the CSP, the honest alternative is to state in the design that the sandbox has ambient egress and that its confinement is the container, not the policy — the current design doc claims only the bridged fetch, which the measurement contradicts.

comments.text:
OPTIONS PAPER delivered (no policy change made): cap-evidence/journal-ahv/4h2x-options-paper.md. Measured on main 2cc62e68 with ovfm.4's egress KAT (server-side observing assertions), three variants:

BASELINE (CSP unchanged): exit 0, 22 PASS — all six ambient paths arrive (XHR, CORS-readable XHR, WebSocket, sendBeacon, image, EventSource); bridged fetch refused and never arrives; bridged fetch inside imported modules works.

VARIANT A (+ connect-src 'none'): XHR/WS/sendBeacon/EventSource BLOCKED; Image() STILL ARRIVES (img-src gap — measured, not spec-quoted); the bridge SURVIVES (module round-trip + imported-module bridge fetch pass).

VARIANT B (+ connect-src 'none'; img-src 'none'): all six ambient paths BLOCKED; bridge + imports + refusals PASS; zero ambient requests on the wire.

ANSWERS: (1) the bridge survives locked-down connect-src — measured; it is postMessage + loopback form-POST, not a connect-src path. (2) Two directives, not one: Image() is a resource load needing img-src. (3) Legitimate breakage: none measured — the designed capability (host-bridged fetch + log) and imports are unimpaired. (4) NOT fixed by B: form-navigation egress (sandbox has allow-forms; a frame form-GET to an external URL is not a connect-src/img-src path) — unmeasured, form-action 'none' is the candidate; the bridge itself is by-design; credentials remain undemonstrated either way.

RECOMMENDATION: Option B (two directives). If approved: ovfm.4's KAT assertions flip from arrives->must-not-arrive (ovfm.4's suite change), and the sibling sandbox page artifact-preview.html shares the manifest declaration (same CSP applies). Paul's answer is one word: approve B (with/without form-action) or reject.

title: Selecting Claude or Codex in the UI still starts the pi harness, and the failure names pi
description:
Found 2026-09-18 by Paul on macOS. Clicking Claude or Codex in the extension fails with 'Could not start pi: executable not found' — a harness he did not select.

ROOT CAUSE (from the code, scripts/acp-bridge.ts): the harness is fixed at BRIDGE-PROCESS level, not per session. args.harness defaults to 'pi' (line 21), HARNESS_ADAPTERS[harness] picks the adapter once (line 164), and childEnvForHarness/harnessCliWarning both key off that same process-level value. The service is installed with '--harness pi' (acp-service.mjs bridgeArgs), so the running bridge serves the pi adapter regardless of what the UI asks for. Two user-visible defects follow:
1. A per-session choice of claude-code or codex cannot take effect on a running bridge — the pi adapter starts instead, and pi has NO bundled fallback (HARNESS_CLI.pi), so it fails fatally when the binary is missing.
2. The error names the BRIDGE's harness ('pi') rather than the harness the user selected, so the message contradicts the click and points at the wrong remedy. For claude-code/codex this class was already softened in 95ve (bundledFallback => NOTE, not a fatal alarm) — the gap is that the selection never reaches that code.

ACCEPTANCE (either path is acceptable):
(a) The selection is honoured: clicking Claude or Codex starts that harness's adapter for that session (or reconfigures/restarts the bridge deliberately, with the reinstall surfaced as an action rather than a silent no-op); or
(b) The mismatch is made legible and non-misleading: the extension reads the bridge's harness from /health (which already reports 'Harness: pi, Adapter: pi-acp') and either disables or annotates the harnesses the running bridge cannot serve, offering the one-command fix — and in every case the failure text names the harness that was actually STARTED, not just the one requested.

EVIDENCE: Paul's error text naming /Users/paulkinlan/.local/bin/pi while he selected Claude/Codex; the doctor output showing 'Harness: pi, Adapter: pi-acp@0.0.33' on that machine; and acp-bridge.ts lines 21/164/106-122 for the process-level pinning.

NOT A CODE REGRESSION IN 95ve: 95ve wired the env-var handoff correctly (HARNESS_CLI/childEnvForHarness) and its verification stands — this is the layer above, where the harness is chosen.
close_reason: Closed

title: ACP continuity pin is load-sensitive and reds npm test
description:
WHAT: tests/acp-runner.test.ts -> "runAcpTaskTurn: turn 2 RESUMES the session (session/new once, session/load after)" reds in the 32-worker phase of `npm test` (observed 4x over two days: "exactly one session/new across two turns" sees 2), while passing 16/16 in isolation on the SAME tree. It is one of the flaky tests that reds a fleet-wide gate.

ROOT CAUSE (measured, not inferred): `deno test --parallel` runs every test FILE in ONE process, so Deno.env is process-global. acp-runner.test.ts set CAP_ACP_FIXTURE_LOG via Deno.env.set, and the bridge spawns the adapter with `env: {...Deno.env.toObject()}` — so a fixture adapter spawned by a CONCURRENTLY running file (tests/acp-end-to-end.test.ts, whose bridge sets the fixture cwd and prompt "fixture prompt") inherited this file's log path and appended ITS frames to this file's frame log. The count then sees two session/new even though the resume itself succeeded. Evidence: cap-evidence/acp-fixture-logs/frames-1789641840690-0.jsonl contains the foreign adapter's frames ({"cwd":"<durable>/acp-fixture"}, prompt "fixture prompt") alongside this test's own (cwd $HOME/journal, prompts "first"/"second"), and the resume in that run DID work (initialize + session/load + prompt "second" on the second connection) — so the "adapter spawn died" theory does not explain this instance. Process-env sharing across --parallel files reproduced directly (a file that Deno.env.set a value was observed by a sibling file mid-run).

SECOND DEFECT: the existing blunt "TWO attempts" retry can never succeed after a first failure, because the runner caches the session id in module state (threadSessions keyed acp:<harness>): the retry's FIRST turn resumes, so the log shows 0 session/new and the pin fails again for a reason that is not the property. A retry therefore needs a fresh conversation key.

FIX (deliverable):
1. createAcpServer(port, adapter, childEnv) — an explicit, additive per-server adapter-child env so per-test adapter knobs never travel through the shared process env (root cause).
2. tests/acp-runner.test.ts passes every CAP_ACP_FIXTURE_* knob through that seam (no Deno.env.set for fixture config anywhere in the file).
3. The resume pin keeps its frame-log observer and gains an evidence-gated retry: an attempt whose failure shows NO `session/load` frame reaching the adapter AND a transport failure (connection closed / adapter exited / cannot connect) is an environmental spawn death and may retry; a `session/load` frame that reached the adapter and was rejected/fell back, or a turn that completed without ever attempting a load, is a PRODUCT regression and fails immediately. Bounded attempts, fails closed, no skip.

ACCEPTANCE / FALSIFICATION:
- M1: make the runner never resume (acp-runner.js: disable the loadSession branch) -> the pin must FAIL, on the product verdict, not by exhausting retries. Report the run.
- M2: make the fixture die on the second connection (CAP_ACP_FIXTURE_DIE_ON_SPAWN=2 + a shared counter file, transient so exactly one spawn dies) -> the pin must NOT report a product failure; it retries and passes. Report the run.
- A shipped fault-injection test pins the environmental branch in every gate.
- Gates: npm run test:file -- tests/acp-runner.test.ts, npm run test:changed, npm test once, all green with numbers reported.

MUST NOT CHANGE: the assertion that two turns must ask a harness for session/new exactly once and session/load after, the frame-log observer, the host-default cwd pin, and the whole-connection-per-turn behaviour these frames prove. title: Permission prompt says 'approvals are available only in Settings' for an already-granted action
description:
Owner report (2026-09-12, live UI): 'Permission request — The agent wants to asset.update: a1d2dd17ff2fe8784672832c00c209b5. approvals are available only in Settings' — for an action whose permission was ALREADY granted, and with no way to approve inline.

Two defects in one flow: (1) an already-granted capability still raises a prompt/blocked state instead of proceeding; (2) when a decision really is needed, the surface sends the owner to Settings rather than rendering the decision card inline (the repo's own rule: request the permission on the user gesture, never just fail with 'permission required' — AGENTS.md 'Ask for permissions on need, never fail silently').

SEAMS: the approval path in extension/background/service-worker.js (the asset.update approval decision + its requirement key), the inline approval card components (appendApproval / permission-approval-card in extension/shared/components.js), and the composer/side-panel surfaces that already render approval cards for other actions.

REPRO: in the side panel (or hub), have an agent run asset.update with asset permissions already granted; observe the 'only in Settings' state instead of the action proceeding or an inline card.

DO NOT: widen any permission to make the prompt disappear — the fix is to recognise the existing grant and to render the decision inline.
acceptance_criteria: An approval the extension already holds never asks; when an approval IS needed, it can be answered inline in the surface that raised it (with the Settings route as a secondary link), and the decision is recorded against the exact action.

title: ACP: the adapter cannot see the harness CLI when the launcher's PATH is minimal
description:
Owner-reported (2026-09-12, his Mac): pi-acp returned 'Internal error: Could not start pi: executable not found (command: pi)' while 'pi is on the path' in his shell — an auto-started process gets a minimal environment, so ~/.local/bin (where pi lives) is invisible.

title: ACP interactive permission cards (Allow/Deny) instead of auto-grant
description:
Gap found in the ACP audit (chrome-agent-platform-iadt); docs/ACP-INTEGRATION-RESEARCH.md §5.2 documents both modes and §7 marks the interactive one not-implemented.

WHAT exists today: AcpClient._handleAgentRequest calls options.permissionHandler when provided, else falls back to the first /allow/-matching option and answers immediately. acp-runner.js passes no permissionHandler, so every request is auto-granted — the harness can run shell commands and write files with no user-visible gate.

CONSTITUTION NOTE: an auto-granted local harness executing with the user's full permissions is a security-relevant default; the card is the honest mode and the default should be reconsidered when this lands.

SEAMS: extension/lib/acp-client.js (_handleAgentRequest, AcpPermissionRequest typedef), extension/lib/acp-runner.js (options.permissionHandler not passed), the conversation component's permission UI used by in-browser runs (reuse it, do not hand-roll a second card).
acceptance_criteria: A session/request_permission renders an inline card listing the requested tool call and its options; the turn waits for Allow/Deny (no auto-answer); the chosen optionId is returned to the harness; a denied action reports honestly in the transcript. Auto-grant remains available as an explicit mode, never the silent default for an unattended window.

WHAT I FOUND — THE CHECK COULD NOT FAIL. cap-evidence/acp-browser-acceptance.ts's owner-gate legs never reached the gate: after the first send the NTP switches to the THREAD view, and the legs typed into the HUB composer (#composer #task-input), so no new permission request was ever made. The legs' checks were satisfied by the UNGATED first turn's card, which had already settled to 'denied' on the 120 s unattended timeout — the deny leg reported 'the card settles to denied' / 'the harness was told deny' / 'the transcript says denied' while the click never landed and could not have. Same class as 7poq's fixture: a check that satisfies itself without exercising the behaviour. The first run of the script as shipped: 26 passed / 3 failed, with the two click checks failing and the allow leg never reaching 'granted'.

FIX (cap-evidence/acp-browser-acceptance.ts): the legs drive the THREAD composer and re-commit the harness chip for THEIR turn; each leg requires a NEW card at its own index (a settled card from an earlier leg is not evidence), asserts the card is PENDING with BOTH controls, asserts the turn is BLOCKED on the owner (no harness answer before the decision), requires the CLICK to be what settles it (a non-settle is a FAILURE, the mirror coord asked for), then checks the harness's optionId and the transcript line.

RESULT — real browser, deterministic fixture, genuine CDP mouse events, product bytes untouched: 37 passed / 0 failed (exit 0). Log: cap-evidence/e24e-owner-gate-acceptance.txt; screenshots + acceptance.json in /home/paulkinlan/cap-evidence/cap-acp-browser-1789722805053.

title: ACP audit: gate honesty, session continuity, host-side defaults, bridge origin guard
description:

2. SESSION CONTINUITY: the runner cached sessions by threadId only; the pi surface and hub @pi delegations pass threadId=null, so every turn started a NEW pi session — the conversation never continued. Now keyed per thread, else per harness (acp:<harnessId>), proven live: a word planted in turn 1 was recalled in turn 2 after the bridge killed the adapter between turns (pi-acp's session/load restores pi's on-disk session).

4. BROKEN INSTRUCTIONS: the runner's error text said 'npm run acp:bridge' (the script did not exist) or 'node scripts/acp-bridge.ts' (a Deno script). The npm script exists now.
5. SECURITY: the bridge accepted ANY origin — a web page could drive the local harness (shell, files) over loopback. Web origins are refused (browsers always send Origin on WS upgrade), pinned by tests/acp-bridge-security.test.ts.
6. FOUR REPO GUARDS the overnight commit had broken and never run: harness-registry (scripts/acp-bridge.ts unregistered), machine-path-honesty (scripts/ home literal), evidence-durable (extension/lib home literal), changelog (no entry + version).

description:

- PID 333994, owner gemini: identical command, etime 1h33m35s, 0.0% CPU, do_epoll_wait.
Both cleared by coord with SIGTERM at 01:45 BST; both process trees exited; no Chrome owned by those runs (only the user's own Chrome present). A third instance (owner glm-flash-1, PID 533782) was started 01:44 and left running.

SUSPECTED MECHANISM (unproven — do not treat as established): the partitioner (scripts/test-partition.mjs) warns in its own SERIAL_REASONS that chrome-launch-lock, chrome-launch-lock-scope, chrome-slot-semaphore and chrome-slot-semaphore-honesty each mutate PROCESS-GLOBAL state (CAP_CHROME_LOCK_PATH / CAP_CHROME_SLOT_DIR) and race with other lock tests; and that -honesty additionally makes wall-clock queueing assertions. Running the whole serial set in ONE deno invocation puts every file in one process, so those globals are shared. The code (scripts/lib/chrome-launch.ts) says the canonical lock wait is bounded (CAP_CHROME_LOCK_WAIT_MS default 20 min, fails loudly) — the observed hangs were 1h33m and 2h51m, so either the bound does not cover the path that hung, or the wait is on a child process rather than the lock. NOT established: which of those.

COLLATERAL: /tmp accumulates cap-chrome-lock-test-*.lock files (13 present, 00:10-01:45) and /tmp/cap-chrome-slot-0.lock (00:10) — the lock tests take isolated scopes by design; they are not cleaned up.

ACCEPTANCE: identify the unbounded wait with evidence (lock vs child vs slot), make it bounded + loud like the canonical lock, ensure the serial phase cannot deadlock on process-global mutations or leaves no stale /tmp locks, and a regression test that reproduces the wedge (or a bounded failure) under the serial invocation. Related: j95l gate wedge (0% CPU 73 min), atve investigation.

title: [bug] Agent edit cannot be saved: named-agent.update missing from OWNER_DIRECT_ACTIONS
description:
When an owner edits an agent in the Hub/NTP agent config dialog and presses Save, the dialog fails to save and displays an error ('Save failed: This operation requires owner approval in Settings.').
Root cause: In extension/lib/owner-approval.js, named-agent.update is omitted from OWNER_DIRECT_ACTIONS.
While named-agent.set-schedule, named-agent.set-mcp-servers, and named-agent.delete are marked as OWNER_DIRECT_ACTIONS, named-agent.update is treated as an unapproved mutation.
Because Settings does not have an approval UI for named-agent.update, the owner cannot approve the edit and is forced to delete the agent.
Adding named-agent.update to OWNER_DIRECT_ACTIONS allows owner UI actions in extension documents (principal === 'extension' || principal === 'owner-options') to apply immediately, while keeping model-facing calls (principal === 'model') subject to owner approval cards.

title: Recursive GitHub skill and command discovery engine (Git Trees API + tree crawler)
description:
Implement recursive discovery of SKILL.md and commands/*.md in GitHub repositories at any depth.
Current implementation in extension/lib/skill-import.js only inspects the root or depth-1 child directories and halts at the first SKILL.md found.
Repositories like phuryn/pm-skills have 68 skills and 42 commands nested under category folders (e.g. pm-ai-shipping/skills/shipping-artifacts/SKILL.md, pm-ai-shipping/commands/ship-check.md) and define .claude-plugin/marketplace.json.
Use GitHub Git Trees API (https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{branch}?recursive=1) to retrieve the entire repo tree in a single API call, parse .claude-plugin/marketplace.json if present, locate all SKILL.md files and command .md files, and fall back to recursive contents API walk when trees API is unavailable.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Calling discoverRepoSkillsAndCommands('https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main') returns all 68 skills and 42 commands with their relative paths, category/plugin metadata, and download URLs.
2. Single-call Git Trees API is preferred to avoid GitHub Contents API rate limits.
3. Frontmatter of SKILL.md and commands/*.md is parsed (name, description, argument-hint).
4. Physical budgets and rate limit defenses are preserved.
5. Unit tests in tests/skill-discovery.test.ts verify tree parsing, nested discovery, and frontmatter extraction on fixtures.
close_reason: Landed on main @ 94a6f0b2 (v0.3.328). Implemented recursive GitHub skill and command discovery engine (discoverRepoSkillsAndCommands) using Git Trees API (?recursive=1) with bounded contents walk fallback, .claude-plugin/marketplace.json support, frontmatter parsing, and honest rate-limit propagation.
