Security model verified hard (Pro e384c626): zero broad injection, host-permission grant stays owner-gesture, transactional enroll/rollback intact.
- Acceptance: an owner can see which open pages are discoverable and enroll one with a single explicit gesture, without typing an origin; discovery no longer requires the origin to be enrolled first; an already-enrolled origin's content scripts are re-registered on service-worker/browser boot so it does not go silent after a restart; no broad injection is introduced and the host-permission grant stays behind an owner gesture with transactional enroll/rollback intact
- Review: PASS (Pro e384c626), 1595/1595, manifest untouched.
- Gates: independent security review (Pro `e384c626`) confirming zero broad injection, owner-gesture host-permission grant and intact transactional enroll/rollback; 1595/1595 unit; manifest unchanged

title: [CAP-FB-20260827-DIALOG-CONSOLIDATION-01] Five dialog implementations, three hand-rolled
description:
## [CAP-FB-20260827-DIALOG-CONSOLIDATION-01] Five dialog implementations, three hand-rolled
- Feedback: 2026-08-27 — product owner: "There's lots of issues with dialogs"
- Updated: 2026-08-27 23:30 UTC
- Status: IN_REVIEW
- Priority: P1
- Owner: coordinator session
- Workspace: main
- Branch: main
- Base: `139b6f92`
- Candidate: —
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: every modal in the extension is raised through the shared component vocabulary — `<agent-dialog>` for a content dialog, `confirmActionDialog` for a decision — with no hand-rolled `document.createElement("dialog")` left outside `extension/shared/components.js`. Focus trap, Escape, backdrop light-dismiss, focus return, the destructive default-focus rule, scrollable overflow and theme/RTL/narrow behaviour are then identical everywhere by construction. Each converted site keeps its exact current semantics — in particular the provider-approval dialog must still be able only to DENY on dismissal, never approve
- Review: author review 2026-08-29 with the falsification gates cleared (see History); a11y behaviours driven in a real loaded extension by `scripts/kat-dialog-consolidation.ts` rather than asserted from source
- Gates: full unit suite; Chrome journeys green; gallery drift check green; the impeccable design pass
- Blockers: —
- Next: owner review of the three converted surfaces in the product. The remaining consolidation work — the ~30 other scripts and any future modal — is now prevented by construction rather than by convention, since there is one confirm and one shell
- Recover: `git grep -n 'createElement("dialog")' -- extension/`
- History:
  - 2026-08-29 — **all three hand-rolled dialogs converted; `createElement("dialog")` now appears exactly once in the extension, inside the shared component itself.** (1) `extension/artifacts/index.js` artifact delete → `confirmActionDialog`, gaining backdrop light-dismiss, an `aria-label` and a settled guard it did not have; its 13 lines of bespoke `.delete-dialog` CSS are deleted. (2) `confirmAgentProviderMutation` → the shared confirm. **This one carried a security property the shared confirm lacked** — approve only on a click that is `isTrusted` AND has active user activation — so rather than keep the duplicate for it, the property moved INTO the shared component as `requireGenuineGesture`, alongside `returnFocusTo` and `note`. Every future approval now gets it by construction instead of by remembering to re-implement it. (3) `editRecipePrompt` → `<agent-dialog>`, the content shell; it gains a close button and backdrop dismissal it never had, and its bespoke panel/backdrop CSS is replaced by the shell's. **Evidence, driven in a real loaded extension (`scripts/kat-dialog-consolidation.ts`, 18/18):** a destructive confirm focuses Cancel; a backdrop click resolves false and removes the node; a non-destructive confirm focuses the confirm control; **an untrusted scripted click cannot approve** and the refusal is explained in the dialog; Escape denies; the shell is announced by its title and its body scrolls on overflow. That last group is why this is a KAT and not only a unit test — a DOM shim cannot tell you whether `event.isTrusted` gating actually holds. **Falsification:** `tests/provider-options-approval.test.ts` pinned the OLD implementation's source lines and had to be rewritten; it now pins the property across BOTH halves (the call site must ASK for the check, the component must IMPLEMENT it and gate the true result on it), because asserting only one half would let the flag become a no-op or let the call site quietly stop passing it. Four deliberate regressions — call site drops the flag, component drops the trusted-click check, the guard warns without refusing, and the hand-rolled duplicate returns — each drove it red before being reverted. **Gates:** build clean; unit **2004 pass / 0 fail**; Chrome journeys **127/127**; gallery, vocabulary and tracker schema green.
  - 2026-08-27 23:30 UTC — captured by source audit. **Five dialog implementations ship.** Two are the intended shared ones in `extension/shared/components.js`: `<agent-dialog>` (the content-dialog shell) and `confirmActionDialog` (the promise-based confirm). Three are hand-rolled duplicates outside the component system: `extension/artifacts/index.js:83` (artifact delete), `extension/options/options.js:1236` (`confirmAgentProviderMutation`), and `extension/options/options.js:1555` (`editRecipePrompt`). This is precisely the failure mode the owner already named as a project rule — "never hand-roll a one-off version of an existing component (the blank-toggle + menu bugs came from hand-rolled duplicates)" — and it is the most likely explanation for dialogs behaving inconsistently: each of the five owns its own focus, dismiss, overflow and sizing behaviour, so a fix to one does not reach the others.
  - 2026-08-27 23:30 UTC — **good news worth recording:** `window.confirm` / `window.alert` / `window.prompt` are already fully eliminated from the extension; the only remaining occurrence is the explanatory comment above `confirmActionDialog`. `CAP-FB-20260823-DIALOG-CONFIRM-MODERNIZATION-01` is therefore substantially further along than its OPEN status suggests — what is left of that task is this consolidation.

description:
## [CAP-FB-20260829-AGENT-BOARD-01] The shared jobs board: agents post and claim work
- Feedback: 2026-08-29 — owner voice note: "agents should be able to ask other agents for work… the chaos extension had a shared message board and a shared jobs board"
- Updated: 2026-08-29 UTC
- Status: DONE
- Priority: P1
- Owner: coordinator session
- Workspace: worker lane
- Branch: cap-agent-board
- Base: `c6406cc7`
- Candidate: `cdb8b491` (r5) — landed as merge `54d70a9b`
- Shipping: 0.2.400
- Acceptance: six management tools, claim lease/expiry, blockedBy DAG, delivery to poster thread, Tasks sidebar Board section
- Review: independent reviewer PASS (round 6); six rounds closed data-integrity findings (fold divergence, forgeable keys, destructive reads, eviction, admission reserve, claim churn, drain kick)
- Gates: suite 2358/0 at merge, board KAT 22/22, build green
- Blockers: none
- Next: idle-agent wake (deferred) — the per-edge deny layer LANDED 2026-08-30 (owner Settings UI, fail-closed guards, corrupt-store refusal)
- Recover: revert merge `54d70a9b`
- What it is: the async/broadcast complement to `delegate_to_agent`. A hub-level
  event-sourced board (jobs + messages logs in the master memory tier) where any
  named agent or the hub posts work, and any capable agent claims it (atomic
  claim + 5-minute lease + heartbeat, the scheduler's exact constants). Tools:
  board_post_job / board_claim_job / board_complete_job / board_send_message /
  board_list / board_read. Results ride back on the job record; the Tasks
  sidebar gains a "Board" grouping (open jobs + latest messages, bounded,
  textContent-only). Guards are pure functions in `extension/lib/agent-board.js`
  mirroring `agent-delegation.js`; caller identity comes from the route context
  (never model args).
- Permission model (owner decision 2026-08-29; deny layer landed 2026-08-30):
  default-open among named agents + the hub, plus owner-controlled per-edge
  DENY rules (Settings → Board permissions; owner-options principal only;
  fail-closed on malformed rules and corrupt store; rules load fresh inside
  each locked post/claim).
- DEFERRED (planned extensions): automatic wake of idle agents on post
  (scheduler/alarm machinery — v1 wakes live surfaces via broadcastProgress);
  bidding/auctions; cross-device boards; A2A wire-protocol interop.
- History:
  - 2026-08-29 — lane built: board lib + SW routes + 6 management tools +
    capability/replay classifications + Tasks-sidebar grouping; 20 unit tests +
    12-check browser KAT (screenshot evidence) green; suite 2266/0.
  - 2026-08-29 — review round 1 REVISE (6×P1 + 3×P2) fixed: board log keys
    reserved from the model's memory_set/memory_get/keys (memory.js
    MASTER_RESERVED_KEYS + hidden namespace; the store uses setTrusted/
    getStrict); event-time lease expiry in the fold (expired claims are
    reclaimable); pruning preserves settled jobs an open job still depends
    on; both logs byte-bounded (192 KiB < the 256 KiB per-value cap) with
    superseded-heartbeat compaction + a fail-closed board-full post gate;
    stale model contexts denied (never hub-escalated); settlements commit
    the result to the poster's thread through the durable thread-commit seam
    (idempotent by board:<jobId>); visible row metadata (never title-only);
    the browser KAT now drives a REAL named-agent claim→complete via the
    @demo-board demo-model marker + asserts live UI refresh; heartbeat
    parity pinned. 31 unit tests + 22-check KAT green; suite 2277/0.
  - 2026-08-29 — review round 2 REVISE (3×P1) fixed: failed/malformed log
    reads propagate instead of becoming destructive empty-log writes (only a
    successful null read means absent; routes surface a structured
    board-store-error); byte/count eviction now leaves compact settled
    TOMBSTONES (identity + outcome + truncated result + delivery state) so
    acknowledged settlements stay retry-idempotent (alreadySettled) and
    readable, with full records capped separately from tombstones;
    poster-thread delivery is durable — the pending delivery persists WITH
    the settle event, the settle ACK waits on the idempotent
    board:<jobId> thread commit, and a startup drain plus the
    repeated-settle path re-attempt delivery. 37 unit tests + 22-check KAT
    green; suite 2283/0.

Cherry-picked onto current `main` (the tracker row and CHANGELOG conflicted and were resolved keeping both lanes' content). **My own falsification, not the implementer's:** adding `--remote-debugging-port=9351` to `kat-usage-viz.ts` drove the gate RED (4 pass / 1 fail); removing it returned to green — so the gate fails for the right reason. A `grep` for a fixed port anywhere under `scripts/` now returns nothing outside the launcher. Gates at the merge tip: build clean, unit **2004 pass / 0 fail**, Chrome journeys **127/127**, gallery + tracker schema green. **One correction applied on merge:** the second test was named "only the shared launcher writes the debugging-port flag" but asserted merely that the launcher is *among* the writers — roughly thirty other scripts spawn Chrome themselves with the safe `=0` form. Renamed to "the shared launcher owns the debugging-port flag" and documented the scope in the test, because a test that claims more than it checks is the same defect class this entry exists to fix. The safety property (no script may name a port) is enforced by the first test and is unaffected. Migrating the remaining ~30 scripts onto `launchChrome()` is a separate cleanup, not a defect.
  - 2026-08-29 — **converted, falsified and gated.** Twelve harnesses now launch through one shared `scripts/lib/chrome-launch.ts`; `launchChrome()` passes `--remote-debugging-port=0` and reads the DevTools endpoint out of its OWN child's stderr, so the endpoint provably belongs to this process and there is no probe to race. The port-0 form was used everywhere — no harness needed the weaker probe-then-bind fallback — and the two scripts that already carried private copies of that helper (`kat-noun-discipline`, `kat-bgagent-delete`) were folded onto the shared launcher too, leaving one spawn path instead of nine fixed ports and two copies. FALSIFICATION: a decoy browser was started holding 9351 (the port `kat-usage-viz` hard-coded) running a deliberately altered copy of the extension; the PRE-CHANGE harness, pointed at the real tree, reported `FAIL: cost card is labelled an estimate — "costs are DECOY approximations (this tree is NOT under test)"` — a string that exists only in the decoy — proving it drove a browser it did not launch; the converted harness, with that same decoy still holding the port, passed 13/13 against the real tree. CONCURRENCY: `kat-usage-viz` + `kat-ux-lows` (both 9351) run together — before, one lane hung to a 300 s timeout when the other killed the browser they were sharing; after, both finish with their solo results. Individually every harness matches its pre-change tally: back-stack 6/0, dark-scheme 32/3, narrow-toggle 20/0, usage-viz 13/0, ux-lows 9/1, axe-audit 7/0, providers-tabs 19/0, agent-templates 13/0, composer-grow 11/0, noun-discipline 14/0, bgagent-delete 11/0 (the 3 dark-scheme and 1 ux-lows failures are pre-existing contrast/landmark findings, unchanged by this work); `kat-failed-runs` went from hanging for the full 300 s timeout against a live zombie on 9357 to 7/0 in 10 s. TWO THINGS FOUND THAT THE REPORT DID NOT DESCRIBE: the slow port poll was also masking a startup race — reading the endpoint off stderr is fast enough that MV3 has not registered its service worker yet, so eight harnesses gained an explicit bounded `waitForServiceWorker()` instead of depending on how long a probe happened to take; and `kat-bgagent-delete`'s own helper called `Deno.listen` outside its `try`, so a taken port threw out of the function rather than moving on to the next. A new gate, `tests/harness-debug-port.test.ts`, fails on any fixed debugging port anywhere in `scripts/` and on a launcher that would accept a caller-chosen one; it was observed RED with a port reintroduced into `kat-usage-viz` and GREEN with it removed.
  - 2026-08-29 — measured, then corrected after the reporting lane pointed out the failure mode is worse than "a flake". **A fixed-port harness does not merely hang or error — it attaches to another lane's browser and reports confident PASS/FAIL results about an extension it is not testing.** The reporting run produced 7 such results. That means a fixed-port harness can go **green against the wrong tree**, which is worse than a red suite, because the output reads as evidence. Eleven scripts name a port; two of them (`kat-bgagent-delete` on `cbf89c33`, `kat-noun-discipline`) already probe for a free one, leaving **nine hard-coded**. Four ports are each claimed by two of those nine: 9347 (`kat-narrow-toggle`, `kat-dark-scheme`), 9351 (`kat-usage-viz`, `kat-ux-lows`), 9353 (`kat-providers-tabs`, `axe-audit`), 9359 (`kat-agent-templates`, `kat-composer-grow`); `kat-failed-runs` holds 9357, the port `kat-bgagent-delete` starts probing from. 28 other scripts already launch with `--remote-debugging-port=0` and read the real port off the `DevTools listening` line, and `scripts/kat-noun-discipline.ts` carries a reusable `freePort()` (probe `/json/version`, then bind-test) — so both the pattern and a helper are already in-repo.

## [CAP-FB-20260828-ARTIFACT-LIBRARY-CAPACITY-01] The library still evicts the owner's oldest artifact silently
- Feedback: 2026-08-28 — found while fixing `CAP-FB-20260828-ARTIFACT-DURABILITY-01`; same bug class, deliberately not folded into that fix
- Updated: 2026-08-28 04:30 UTC
- Status: OPEN
- Priority: P1
- Owner: unassigned
- Workspace: none
- Branch: none
- Base: `4ed8cf8a`
- Candidate: —
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: the artifact library never silently discards the owner's work. When the index reaches its bound the owner is told and given a choice — the create fails honestly, or old artifacts are offered for review — rather than the oldest row being dropped inside a write it did not ask for. Whatever the policy, a test proves an artifact cannot leave the library without either an explicit `asset.delete` or an owner-visible decision
- Review: fresh-session review; falsification — the test must be shown failing against a build that still evicts silently
- Gates: unit suite; Chrome journeys green; `npm run test:opfs`
- Blockers: needs an owner decision — refusing a create fails a task mid-run, while evicting loses work silently. Both are bad in different ways and it is a product call, not an engineering one
- Next: put the two options to the owner with the real numbers (the bound is now ~15,000 rows) before building either
- Recover: `git grep -n "maxIndexBytes" -- extension/lib/artifacts.js`
- History:
  - 2026-08-28 04:30 UTC — the index carries a byte bound and, when a create would exceed it, drops the OLDEST rows (`idx = idx.slice(1)`) and records eviction obligations to clean their bodies. For a library whose stated purpose is being "the central source of all the information that has been created by the worker", silently discarding the oldest thing the person made is the wrong terminal behaviour — it is the same class as the bug just fixed, reached by a different route. The durability fix raised the bound from 128 KiB to 2 MiB (~940 rows to ~15,000) because the bound had been PER ORIGIN and became shared, which would otherwise have been a capacity regression. That defers the problem by roughly an order of magnitude; it does not fix it, and it is recorded here rather than left implied.

design:
## Design (2026-09-02, cap-beads-4dg increment): in-context provider host-access grant card

Scope: the last remaining Settings-redirect dead-end in the permission UX. Every
browser-tool denial already renders one in-context `<permission-approval-card>`
(Allow / Not now) — but when the configured NETWORK provider's exact origin is
not granted, the conversation preflight (extension/shared/conversation.js
runConversationTurn, "provider.permission-summary" check) appends a terminal
error reading "open Settings → Providers and approve that exact origin" and the
turn ends. The card UX directive: when an agent needs a permission, show an
in-context card, not a Settings redirect, with a clear grant/deny choice.

Change:
- On preflight ungranted-origin: do NOT return a dead-end error. Render ONE
  in-context permission card via the existing maybeRenderApproval machinery
  with requirement `{ reason: "connect to <host> (the provider that runs this
  task)", hostOrigins: [exact origin] }` (hostOrigins = the read-page-host-grant
  shape: Allow requests `<origin>/*` through chrome.permissions.request from
  the owner's genuine card click; the same request Settings' Use button makes).
- Allow (grant succeeds) → the run starts (executeTurn) — the SW run gate then
  passes; no Settings trip. Not now → honest terminal denial bubble: "Network
  access to <host> was not granted — you declined. The run did not start."
- Grant refused by Chrome → card shows the error and stays pending (Try again),
  matching the live-card contract; nothing is granted silently.
- Config problems (missing/invalid base URL, local-provider checks) are
  UNCHANGED — Settings remains the right surface for a configuration edit; this
  increment covers only the permission ask.

Mechanics (conversation.js only):
- runConversationTurn gains a pre-run pause state between the preflight and the
  first executeTurn: maybeRenderApproval is called with two new internal
  options (preRun: skips the legacy turn-retry flag, settle: an entry resolver)
  so the outer flow awaits the card decision deterministically — no polling,
  no double-run (the legacy approvalRetryRequested path would otherwise start a
  second attempt after a granted pre-run card).
- The user's own message bubble renders first (today the dead-end leaves the
  conversation without it).

Why hostOrigins: provider network access IS Chrome site access for one exact
origin (`<origin>/*`). The card already renders "Access this site: <origin>",
the exact-scope request, the "Chrome will ask you to confirm" note, and
granted/denied/error states. Reuse beats a new card type.

Not in scope (later increments of the bead): durable pending inbox for
background/scheduled runs with no open surface; multi-waiter ordering on one
browser-global permission; Settings decision history; in-run provider-access
revocation recovery (post-error) — the mid-run path still ends honestly and
points at Settings for the re-grant.

Tests: unit test driving runConversationTurn with a stubbed
provider.permission-summary (ungranted origin) + fake DOM container asserting:
(1) no Settings-redirect error is appended, one permission card entry is
created, status waiting-for-permission; (2) Allow → chrome.permissions.request
carries exactly the provider's `<origin>/*` and agent.run then executes exactly
once; (3) Not now → honest declined error, agent.run never dispatched, nothing
granted.

comments.text:
DESIGN (cap-beads-lj7 lane) — Directory tool explorer + enrollment policy, posted before implementation.

RESEARCHED DECISION (enrollment vs per-tool/invocation approval; resolves the bead blocker):
- Enrollment (owner gesture that makes a site a Site Agent) remains the coarse ALLOW and the consent for that origin's tools as a class (WEBMCP-AUTOAPPROVE-01 stands — no per-tool approval UI dead-ends).
- Per-tool invocation consent exists ONLY as the per-site "ask" policy state, paid per call through the SAME in-run owner-approval card machinery the destructive/cookie classes use (requireOwnerApproval, CAP-FB-20260830-DESTRUCTIVE-ACTION-POLICY-01). Unattended/scoped runs without a conversation fail closed (never auto-run).
- Directory (owner surface) always shows truthful per-tool provenance for review; the AGENT toolset is where deny excludes tools.

POLICY MODEL — per-site, stored in the enrollment registry entry (cap:enrollment, atomic under the existing global enrollment lock, generation bumped on change so in-flight catalogs revoke):
1. allow (default) — tools flow today unchanged (enrollment = consent).
2. deny — the site's tools are EXCLUDED from every agent toolset (readSiteLazySources returns no records — the falsification gate) and every invocation path fails closed with a named reason (authorization-guard conjunct + invokeSiteTool early reject).
3. ask — tools stay discoverable; every invocation pays an in-conversation owner card (Allow once / Deny) via a new extension-only approval action webmcp.use-tool, gated by the run-bound model dispatcher threaded into the WebMCP dispatch closure; absent a card channel the call fails closed honestly.

EXPLORER UX (extension/directory):
- Per-site groups keep bounded tool cards (name, description, input-schema summary, source chip) and gain page provenance (declaring page URL) on the card + origin in the heading.
- Each site group header gains the enrollment-policy control: Allow / Ask before use / Blocked, exactly labelled to the site; Blocked sections state the site's tools are not available to agents; cards carry the policy state so a blocked/"ask" badge can never detach from the tool (containment + exact AX labels per the acceptance).

TESTS (falsification-gated): enroll + declare tools → set deny → build the agent toolset exactly as readSiteLazySources does → the blocked site's tool MUST NOT appear and its invocation MUST fail closed with the named reason; allow default regression (tool present + dispatches); ask gate: dispatch consults the owner gate (approved → runs, denied → refused); registry unit tests (default allow, set/get, generation bump).

title: CDP evaluate helpers still swallow page-side exceptions in 34 scripts (49 sites); extract one shared typed helper instead of hand-copying the guard
description:
Measured during the independent review of chrome-agent-platform-0lb4 (2026-09-25). 0lb4's stated scope is instance 3 (chrome-journeys' evalIn) plus sibling drivers, and it delivers that - so this is a follow-up, not a gap in that bead.

THE MEASURED RESIDUAL. 34 files under scripts/ contain a Runtime.evaluate whose value is read back, and NO exceptionDetails check: 49 value-reading sites in total. Counted by a per-file sweep (grep for Runtime.evaluate, exclude files mentioning exceptionDetails, then require >=1 value-read of result?.value / result.result.value), not estimated.

Gate-relevant non-KAT drivers: scripts/security-suite.ts (2, detailed in chrome-agent-platform-4s4j), scripts/verify-script-run.ts (5), scripts/axe-audit.ts (3), scripts/validate-package-load.ts (2), scripts/sidepanel-companion-journey.ts (1), scripts/p0-repro.ts (1), scripts/screenshot-vision-evidence.ts (1), scripts/agent-role-preview.ts (1), scripts/data-memory-clear.ts (1). The remaining ~25 are kat-*.ts evidence drivers.

WHY IT IS THE SAME DEFECT, NOT A Style NIT. The mechanism 0lb4 documents: a harness helper wraps Runtime.evaluate, returns the value, never inspects exceptionDetails, so a page-side throw becomes undefined and the CONSUMER reports a product failure. Three instances of that conversion are already on the record: 4vfj (a11y-audit, four combobox checks red on main), cwy2 (sidebar-parity, 20 checks skipped), and the security gate's composer:false (0lb4's own text). Each new driver that hand-rolls its own eval is another copy of the same landmine, and 0lb4 added six more hand-written guards rather than one shared one.

STRUCTURAL POINT. The repo rule is "Real libraries, not patterns" and "when you change one subsystem, CHECK + UPDATE every related part". The guard is now written out in six places with TWO different spellings, because the two transports differ: some harnesses resolve the whole CDP wire message (chrome-journeys resolve(d) -> r.result.exceptionDetails) and some resolve the unwrapped method result (capability-lifecycle resolve(m.result), perf-leak-trace explicit .result unwrap -> r.exceptionDetails). Both are correct as written - I verified all six per-file - but the difference is invisible to a reader, so the next copy will be wrong in a way that no test notices. The source pins added in 0lb4 are regex-on-text and CANNOT distinguish the live path from the dead one.

ACCEPTANCE. (1) ONE typed, importable helper - e.g. scripts/lib/cdp-eval.ts alongside quiet-window.ts and chrome-launch.ts - owning the evaluate-plus-exception-surface decision, exposing the transport shape explicitly (wire-envelope mode and method-result mode) so a caller picks the right one rather than pasting the wrong spelling; (2) the harnesses above migrated to it, each migration proven by a falsification test that goes red when the guard is removed - not by a source regex; (3) where a driver genuinely wants tolerance, the call site carries a comment saying why and returns a NAMED diagnostic instead of undefined/false (0lb4 FIX SHAPE items 3 and 4); (4) a guard that fails when a new scripts/*.ts calls Runtime.evaluate and reads a value without going through the helper - so the count cannot silently regrow; (5) retire 0lb4's source-pin regexes once behaviour tests cover each shape, keeping the behavioral tests.

DEPENDS ON / RELATES TO. 4s4j (the live security-suite instance, which this subsumes but should not block, being P2 and security-relevant). Also relevant to chrome-agent-platform-qptq, whose finding is that this tree's CDP harness surface is under-measured in other ways.

DO NOT. Do not do this as a sweeping formatting change, and do not weaken any existing assertion to make a migration pass. Land per-file with its own proof.

title: [owner decision] Does the per-agent SharedWorker decision stand, or is the unused worker path retired? mxu5 waits on the answer
description:
Owner decision, not implementation work. Same rule as u51: an agent may prepare the options; it may not choose.

## The question
The owner chose per-agent SharedWorkers for agent runs, and Phases 1-4 shipped on 2026-08-27 (docs/AGENT-EXECUTION-ARCHITECTURE.md:3 and :73; §6 is headed "DECIDED: shared workers"). On 2026-08-30 the reanalysis found that nothing calls the worker (perf lane finding 7), and vuxz proposed reversing the decision. The owner's answer to that proposal is not recorded. Does the per-agent SharedWorker decision stand (option A: wire the worker path), or is it reversed (option B: retire it)?

## How the answer went missing
- vuxz (CAP-FB-20260830-DEAD-CODE-CUT-01), step 6, asked for the SharedWorker decision to be recorded before anything was cut. Its 2026-09-02 History entry in the retired TASKS.md (as of ac3ba3c16) reads: "the SharedWorker decision — proposal stands as option B (retire `workers/agent-worker.js`, `agent-worker-host.js`, the `agent-worker` routes and `reconcileAgentWorkers`, rewrite `docs/AGENT-EXECUTION-ARCHITECTURE.md` to say the loop runs in the service worker) but it is the owner's call and all of that code is reached today, so nothing was touched."
- ac3ba3c16 then marked vuxz's TASKS.md entry DONE and replaced "Next: ... the owner records the SharedWorker decision" with "Next: none". Its Blockers line still reads: "The SharedWorker decision (option A wire / option B remove) is the owner's; the code is unchanged either way until it is recorded here." The tracker that line names is retired.
- No answer turned up where I searched: docs/, PLAN.md, CHANGELOG.md, REVIEW-*.md and PRODUCT.md on origin/main, plus a beads search for "SharedWorker" and "shared worker". The beads search found only vuxz and wr3, and wr3 (2026-08-26) predates the proposal. docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md has no entry for it (Q21 covers worker-run history only). docs/AGENT-WORKER-PHASE4.md still presents A and B as open, and docs/RISK-REGISTER.md:68, written on 2026-09-11 (706c76da2), after the proposal, still asks when alarms will move to SharedWorkers.

## Why mxu5 waits on it
mxu5 (flip handleAlarm to the worker) was filed by a docs sweep on 2026-09-02 from the Phase 4 sentence "The reroute is the NEXT increment". That sentence was written on 2026-08-27 (a7612031e), before the reversal was proposed. Under A, mxu5 is the next step; under B, it is abandoned. It moves runTask's fence, journal and attribution, which docs/AGENT-WORKER-PHASE4.md warns is risky to move. So it is held until this is answered, and closing this bead releases it.

## Facts at origin/main@a12f887c (checked 2026-09-25)
- Still present: extension/workers/agent-worker.js (12,201 B source), extension/lib/agent-worker-host.js (8,336 B), extension/background/routes/agent-worker.js (28,734 B; the SW imports it through routes/index.js:13), and the boot call to reconcileAgentWorkers (service-worker.js:11210).
- No product caller: a grep over extension/ (dist excluded) finds no page or service-worker path that sends agent-worker.ensure, .run or .dispatch. Outside the route file, only .tool (sent by the worker itself) and .steer (service-worker.js:9131) appear. Scheduled runs still go through runTask in the SW (docs/AGENT-WORKER-PHASE4.md).
- reconcileAgentWorkers returns at once when the alive-set is empty, and only otherwise ensures the offscreen document. docs/AGENT-EXECUTION-ARCHITECTURE.md:110 says agent-worker.ensure writes that set, and nothing calls ensure.
- docs/AGENT-EXECUTION-ARCHITECTURE.md:3 still says Phases 1-4 are "all implemented and shipped", including "the UI port client with live redacted progress", which 6d4dee9dc deleted.
- Built worker bundle: 1,125,413 B in this tree's store build (dist-versions/<v>/workers/agent-worker.js). vuxz's 2 MB figure dates from 2026-08-30.
- Service-worker budget: the store SW bundle is 2,982,918 B against the unchanged 3,000,000 B budget, leaving 17,082 B (same build). vl6c's harness candidate measured 3,003,397 B on 2026-09-21. How many bytes option B would free is NOT measured.
- Worker runs are "stateless single-shot executions by design" (OPEN-QUESTIONS Q21).

## Option A: the decision stands, wire it
Bring agent-worker-client.js back from history (deleted in 6d4dee9dc) so a surface holds a live port to its agent, as the decision intended (AGENT-EXECUTION-ARCHITECTURE.md:73). Then do mxu5: move runTask's fence, journal and attribution into SW-side callbacks, and point handleAlarm at agent-worker.dispatch. Then Q21: pass thread history into agent-worker.run. In the architecture doc's words, A would deliver "fault + memory isolation (one crashed/leaky agent no longer kills the router + every other agent), plus low-latency client streams" (AGENT-EXECUTION-ARCHITECTURE.md:5). Today no run gets that isolation, because nothing dispatches to the worker.

## Option B: reverse it and retire the worker path (vuxz's proposal)
Delete workers/agent-worker.js, lib/agent-worker-host.js, routes/agent-worker.js, reconcileAgentWorkers and the build entry (build.mjs:505-515). Rewrite docs/AGENT-EXECUTION-ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/AGENT-WORKER-PHASE4.md to say the loop runs in the SW. Close mxu5 ABANDONED citing this bead, and close Q21 as moot. Before deleting, check what service-worker.js:9131 routes through handlers["agent-worker.steer"]; steering of SW runs must keep working. B drops the 1,125,413 B worker bundle and the routes whose entry points have no caller, gives back some SW budget (amount unmeasured), and makes the architecture docs match what runs. It gives up the isolation that A would deliver.

## Done when
The answer and its reason are recorded in docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md; docs/AGENT-WORKER-PHASE4.md, the status line of docs/AGENT-EXECUTION-ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/RISK-REGISTER.md:68 are updated to match; and in the same change mxu5 is either released (A) or closed ABANDONED (B).

title: Harness browser-tool calls cannot raise an owner approval card, so the six destructive tools are permitted but unusable
description:
FOUND while landing chrome-agent-platform-wfo5 (a12f887c, v0.3.487), and deliberately NOT resolved there: wfo5 made all 135 browser tools callable by a harness, but six of them can only ever answer with a refusal.

MEASURED, two steps:
  1. OWNER_DIRECT_ACTIONS (extension/lib/owner-approval.js) does NOT contain browser.close-foreign-tab, browser.close-window, browser.wipe, browser.remove-bookmark, browser.set-cookie or browser.remove-cookie. Verified by importing the module and asking the Set directly, not by grepping the file (a grep counts occurrences anywhere, which is not membership).
  2. A harness call arrives at browser.callTool with principal 'extension', not 'model'. So requireOwnerApproval (service-worker.js:4916) skips the owner-direct shortcut AND skips the in-conversation approval-card branch, which is gated on context?.principal === 'model', and falls to its tail: { ok: false, error: 'This operation requires owner approval in Settings.' }

CONFIRMED IN A REAL BROWSER, not only in unit tests: the extended canonical drive (scripts/kat-browser-tool-proxy.ts, run 2 on b6f9b457, 22/22) has the harness call close_tab on a tab it did not open. The reply is a refusal AND chrome.tabs.get shows the tab still open afterwards.

WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT STATE TODAY, so nobody 'fixes' it by deleting the refusal: before wfo5, runBrowserToolCall called browserToolset() with no gates, and requireDestructiveApproval returns { ok: true } when destructiveActionGate is null. Simply widening the allow-list would have let these six mutate the owner's browser with NO card at all. The refusal is the safe end of that trade and is pinned by tests/browser-tool-proxy.test.ts ('a gated tool REFUSES rather than mutates').

WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING: a harness call has no originating conversation, so there is no progress channel on which to publish a card and no run execution id to bind an approval to. The model path has both. So this is not a one-line permission edit — it needs a decision about WHERE an approval card for an external-agent action appears and WHAT it is bound to.

THE DECISION IS THE OWNER'S, not an implementer's. Three shapes, none chosen:
  (a) Leave it. External agents get read + non-destructive write; destructive actions stay owner-only. Cheapest, and honest — but Paul's wfo5 directive was 'get all the other browser tools available', and six are not.
  (b) Bind the harness's ACP session to a conversation surface so the existing in-context card mechanism works, with the approval bound to that session rather than a model run.
  (c) A Settings-side pending queue the owner resolves out of band. Note the existing route only LISTS pending approvals (ownerApprovalRows); there is no resolve route for a ui: row, so this is more work than it looks.

ACCEPTANCE (whichever shape is chosen): the drive in scripts/kat-browser-tool-proxy.ts must show a harness-initiated destructive action either (i) refused with the reason, as today, or (ii) approved through a real owner action and THEN performed, asserted through Chrome's own API. Never performed without an approval — that regression is what wfo5's fail-closed branch and its mutant M2 exist to prevent.

Discovered-from: chrome-agent-platform-wfo5. Evidence: ~/cap-evidence/cap-wfo5/REPORT.md, kat-run2.log.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN TEXT, by its author (cap-k3). The description says a harness call 'has no originating conversation, so there is no progress channel on which to publish a card'. That is WRONG, and coord corrected it with a source pointer.

MEASURED, on origin/main a12f887c:
  extension/lib/acp-runner.js:401 runAcpTaskTurn executes an ACP turn ON a conversation container (the <agent-conversation> element), passed in by extension/ntp/ntp.js:81 and extension/shared/conversation.js:18.
  extension/lib/acp-runner.js:331 requestAcpPermission ALREADY renders a <permission-approval-card> into that container via container.appendTranscript(card), waits on its approve/deny events with a timeout, and — critically — DENIES when no surface exists: 'No surface to ask on: DENY rather than silently granting' (:342, reason 'no-surface').
So the surface exists AND the fail-closed-on-no-surface pattern is already established in this codebase. I asserted the opposite without checking acp-runner.js, and filed it as a premise. My error.

  1. requireOwnerApproval's card-publishing branch (service-worker.js:4967) is gated on context?.principal === 'model'. A harness call arrives as 'extension', so it never reaches that branch and falls to the Settings-tail refusal.
  2. mayResolveApproval (owner-approval.js:843) refuses an extension principal for any row whose runId starts with 'ui:' — which is exactly what approvalExecutionId returns for an owner principal.
  3. PRECEDENT for the fix already exists: webmcp.use-tool carries a bespoke resolverDocumentId carve-out (service-worker.js:4941-4953) that binds a card to an originating document and lets an extension principal resolve exactly that row. The harness case is the same shape with a different action set.
  4. The six actions are ALREADY in DESTRUCTIVE_ACTIONS (owner-approval.js:65-70), so createPendingApproval accepts them — no change needed there.

Also correcting item (c) in the description: it says there is no route to resolve a ui: row, only to list them. There IS a resolve route ('approval.resolve', service-worker.js:~8488) — what blocks a ui: row is mayResolveApproval's rule, not a missing route.

Card mounts in the active task conversation container where the task was entered, with Approve/Deny. Policy default stays 'ask' with 'never' as the strict opt-out; no third state for now. comments.text:
FIXED AND PUSHED — `fix/4lc0-cas-rewriter-vs-readers` @ `ab684f65`. The bead's open question is answered, and the answer was a module-import side effect.

IDENTIFIED (it was NOT a spawn): `tests/tool-descriptions.test.ts` rewrites `extension/wasm/cas/`. It imports the generator for one constant:
  `import { AGENT_DESCRIPTIONS } from "../scripts/build-bundled-tool-packages.mjs";`
and **the import RUNS it** — the generator's work is at module top level (WASM_OUT rm/mkdir at :394-398, the loops at :230/:236/:247/:318, the write path at :482) and its `isMain` flag (:34) gates only the final `process.exit(0)`. So a *reader* of a constant regenerates 38 shipped files.
HOW IT WAS FOUND: the sweep the bead asked for — run each candidate ALONE and fingerprint the CAS dir by per-file mtime. It was one of 19 candidates, and the only one whose fingerprint moved (18 clean). Two candidates initially "failed" alone with no dist built; after `npm run build:production` the sweep was decisive.

THE FALSIFICATION PAIR (driving the partition's phases with a fingerprint watcher, `/tmp/4lc0-demo.sh`):
| | serial phase | CAS changed DURING parallel | samples seeing it |
|---|---|---|---|
| pre-fix (main's partition) | none | **yes** (`c5c28e…`→`9a7b5e…`) | **3** |
| post-fix | `tool-descriptions` | no | **0** |
Pre-fix, gzip-preview did not red in *my* window (the rewrite takes ~15 ms and gzip-preview's reads missed it) — which is exactly why the *mechanism* had to be made deterministic rather than chased run to run. The bead's own NotFound came from the same window.

FIX (two parts; either alone is insufficient):
1. `SERIAL_REASONS` names `tests/tool-descriptions.test.ts` with the measured reason — the established mechanism, ordering the rewriter before its readers.
2. The hazard scan learns the shape that let it join the parallel phase: `IMPORT_BUILD_RE` → class "imports build.mjs or the bundled-tool generator (module side effects)", equal to spawning one. Without this, a future importer joins the parallel phase silently: the guard is structurally blind to it.

ACCEPTANCE (the bead asked for 10 consecutive subset runs): **10/10 green**, 0 CAS changes during the parallel phase in every run, 0 NotFound, 0 FAILED, writer serial in every run.

MUTANTS: **M1** declaration removed → guard test **RED** ("build-artifact hazard(s) would run in the PARALLEL phase — add each to SERIAL_REASONS … or to EXEMPTIONS with a proof of parallel-safety"); **M2** declaration AND scan class removed (= main's state) → guard **GREEN**, i.e. blind — that is the blind spot the scan change closes.

GATES: `npm run test:changed` 150 passed / 0 failed; `npm test` serial phase **18 files** GREEN in 192 s (was 17), parallel phase **477 files** GREEN in 59 s (was 478), 4459 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored. The phase counts moved exactly as intended: the rewriter left the parallel phase.

ROOT CAUSE LEFT STANDING: importing a generator should not rewrite the tree. Filed as **`chrome-agent-platform-i1i9`** (P3, discovered-from this bead) with the measurement and the reviewable shapes (work behind `isMain`, or constants moved to a pure module — explicitly NOT a 900-line mechanical indent). This bead's fix contains the hazard by ordering and detection; i1i9 removes it.

title: Two landed tests measure the box: the fleet-slot test assumes a free slot, the compiler test lets ambient load cause its refusal
description:
Two of my own landed tests are not hermetic to a busy box, found when npm test on the rshb branch ran at load1 20.9 / load5 43.4 with another lane's real journey gate active. Neither red is caused by rshb (that tree was green at 4437/0 in npm run test:changed minutes earlier); both are the "a test that measures the box as well as the code" class the 2026-09-23 review named, and both are in branches that already landed:

1. tests/heavy-gate-slot.test.ts — "0lj3: a HELD fleet slot makes the REAL journey gate refuse, naming the holder, and start no browser" (tests/heavy-gate-slot.test.ts:277).
   Observed: HeavyGateSlotRefusedError — "the fleet-wide heavy-gate slot is busy (waited 2009 ms) — held by chrome-journeys (pid 3128320 …)".
   Cause: the test HOLDS the real fleet slot /tmp/cap-heavy-gate.lock and then expects the real journey gate to refuse. If another lane's journey gate already holds it, the TEST's own hold is refused, so the test reds. The mechanism is correct — two gates must not share the machine — and the test assumes a free fleet slot.
   Acceptance: the test acquires the held slot with a bounded retry (or reports an explicit SKIP-with-reason that names the foreign holder), so a concurrent real gate cannot red it, while the assertion (the real journey gate refuses and starts no browser) is unchanged and still proved when the slot is free. Do NOT weaken the assertion to "it refused for some reason" — the property is that the holder is named.

2. tests/quiet-window.test.ts — "mkax: the REAL journey gate refuses with exit 75 while a REAL compiler is compiling (dnop)" (tests/quiet-window.test.ts:561).
   Observed refusal payload: {"load1":25.39,"loadPerCore":0.79,"compilers":12,"activeCompilers":0,"measurable":true} — the refusal came from the box's LOAD, not from the test's burner, and the test asserts activeCompilers >= 1.
   Cause: the spawned gate's env pins CAP_QUIET_WAIT_MS / SAMPLE_MS / MAX_COMPILERS / SUSTAINED but NOT CAP_QUIET_MAX_LOAD_PER_CORE, so on a loaded box the load condition alone causes the refusal. The test can then neither prove its own property nor fail honestly — and worse, on a slightly less loaded box it could pass for the load reason rather than the compile reason.
   Acceptance: pin CAP_QUIET_MAX_LOAD_PER_CORE high (the startup-failure drill already does this with maxLoadPerCore: 100) so ONLY the compile condition can produce the refusal; then the existing assertion (the refusal payload reports a compiling builder) is exactly the property. Falsification: remove the burner and the gate must NOT refuse.
close_reason: Landed on origin/main as v0.3.462 at commit 61e4fdabef7752f48df1737e674d806bee3fe75b. Private slot paths for contention tests prevent collision with live fleet gate locks.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
PATTERN, stated plainly as coord asked (this is the generalisation, not the two instances):

**A test whose SUBJECT is contention, written without accounting for the contention the fleet creates by existing.** Both failures are that one shape:
• tests/quiet-window.test.ts attributed a refusal to its own deliberate burner while ambient LOAD was the real cause — the payload it printed said so and it read past it: {"load1":25.39,"loadPerCore":0.79,"compilers":12,"activeCompilers":0}.
• tests/heavy-gate-slot.test.ts assumed a free fleet slot while a real journey gate held it.
The tell is in both messages: the test's own evidence names the foreign cause, and the assertion blames the local one. Same defect as voicebox's gate tonight, one level up: an instrument that cannot distinguish "my input caused this" from "the world caused this" will report whichever it was told to expect.

FIXES (acceptance already in the description; the shape of each):
1. heavy-gate-slot.test.ts: take a PRIVATE slot path for the test's own hold and pass CAP_HEAVY_GATE_SLOT=<the same private path> to the spawned journey gate, so the test neither collides with a real gate nor blocks one. The assertion stays exact (the refusal names the fixture holder and no browser starts).
2. quiet-window.test.ts: pin CAP_QUIET_MAX_LOAD_PER_CORE high in the spawned gate's env so ONLY the compile condition can cause the refusal — the startup-failure drill already does exactly this with maxLoadPerCore: 100. Falsification: with the pin removed, the same test at load1>11 reds for the load reason; with it, the compile is the only possible cause.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
LANDED: fix/zeew-hermetic-tests @ 2a302db20bbd3775734e2dc4e111b0067b31b508 (remote verified). Version 0.3.460 — NOTE FOR THE MERGER: chrome-agent-platform-rshb (fix/rshb-pad-left-shorthand @ 0c77c288) is ALSO 0.3.460, both branched from main's 0.3.459; whichever lands second needs renumbering.

GATE: npm test at this tip is GREEN — 16 serial + 474 parallel files, 490 total, 4431 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored, wall 237 s. All three failures from the rshb-tip run are gone, including tests/serial-phase-resilience.test.ts (which did not reproduce at this load — see the note below).

THE DIAGNOSIS IN THIS BEAD WAS HALF WRONG, AND THE DRILL CORRECTED IT — recorded because the wrong half is instructive:
• The bead proposed pinning CAP_QUIET_MAX_LOAD_PER_CORE as the fix for the compiler test. I implemented it, ran the mutant, and the mutant SURVIVED — the pin is necessary-but-not-sufficient.
• The real mechanism was fleet-slot contention, visible in the failure's own duration: the test took 7m29s because the gate it spawns takes the fleet-wide slot BEFORE it measures, so it queued behind another lane's real journey gate. By the time it measured, its own burners (40 × 3 s compiles) had exited — so the refusal came from the box's load with activeCompilers 0, the payload the assertion cannot satisfy.
• Same root cause in the other test, from the other side: it held the REAL slot to prove the journey gate refuses while held, so a real gate made the TEST's hold fail ("held by chrome-journeys (pid 3128320)").
So both tests assumed the fleet's own gate slot was free. The primary fix in each is a PRIVATE slot path; the load pin stays as a secondary guard, and a bounded slot wait means a future mistake fails in seconds rather than in 20 minutes.

VERIFIED PAIRS (ambient conditions deliberately worse than the failing run: a live foreign holder on the REAL slot, load1 23.19 = 0.72/core):
• heavy-gate-slot.test.ts — fixed: PASS in 2 s; mutant (real path, same holder): RED naming foreign-holder-drill.
• quiet-window.test.ts — fixed: PASS in 8 s (was 7m29s FAIL at a lower load); mutant (no private slot, holder alive): RED in 14 s refusing {"reason":"heavy-gate-slot-busy","holder":{"gate":"foreign-holder-drill",…}} — it refuses for the SLOT reason, not the compile reason, which is exactly what the assertion exists to catch.
My load generators were bounded and mine (16 CPU burners, 100–120 s, stopped); the foreign holder is a fixture on the real slot for 150 s.

STILL OPEN, filed separately: tests/serial-phase-resilience.test.ts "pozs: timed-out serial file leaves no descendant processes behind" failed once with "grandchild pid must have been recorded" at load1 20.9 / load5 43.4 and did NOT reproduce on the green run — a load-sensitive fixture with a timing assumption, not one of the two fixed here.

comments.text:
FIXED AND PUSHED — `fix/n772-one-sidecar-path` @ `0dae9c74`, with one honest correction to the bead's premise and one new defect found in the same observable.

**1. THE REPORTED PATH MISMATCH IS ALREADY FIXED ON MAIN — verified by execution, not by reading the file.** `heavyGateHolderPathFor(HEAVY_GATE_SLOT_PATH) === HEAVY_GATE_HOLDER_PATH` (the pure agreement), and a real acquisition followed by `readHeavyGateHolder()` **with no path argument** names the live holder: `n772-probe (pid 1117647, alive=true)`. On disk only `/tmp/cap-heavy-gate.holder.json` exists — there is no `cap-heavy-gate.lock.holder.json` anywhere. The default-case special-case came in with the 0lj3 revision, so the bead's description matches the **pre-revision** code (`slotPaths:95` reading `${slotPath}.holder.json` unconditionally). Recorded rather than silently delivering a no-op fix.

**2. WHAT WAS GENUINELY MISSING, and is the substance of the change: the tests that would have caught it.** The existing checks compared the exported constant to a literal, and the live round trip used a *private* slot with a path computed by the same function under test — neither exercises "the writer's announcement for the DEFAULT slot is visible to the DEFAULT reader". Added three drills:
- **n772-a**: the pure agreement PLUS an executing default-path check — acquire the real default slot only if it is free (300 ms bound, so it can never hold a real gate up), then read through the **default reader**. If another lane holds the slot it prints an explicit **INCONCLUSIVE** line rather than passing quietly, and it never waits for the fleet slot.
- **n772-b**: private-slot isolation — the announcement lands beside its own slot; the default path's bytes are identical before and after; the default reader never names the private holder.
- **n772-c**: see (3).

**3. A SECOND DEFECT, MEASURED WHILE VERIFYING THIS ONE.** Acquiring a **FREE** slot fired `onWait` once with:
  `heavy-gate: free-slot-probe waiting for the fleet-wide gate slot [...] (bound 2000 ms) — held by an unnamed holder (no announcement sidecar)`
while the acquisition completed in **~8 ms** — a holder claim **where there was no holder**. Consequence: real contention was indistinguishable from an uncontended acquisition in every gate's log (this lane misread that line repeatedly during the 2026-09-23 gate work, and it appears in this repo's own gate logs). Cause: the line was printed at the TOP of the first loop iteration, before any read. Fix: announce only after a **200 ms grace** with a **fresh** holder read (so the lane that actually holds it is named), and poll the read at **250 ms** so the loop can reach that point at all while still respecting the bound — a read that blocks for the whole deadline never gets a second chance to speak. A genuinely held slot still names its holder correctly: `held by the-real-holder (pid 1121876, started …)`.

**MUTANTS, all run — each reddens the check that names its property:** **M1** reintroduce the reported drift (derivation never special-cases the default) → n772-a **RED**; **M2** a private slot resolving to the DEFAULT path → n772-b **RED**; **M3** announce at the top of the first iteration again → n772-c **RED**; **M4** read the whole deadline instead of polling → n772-c **RED** (the held-slot half cannot speak).

**GATES:** `npm run test:changed` 26 passed / 0 failed + 325 passed / 0 failed; `npm test` **GREEN** — 4466 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored (14 steps), serial phase (17 files) GREEN in 234 s, parallel phase (478 files) GREEN; build + `check:dist` clean.

**STATE: in review.** Nothing here weakens the original property; M1 is the direct proof that the drift would now be caught.

title: Distinguish flock setup errors from heavy-gate contention
description: Independent 0lj3 review at 5fb8d954: scripts/lib/heavy-gate-slot.ts:208-259 discards flock stderr/status and maps all missing handshake results to busy/environmental75. Private missing-parent lock path fails immediately in6ms but reports heavy-gate-slot-busy held by unnamed holder. Evidence ~/cap-evidence/0lj3-independent-review/probes.ts bad-path and probes.log. comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
FIXED AND PUSHED — `fix/o3rx-flock-setup-vs-contention` @ `f0959578` (off main `d31158b0`).

**1. THE REVIEWED CASE IS ALREADY CORRECT ON THIS TREE — verified by execution.** The review's bad-path probe (a lock path under a missing directory) now yields `HeavyGateSlotSetupError`, not `HeavyGateSlotRefusedError`: measured `missing parent dir (the reviewer's bad-path): HeavyGateSlotSetupError — ENVIRONMENT: … could not be SET UP at …`. The 0lj3 revision added that classification, so the review at `5fb8d954` describes the pre-revision code — as with n772, recorded plainly rather than shipping a no-op.

**2. WHAT THE CLASSIFICATION STILL GOT WRONG, which is what this change fixes.** The discriminator was a **message scan** (`/cannot open lock file|Permission denied|No such file or directory/` or exit 66). Measured flock behaviour (util-linux, 2026-09-24) shows why that cannot be the rule:
| shape | exit | stderr |
|---|---|---|
| contention (held, `-w` elapsed) | **1** | **empty** |
| missing parent / permission / read-only fs | 66 | `cannot open lock file …` |
| invalid timeout value | 64 | `invalid timeout: 'abc'` |
| cannot execute the command | 69 | `failed to execute …` |
| helper killed (OOM or the backstop) | `status.code = null` | signal `SIGKILL` |
So contention is **a quiet exit 1** — or a helper our own backstop killed while it was still waiting — and everything else is a setup/system fault. The old rule still classified a helper that **never performed the handshake** (silent exit 0, or any code it did not recognise, e.g. a stub/wrapper `flock` resolved from PATH, or a signal-killed helper) as *"the slot is busy, held by an unnamed holder"*: a peer blamed for something that was not contention, the exact inverse of this file's own note that "reporting a setup fault as busy sends a lane to wait for a holder that does not exist".

**3. CHANGE.** `contention = (exit === 1 && stderr === "") || (status.code === null && signal === SIGKILL)`; otherwise `HeavyGateSlotSetupError` carrying flock's own **bounded (300 char)** words plus its exit status or signal — the "retain bounded diagnostics/status" half of the acceptance.

**4. TESTS (executing, each staging a real failure).** `o3rx-a` a helper that cannot execute its command (PATH containing flock but no `sh`) → SETUP naming *"failed to execute"*; `o3rx-b` an unwritable lock directory (chmod 500) → SETUP naming the access failure; `o3rx-c` a helper that never performs the handshake (stub `flock` exiting 0 and 70, silently) → SETUP, never busy, and never naming a peer. Real contention still yields the refusal and names the holder (existing 0lj3 drills).

**5. MUTANTS.** **M1** the previous message-scan rule restored → `o3rx-c` **RED** (silent exit 0 blamed on a peer — the proof this rule is load-bearing); **M2** everything is contention → all three SETUP drills **RED**; **M3** nothing is contention → the two 0lj3 **contention** drills **RED** (so I did not simply make everything a setup error).

**6. GATES.** `npm run test:changed` GREEN on re-run: 19 + 26 + 325 passed, 0 failed. **The first run reddened on an unrelated check — `dqxa: prepareLoadedExtension refuses a pre-existing probe before destination copying or injection` (`tests/emscripten-abi-loaded-harness.test.ts:252`) — because a stale `extension/_emscripten_abi_probe` directory was present in that worktree, which that check refuses BY DESIGN; the exact check passes alone on re-run, and the whole gate was green afterwards.** Worth a separate look: a leftover probe directory from an interrupted run makes *any* unrelated change's `test:changed` red. `npm test` GREEN — 4466 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored (14 steps).

WHAT WAS STILL WRONG, and is this change — one residual instance of the same shape.** The helper's 1500 ms backstop watchdog was cleared on the success line after `await child.status`, so a rejection there (the helper already reaped, ECHILD) left it pending. A PATTERN WORTH RECORDING, since this is the third bead in a row with the same shape:** `n772`, `o3rx` and `k9i3` all cite `scripts/lib/heavy-gate-slot.ts` and all describe the **pre-revision** code — the independent 0lj3 review's revision (`5fb8d954`) is **not an ancestor of main**, and the landed fix (the 0lj3 revision, `9811e07c`) already carries the classification, the sidecar derivation and the timer clears. title: Every negative assertion in a security gate needs a positive counterpart proving there was something to be negative about — audit criterion after nweh
description:
Follow-on from chrome-agent-platform-nweh, filed rather than done blind because the sweep is wider than one gate and coord's instruction was to file it if large.

THE CRITERION, extracted from a defect that survived a green gate: a check of the form `!X.includes(bad)` or `count === 0` or `!/"value"/.test(text)` passes on EMPTY, ABSENT or NEVER-FETCHED data exactly as happily as it passes on clean data. It is only a check if a SIBLING assertion proves the payload was non-empty and the thing that should have produced it actually ran. In nweh both halves were missing at once: the fixture returned zero cookie rows (and Array.isArray([]) is true), and the regex could not have matched its own text because the text was double-stringified. The production mapper was correct the whole time — the instrument could not see a leak, and it was the gate whose subject is credential leakage.

The fix pattern that worked, and which is the template for the rest: THREE checks where there was one — (a) a POSITIVE check that the fixture was non-empty and the seeded marker reached the code under test, (b) the negative property asserted on DECODED structure rather than on a stringified blob, (c) the marker absent from every message that crossed the boundary, not just the last one. Then falsify by mutating production and requiring (b) and (c) to redden SPECIFICALLY while (a) and the plumbing check stay green — a differential, not just a red.

WHAT I VERIFIED, and what I did not. Bounded static pass over scripts/security-suite.ts only:
- The cookie section now has the pairing (checks at :497, :516, :527, :537). Measured: pristine 21/0, and the production mutant reddens exactly the two redaction checks.
- The negative assertions I found elsewhere in that file and did NOT verify: "network exfil: no request escaped the sandbox" and "network exfil: still zero after settle" (both count-based negatives; the four cap:fetch refusal checks look like their positive counterpart, but I did not prove the probes executed rather than failed to fire), "sandbox escape: window.opener is null", "prompt-injection: no chrome.runtime (extension API) in the sandbox" (absence of an API in a page — needs proof the sandbox document actually executed), and "sandbox escape: the outer page did not navigate away". LABEL: static reading, not measured. Each needs the same question asked of it: what positive fact proves there was something to be negative about?
- NOT SWEPT AT ALL: the other security-shaped gates and harnesses (scripts/security-injection.ts, scripts/security-suite-custody.mjs's own self-tests, the KATs, kat-webmcp-honest-errors.ts, and the ~40 harnesses in scripts/). The criterion is general; the sweep is not done.

METHOD FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT: for each check whose condition is a negative or a zero-count, write down the positive fact that must be true for the negative to mean anything, then look for that fact in the same run's assertions. If it is not there, add it as its own check (nweh's (a) is the model) and falsify the pair by mutating production, requiring the negative to redden while the positive stays green. Do not weaken or delete a negative to make a suite pass; a negative that cannot fail is the finding.

WHY THIS IS P2 AND NOT P3: a green check on a security property is the most expensive kind of reassurance there is. Tonight two gates inside test:all were red on main and a third (this one) was green while asserting nothing; the green one is the dangerous case, because it is the one nobody goes looking at.

title: Custody teardown crashes on ENOENT when the runner child has already exited: readProcIdentity reads /proc/<pid>/stat unguarded, so the run leaves NO receipt at all
description:
OBSERVED, not inferred. I launched npm run test:security and then killed it from outside (my own error: a pkill whose pattern matched more than I intended, during a run I should not have started while a flock -n check in the same command batch was reporting the lock held). The supervisor did not report a kill — it CRASHED:

  node:internal/fs/promises:1345
  Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/proc/3756057/stat'
      at async readFile (node:internal/fs/promises:1996:14)
      at async Promise.all (index 0)
      at async readProcIdentity (scripts/security-suite-custody.mjs:61:27)
      at async terminateAttestedGroup (scripts/security-suite-custody.mjs:326:21)
      at async scripts/security-suite-supervisor.mjs:344:17
  Node.js v24.21.0

The lock HAD been acquired normally first (CAP_SECURITY_LOCK_WAIT 1790119648220 / CAP_SECURITY_LOCK_ACQUIRED 1790119648299 — a 79 ms wait), so this is not a lock defect.

THE DEFECT: readProcIdentity reads /proc/<pid>/stat for a process that has already exited, and the ENOENT is not caught. That is a TOCTOU race inherent to the design — the group is scanned, then each member's identity is read, and a member can exit in between. It does not require an outside kill: any runner that dies on its own during teardown (a crash, an OOM kill, its own timeout firing at the same moment) can hit it.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A CRASH: the supervisor's whole job is to leave an attested verdict. When this throws, there is NO CAP_SECURITY_RESULT line and NO receipt.json — the evidence directory is left without the record that says what happened. So the failure mode erases its own evidence, which is the same shape as the rest of tonight's defects: an exit-124 timeout hiding a FAIL printed 100 s earlier (bead im52), a swallowed page exception turning a missing element into a product accusation (bead 0lb4), a harness crashing before any check runs while its registry row still asserts a verdict (bead cwy2). A gate that cannot report how it died is a gate whose death gets attributed to the environment.

Note the contrast, which is why I am filing this as narrow rather than as a custody redesign: the 120 s TIMEOUT path handled the same situation correctly earlier tonight — receipt written with timedOut:true, termSent:true, residue [], cleaned true, groupSurvived false. So the attestation machinery works when the supervisor drives the termination and fails when the child is already gone.

FIX SHAPE: make readProcIdentity tolerate a vanished pid — return a distinguished "already-exited" identity rather than throwing — and make terminateAttestedGroup treat that as the benign case it is (the process is gone, which is what termination wanted), while still recording it in the receipt so the run says "child exited before identity read" instead of saying nothing. Keep the fail-closed behaviour for every OTHER error: an unreadable /proc for a process that still EXISTS must not be silently treated as exited, or the custody chain loses the ability to tell "it died" from "I could not see it".

ACCEPTANCE: kill the runner child from outside mid-run and get a receipt with a verdict rather than a Node stack trace and an evidence directory with no CAP_SECURITY_RESULT; the existing timeout path still produces its current receipt shape unchanged; a unit test covers both branches (pid vanished -> benign and recorded; pid present but unreadable -> still fail-closed).

REPRO: start npm run test:security, kill the runner child (not the supervisor) after CAP_SECURITY_LOCK_ACQUIRED, read stderr. Evidence of my instance: /tmp/cap8-sec-pristine.log. The clean re-run that followed waited for the lock and produced receipts normally (runId 72e9f4e6e938d4e8), so this did not leave the lock or the tree in a bad state — verified NOW-FREE afterwards and the worktree clean.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
CANDIDATE PUSHED — branch cap/8ixk-custody-enoent @ 18c6e01c2e9d5aaebd69e2c14091a82da971a1fd, based on origin/main d31158b0. Worktree /home/paulkinlan/worktrees/cap-8ixk-custody, clean, check:dist clean at HEAD. 3 files: scripts/security-suite-custody.mjs, scripts/security-suite-supervisor.mjs, tests/security-suite-custody.test.ts. No product code, and the commit subject is prefixed `internal:` so the post-commit hook bailed and consumed no version — verified: package.json is still 0.3.475 and CHANGELOG's top entry is unrelated. That is ku6o's hook fix working end to end on a real internal commit.

MECHANISM, refined from what I filed. I originally described this as readProcIdentity being unguarded, which is true but is not where the crash escapes. The ENOENT IS caught: terminateAttestedGroup's catch calls procIdentities(), filters by pgid, and when the group is empty — exactly the case where everything already exited — `rows.length === 0` RETHROWS the original ENOENT. So the benign outcome (nothing left to terminate) took the fail-closed exit, escaped the supervisor as an uncaught rejection, and the run wrote no receipt. Fixing only readProcIdentity would have left the rethrow in place.

FIX, at the teardown site rather than in readProcIdentity, so that function's strict contract stays intact for its other three callers (attestOwnedGroup, procIdentities, and the supervisor's parent/self reads):
- new exported isVanishedProcError(error): true ONLY for code === "ENOENT". An unreadable /proc for a process that still exists is a different fact and is not laundered into "it exited" — that was the acceptance condition I wrote when filing this, and it is the reason the predicate is exported and unit-tested rather than inlined.
- terminateAttestedGroup's catch returns a distinguished benign result when the error is a vanished /proc AND the group is also gone. BOTH conditions are required and that conjunction is the fail-closed boundary: a dead leader inside a LIVE group still falls through to the observed-descendant ownership check and can still throw.
- readIdentity and isAlive became injectable options defaulting to readProcIdentity and groupAlive, the same pattern attestOwnedGroup already uses. Without them the race can only be tested by timing a real process death, and a flaky test of a teardown race is worse than none.
- the supervisor threads leaderExited into `termination` and sets custodyReason ||= "leader-exited-before-identity-read", so the receipt SAYS the child exited before the identity read instead of saying nothing. `||=` so it can never displace a real custody finding.

VERIFIED IT CANNOT CHANGE A VERDICT, which was the risk of touching a receipt field: exits 70/71/72 are gated on termination.survived, residue.length and cleanup.ok alone (security-suite-supervisor.mjs:385-387) and custodyReason is not consulted for the exit code. - vanished leader + group STILL ALIVE -> rejects, so the benign path provably needs both facts.
- EACCES + dead group -> rejects under the SAME alive sequence as the benign case, proving the gate is the error kind and not merely the group being gone.

FALSIFICATION, as a differential. First attempt removed the whole benign block and was killed at TYPE level (dropping the return removed leaderExited from the inferred type, so the test did not type-check) — a kill, but not the one that proves the behavior. Redone as `if (false && ...)` so the return type is preserved and only the BEHAVIOR is removed: 16 passed / 1 FAILED, and the one red is exactly "a leader that vanished while its group also died is benign, returned and RECORDED — not rethrown", with the ENOENT visibly propagating. REVISION PUSHED addressing all of cap-astra's finalized REVISE findings on 18c6e01c. Branch cap/8ixk-custody-enoent now at 285c3adb00d785141cefc594ceb43592a452bea1, three commits on base d31158b0: 18c6e01c (the original ENOENT guard, credited as working by review), 4092e2f5 (finding 2), 285c3adb (finding 3). FINDING 2 — EARLY-EXIT COMPLETENESS (4092e2f5). Review reproduced with a LIVE owned fixture at the unchanged 18c6e01c: both kernel identity reads complete, the own child then dies before completion is delivered, and process.kill(-pgid, SIGTERM) throws killESRCH — escaping uncaught, Node exit 1, NO receipt. A pre-existing sibling of the ENOENT race, not newly introduced, but the acceptance is "an early exit leaves a receipt", which guarding one read does not deliver. Fixed: both process.kill calls tolerate ESRCH (a group that finished dying between the alive check and the signal is the outcome termination wanted) and return a distinguished groupGoneBeforeSignal result. ONLY ESRCH qualifies — EPERM and every other kill failure still propagate, because not being ALLOWED to signal a group is a real custody finding and must not be laundered into "it already exited". isVanishedGroupError is exported and unit-tested for exactly that boundary. `kill` became injectable so no test ever signals a real group (an impossible pgid is inside the pid range on some kernels). The supervisor additionally wraps teardown in terminateAttestedGroupSafely, so the no-lost-receipt property is now STRUCTURAL rather than an enumeration of the races I thought of — which is the point, since review found one I had not. It records teardownThrew in the receipt and deliberately does NOT change any exit code; whether a non-ESRCH teardown refusal should also force a non-zero exit is a policy call for the desk, and today the refusal is at least visible instead of erasing the receipt.

FINDING 3 — CALLER COVERAGE AND CLEANUP DIAGNOSTIC PRIORITY (285c3adb). Two things, the second a REGRESSION I INTRODUCED. (a) A caller-only mutant, `if (false && termination.leaderExited)` in the supervisor, survived all 17 custody tests because every test asserted what the HELPER RETURNS and nothing asserted what the RECEIPT RECORDS; review's live probe confirmed custodyReason came back empty where it should have said leader-exited-before-identity-read. My own commit message had claimed the marker was "recorded" — the helper returned it and nothing downstream was tested. (b) I assigned the benign markers BEFORE the cleanup check, and cleanup used `||=`, so it could no longer replace them: a run with both a benign leader exit and a private-profile symlink refusal reported custodyReason=leader-exited-before-identity-read at exit 71 with cleaned:false (receipt b21e2e6180fb0ca9), where the control with only the marker assignment disabled reported the proper cleanup-refused:profile is not an owned regular directory (d09361b8bf36e32c). The exit code failed closed correctly throughout, so this was a WRONG DIAGNOSTIC rather than a wrong verdict — and it is precisely what my own code comment promised could not happen ("must never displace a real custody finding"). Only a live fixture caught it; no unit test covered the order at all. Fixed by making the derivation ONE pure exported function, custodyReasonFor({survived, residueCount, cleanupOk, cleanupReason, leaderExited, groupGoneBeforeSignal, teardownThrew}), called by the supervisor once AFTER cleanup. The order is the semantics, so it now lives in one testable place instead of in the sequence of mutations applied to a local. Precedence most-severe-first: descendant-residue, owned-group-survived, cleanup-refused, teardown-threw, then the two benign races. The first three are byte-for-byte the pre-8ixk behaviour (residue overwrote survived; cleanup only filled an empty reason); the benign markers are new and go last, which is what fixes the regression.

New derivation tests: a clean run records no reason; each of the six findings records its own; THE REGRESSION CASE — benign marker plus cleanup refusal — records cleanup-refused for all three benign markers; and the full severity order is pinned including residue-overwrites-survived, survived-not-replaced-by-cleanup, threw-outranks-benign and first-benign-wins.

comments.text:
REVISION 2 PUSHED — cap/8ixk-custody-enoent @ 7de4802de8a10c68c1ad26bdb7eeffc29afa32a8 (four commits on d31158b0: 18c6e01c, 4092e2f5, 285c3adb, 7de4802d). Addresses cap-astra's two points on 285c3adb, and the first is a LOOSENING I SHIPPED BY INFERENCE.

1. FAIL-CLOSED TREATMENT OF A GENUINE REFUSAL, RESTORED. terminateAttestedGroupSafely catches a teardown throw so the receipt is still written, but it did not restore the exit code. Before this bead's work an EPERM or identity-change refusal escaped as an uncaught rejection: supervisor exit 1, no receipt. After it, the same refusal produced a receipt with custodyReason=teardown-threw:... and the RUNNER's exit code — which is 0 when the run itself passed. So a real custody refusal had become a pass-with-a-note. My previous commit message said the change 'deliberately does NOT change any exit code', which was true about not adding a change and FALSE IN EFFECT, because the previous behaviour was a non-zero exit. Review is right that any new potentially-successful teardown refusal needs explicit review or owner decision rather than inferred policy approval, so this restores the prior fail-closed outcome verbatim rather than re-deciding it: exitCode becomes 1 when teardownThrew is set and the run would otherwise have exited 0. Applied only in that case so a runner's own failure code is never masked. Whether a dedicated code in the 70/71/72 family is better than 1 is flagged as a desk/owner decision and NOT taken.

2. CALLER-LEVEL COVERAGE, AND MY 'UNIMPORTABLE' CLAIM WAS WRONG. I had declared the supervisor untestable because it is a top-level script. This test file already spawns it via runSupervisor with the self-test fixture and parses CAP_SECURITY_RESULT, and has done so for the guard, pgid-mismatch, timeout, stubborn, exit37, signal and escape scenarios. So the wiring was testable all along and I called an instrument a blocker. Added a caller-level test: a real TERM teardown writes its receipt, records termSent:true, and records NO benign custody marker. Without it, a change that made the benign markers fire on any termination would pass every unit test, because the unit tests pin custodyReasonFor's derivation and not what the supervisor passes into it.

COVERAGE BOUNDARY, stated rather than rounded up. The caller-level test covers the NEGATIVE direction. Two things it does not cover, neither hidden by it: (a) a benign marker actually reaching the receipt needs a fixture scenario where the leader vanishes or the group dies before the signal — none of the existing scenarios does, so the positive direction is still covered only by the reviewer's live owned fixture probe; (b) the restored fail-closed exit for teardownThrew cannot be driven end to end either, because no fixture scenario produces a teardown throw and no CAP_SECURITY_TEST_* hook forces one (the hooks are ESCAPE_CHILD_FAIL, FORCE_ATTEST_MISMATCH, SAMPLE_FREEZE_MS, SCENARIO, STATE). Adding such a hook means putting test-only surface into production code, which is a reviewed change and not one to make unilaterally at the end of a revision. The invariant is asserted as 'a run that exits 0 must not be carrying a custody finding', which is weaker than driving it and is labelled as such.

GATES AT 7de4802d, all re-run: npm test exit 0 — parallel phase 478 files GREEN 71s, 495 files total, wall 275s, zero failures; npm run test:security exit 0 with receipt {"result":"PASS","exit":0,"custodyReason":""} and runner.log RESULT: 21 passed, 0 failed, so neither benign marker fires spuriously on a normal run; build rc=0; check:dist clean at HEAD; canonical lock FREE and worktree clean.
