comments.text:
COVERAGE GAPS KEPT EXPLICIT for the next review, plus a correction to my own boundary claim (cap-astra seq164).

CORRECTION — MY 'NEEDS A PRODUCTION HOOK' CLAIM WAS WRONG. I wrote that driving the positive direction and the fail-closed refusal end to end would require putting test-only surface into production code, and therefore was not a change to make unilaterally. cap-astra is right that it is not: the supervisor's self-test path already spawns a FIXTURE runner (CAP_SECURITY_RUNNER=tests/fixtures/security-suite-fake-runner.mjs) selected by CAP_SECURITY_TEST_SCENARIO, and that fixture already drives timeout, stubborn, escape, guard, pgid-mismatch, exit37 and signal. A new scenario in that fixture — a child that dies after the identity read but before completion is delivered, and one that provokes a genuine refusal — is TEST-SUPPORT CODE ONLY. No production hook is needed, and cap-astra's own durable probes already demonstrate the pre/post-identity-death and genuine-refusal cases with a test-support preload around the existing owned fixture. So the gap is closable without touching shipped code, and my reason for not closing it does not hold.

STILL OPEN, AND DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED AS COVERED:
1. POSITIVE CALLER COVERAGE (the original R2). Nothing in the committed suite proves the benign flag actually REACHES the receipt on disk. tests/security-suite-custody.test.ts proves custodyReasonFor derives leader-exited-before-identity-read and group-gone-before-signal correctly, and the caller-level test proves a NORMAL teardown records NO benign marker. Negative marker coverage does not close R2: a supervisor that dropped termination.leaderExited on the way into custodyReasonFor would pass every committed test. Today that wiring is verified only by cap-astra's live owned-fixture probe (receipt 49cdbaf342180fa9, custodyReason leader-exited-before-identity-read, cleaned true) — reviewer-side evidence, not a shipped regression test.
2. FAIL-CLOSED REGRESSION COVERAGE. The restored exit-1-on-teardownThrew is asserted only as the invariant 'a run that exits 0 must not be carrying a custody finding'. No committed test drives a genuine refusal through the supervisor and asserts a non-zero exit, so a future change that re-loosens it would not be caught by the suite. This is the exact defect class I shipped once already at 285c3adb (fail-open on a genuine refusal), which is why it should not rest on an untestable-by-me claim.

SHAPE OF THE FIX, so the next lane does not re-derive it: add fixture scenarios that (a) let the child exit after both kernel identity reads complete but before completion is delivered — expect a receipt with custodyReason leader-exited-before-identity-read and the run's own exit code; (b) let the group die before the signal — expect group-gone-before-signal; (c) provoke a genuine refusal (EPERM or an identity change) — expect a NON-ZERO exit AND a receipt naming teardown-threw, which is the pairing that was broken at 285c3adb. All three are fixture-side. Then the reviewer's live probe becomes corroboration rather than the only coverage.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
CORRECTION to the fixture-scenario labels in my previous comment, from cap-astra seq166 and verified against the shipped code. I recorded a WRONG expected marker, and a wrong expectation written on a bead is how a future lane encodes the wrong test — so it is corrected here rather than only in chat.

WHAT I GOT WRONG: I wrote that a child exiting 'after both identity reads complete but before completion is delivered' should expect custodyReason leader-exited-before-identity-read. It should expect **group-gone-before-signal**.

WHY, from the code at 7de4802d rather than from memory:
- leaderExited:true is returned at scripts/security-suite-custody.mjs:397, inside the catch guarded at :392 by . So it requires the IDENTITY READ ITSELF to throw ENOENT — the leader's /proc entry vanished before or during readProcIdentity — AND the group to be dead. That is cap-astra's BEFORE-identity probe.
- groupGoneBeforeSignal:true is returned at :427 and :442, inside the two kill guards . Reaching them means the identity read SUCCEEDED (the try completed, the identity matched), and then process.kill(-pgid, SIGTERM) or the SIGKILL escalation threw ESRCH because the group finished dying in between. That is the AFTER-identity case.

So the two markers are distinguished by WHICH syscall found the process gone — the /proc read or the signal — and a fixture scenario has to aim at one or the other deliberately. Encoding 'dies after the identity reads' as leader-exited-before-identity-read would have produced a test asserting a marker the code can never emit on that path, which would fail and invite someone to 'fix' it by weakening the assertion.

CORRECTED FIX SHAPE, replacing the one in my previous comment. Three fixture scenarios in tests/fixtures/security-suite-fake-runner.mjs (test-support code only, no production hook):
  (a) BEFORE-IDENTITY DEATH: the child exits so that readProcIdentity throws ENOENT while the group is also gone -> expect a receipt with custodyReason **leader-exited-before-identity-read** and the run's own exit code.
  (b) AFTER-IDENTITY DEATH: both kernel identity reads complete and their actual bytes are delivered, then the child/group dies before the signal lands, so process.kill raises ESRCH -> expect **group-gone-before-signal**.
  (c) GENUINE REFUSAL: provoke EPERM or an identity change (starttime/pgid/sid/uid mismatch) -> expect a **NON-ZERO exit AND a receipt naming teardown-threw:<message>**. That pairing is exactly what was broken at 285c3adb, where the receipt survived but the exit code did not.
After those three, cap-astra's live owned-fixture probe becomes corroboration rather than the only coverage of the wiring.

STATUS UNCHANGED AND NOT UPGRADED BY THIS CORRECTION: both coverage gaps in my previous comment remain open author acknowledgements — positive caller coverage (the benign flag actually reaching the receipt) and fail-closed regression coverage (a genuine refusal exiting non-zero). cap-astra records them as author reports with no new runtime approval, and 7de4802d remains a new author-reported candidate, not an approved one. Nothing here claims otherwise.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
TEXT REPAIR for my previous comment: two code conditions were eaten by shell command substitution because I wrote them inside backticks, so that comment reads "inside the catch guarded at :392 by ." and "inside the two kill guards" with the predicate missing. A bead comment with the condition silently deleted is worse than no comment, since it still looks authoritative. The substance of the correction is unchanged; only the two predicates are restated here, without backticks.

Predicate 1 — the leaderExited path, scripts/security-suite-custody.mjs:392 guarding the return at :397:
    if (isVanishedProcError(error) && !isAlive(pgid))
So leader-exited-before-identity-read requires BOTH that the identity read itself threw ENOENT (isVanishedProcError is true only for code === "ENOENT") AND that the group is already dead. This is the BEFORE-identity case.

Predicate 2 — the groupGoneBeforeSignal paths, the kill guards at :422 and :437 guarding the returns at :427 and :442:
    if (!isVanishedGroupError(error)) throw error;
So group-gone-before-signal is reached only when the identity read SUCCEEDED and the try block completed, and then process.kill(-pgid, SIGTERM) or the SIGKILL escalation threw ESRCH (isVanishedGroupError is true only for code === "ESRCH"). Every other kill failure is rethrown, which is what keeps an EPERM refusal fail-closed. This is the AFTER-identity case.

The distinction the correction turns on, restated plainly: the two markers are separated by WHICH syscall found the process gone — the /proc identity read, or the signal. A fixture scenario must aim at one deliberately, and encoding "dies after the identity reads" as leader-exited-before-identity-read would assert a marker the code cannot emit on that path.

PROCESS NOTE, second occurrence tonight and worth naming as a habit rather than a slip: my earlier nco2 comment lost a git command the same way, and I patched it with a follow-up then too. The fix is mechanical — pass bead text through a single-quoted heredoc, or avoid backticks entirely — and the check is to read the stored comment back rather than trusting the tool's success line, which is how both were caught.

title: Take the fleet-wide gate turn in the remaining gate-class harnesses — read the custody fd-9 protocol first, because a second lock is how you get a deadlock neither lock can see
description:
Follow-up from chrome-agent-platform-0lj3 (the fleet-wide heavy-gate slot). Landed scope there: chrome-journeys.ts and scripts/kat-runner.ts take the turn through launchChrome's fleetSlot/requireQuiet pairing. NOT done there, deliberately:

1. The other gate-class entries in scripts/lib/harness-registry.ts still take only a browser slot (or their own scope) and can therefore run concurrently with a journey: the a11y gate (scripts/a11y-audit.ts, npm test:a11y), the components gate (scripts/component-gallery-smoke.ts, npm test:components), the width gate (scripts/npm run test:width), and the named on-demand suites that drive many browsers.
2. The security custody chain (scripts/security-suite-supervisor.sh + scripts/security-suite-supervisor.sh's fd-9 to the canonical lock, guarded by tests/security-suite-custody.test.ts) must be READ before anything else is layered onto its exclusivity.

THE CAUTION, in coord's words (2026-09-22), because it is the acceptance condition and not a note: 'A second lock introduced into a system that already has one is how you get a deadlock neither lock can see.' Concretely for this work: a harness that takes the heavy-gate slot and then requests the canonical lock (or vice versa) can wait on itself if the ordering is not fixed; the security supervisor already holds the canonical lock on fd 9 for its whole run, so a naive 'wrap everything in the heavy slot' would add a second wait to a process that is already a lock holder. Fix the ORDER first (one documented acquisition order across the fleet), then wire.

ACCEPTANCE: each gate-class entry either takes the fleet turn (verified by the same two-way guard 0lj3 uses: registry declaration set == sources passing fleetSlot) or carries a recorded reason why it deliberately does not, with the deadlock analysis for the custody chain written down. Plus: a test that a process holding the heavy-gate slot and then asking for the canonical lock cannot self-deadlock (bounded wait + named holder, whichever order is chosen).
close_reason: Landed on origin/main as v0.3.469 at commit 1ea2b47a673637598361d50911edb11f1cf568fe. Deadlock order refusal between fleet turn and canonical lock enforced in launchChrome; all gate entries specify turn reasons. tests/harness-registry.test.ts and tests/heavy-gate-slot.test.ts green.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
LANDED: feat/ryrr-fleet-turn-order @ 813b8306de81c088e9f4aed9a9ccd2cac44571a6 (remote verified), version 0.3.466. npm test at the tip: 16 serial + 476 parallel, 492 files, 4446 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored, wall 224 s; check:gallery green; the worktree is clean after the build (no generated-file drift).

WHAT THE BEAD ASKED FOR, delivered as the two halves that are decidable today:
1. THE DEADLOCK CAUTION, IN CODE. The system already has one lock — scripts/security-suite-supervisor.sh holds the canonical serialized-Chrome lock on fd 9 for its whole run (exec 9>"$LOCK"; flock -x 9) and launches its harnesses as children. The fleet-wide order is TURN then canonical, so a custody child asking for the turn would queue behind a gate waiting for the canonical lock. launchChrome now REFUSES `fleetSlot` when this process already holds the canonical lock (CAP_SECURITY_NONCE / CAP_CHROME_LOCK_HELD — the same markers acquireChromeLock bypasses on), with an error that names the inverted order and the fd-9 holder.
2. EVERY GATE-CLASS ENTRY SAYS WHETHER IT TAKES THE TURN. HarnessEntry.reason is widened for that purpose; the custody reasoning is recorded on security-suite.ts and security-injection.ts, and the honest "no recorded load-sensitivity evidence yet" reason on a11y-audit.ts and component-gallery-smoke.ts. tests/harness-registry.test.ts keeps record and source in step BOTH ways (a gate that does neither must carry a reason; a gate with such a reason must not pass fleetSlot/acquireHeavyGateSlot).

MUTANTS: order guard removed → drill RED on the message assertion (without it the call fails later as "no DevTools endpoint", the mis-attribution the message check exists to prevent); reason stripped from a non-taking gate → RED; reason added to a taking gate → RED.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE (stated in the commit): making a11y-audit/component-gallery-smoke load-sensitive. The turn is PAIRED with that declaration, and the declaration requires recorded run-history evidence those gates do not have — declaring them now would be a declaration without evidence and would make them wait for a quiet box on no basis. Their reasons point here, so gathering that evidence is the next step rather than a guess.

title: evalIn/evl swallow page-side exceptions: the shared CDP evaluate helper behind chrome-journeys (and a11y-audit before it) returns undefined for a throw, so a missing element reads as a product defect
description:
THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE CLASS, and the first two are what make this worth filing rather than noting.

The shape: a harness helper wraps Runtime.evaluate, returns the value, and never inspects exceptionDetails. A page-side throw therefore becomes undefined, the harness continues, and whatever assertion consumes the undefined reports a PRODUCT failure instead of an instrument failure.

INSTANCE 1 — FIXED (bead 4vfj, landed on main @ 5d51debf). scripts/a11y-audit.ts's local evl() did `return r?.result?.value`. Its own guard, `if (!t) throw new Error('no composer textarea')`, had been swallowed for the guard's whole life; four combobox checks then read ARIA attributes off a null element with ?. and reported {} — so a GATE inside test:all was red on main and the red looked like a broken WAI-ARIA contract. Repaired: evl surfaces the exception, the required elements throw, and the gate measures 40 passed / 0 failed (was 36 / 4).

INSTANCE 2 — FIXED (bead cwy2, on main @ 983706df). scripts/sidebar-parity.ts's evaluate() DID inspect exceptionDetails, but the probe itself read `.getBoundingClientRect()` off a null element, so the run died as an uncaught TypeError naming no selector and skipping all 20 checks. Repaired: a missing required control is a recorded, named check plus an abort that names the selector, and an aborted run still prints its summary.

INSTANCE 3 — OPEN, and it is the shared helper behind the strongest gate. scripts/chrome-journeys.ts:318-329:

    async function evalIn(cdp, session, expression) {
      const r = await withTimeout(cdp.send("Runtime.evaluate",
        { expression, returnByValue: true, awaitPromise: true }, session), 15000, "evalIn");
      return r?.result?.result?.value;
    }

No exceptionDetails. Every one of the suite's ~370 checks that reads the page through evalIn inherits the swallow. Also check the sibling helpers before fixing: boxOf (:367), clickSel (:394), typeInto (:445) all route through evalIn, and scripts/security-suite.ts's cdp.eval path plus its clickAt (:194-200, which does `.catch(() => null)`) are the same shape in a different file — clickAt turning a throw into `false` is precisely how the security gate's `composer:false` presented as a product state until the receipt was read.

WHY THIS IS NOT JUST TIDINESS: tonight two gates inside test:all were red on main and in BOTH cases the red was a missing element reporting itself as a product defect — once through a swallowed exception, once through an exit-124 timeout that our own canon told lanes to read as environmental. The swallow is what converts an instrument defect into a product accusation, and a product accusation sends the next lane to debug working code.

FIX SHAPE:
1. evalIn inspects exceptionDetails and throws with the page-side description, exactly as the a11y-audit repair now does. One place, ~4 lines.
2. But it must NOT be done blind: surfacing throws across ~370 checks will convert every latent swallowed throw into a visible failure at once. That is the point, and it is also why the change needs a QUIET-WINDOW drive of the whole suite before it lands — the suite is 370 sequential CDP round-trips, its registry entry records 370/370 only in an uninterrupted quiet window, and a run under load produces a verdict that means nothing (bead eo4d.1). Budget for a red run that names a dozen latent instrument defects, and treat each as a finding rather than as a regression.
3. Where a caller genuinely wants tolerance, make it explicit at the call site (`.catch(() => null)` with a comment saying why), never implicit in the helper.
4. The same pass should give the two multi-slash sites' pattern a home: an absent required element returns a NAMED diagnostic in the payload ({error: "composer input not found: <selector>"}), which works even while the helper swallows, and is what chrome-agent-platform-4vfj's latest branch does at :2699 and :2736.

ACCEPTANCE: evalIn surfaces a page-side exception with the description; npm run test:chrome driven in a quiet window with the verdict reported by count (n/370) and any newly-surfaced failure listed by check name and classified as instrument or product; no check silently downgraded to keep the count.

NOT MEASURED: I have not run test:chrome under this change or any other tonight — the box was not quiet (38 heavy build processes against CAP_QUIET_MAX_COMPILERS=1; bead dnop says that count is inflated by name-only matches on parked esbuild services). Everything above about instances 1 and 2 is measured with transcripts; everything about instance 3's blast radius is read from source and labelled as such.

title: chrome-journeys quiet-window gate can be held closed by fleet build concurrency alone — the two conditions fail independently
description:
Found taking the journey leg for chrome-agent-platform-muc. The gate refuses (exit 75, EX_TEMPFAIL) unless BOTH conditions hold, SUSTAINED 3x2s: load1/core <= 0.35 (CAP_QUIET_MAX_LOAD_PER_CORE) AND heavy compilers <= 1 (CAP_QUIET_MAX_COMPILERS), where heavy = rustc/cargo/cc1/ld/esbuild/ninja/make/wasm-opt/magick/ffmpeg. It waits CAP_QUIET_WAIT_MS (10 min) then refuses with an ENVIRONMENT: line and CAP_ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL.

TWO MEASURED REFUSALS, TWO DIFFERENT MECHANISMS — this is the finding, not the count:
1. 23:07-ish run: load1=9.09 (0.28/core) AND heavy-builders=4[esbuild] — both conditions failed.
2. 23:07:48 → 23:17:50 run (waited 601,839 ms): load1=5.70 (load/core 0.178) — LOAD WAS SATISFIED FOR THE WHOLE WINDOW — and heavy-builders=4[esbuild] kept it closed on the second condition alone. CAP_ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL {"at":1790115470233,"load1":5.7,"load5":9.9,"load15":13.56,"cores":32,"loadPerCore":0.178125,"compilers":4,"compilerNames":["esbuild"],"measurable":true}.
A third lane reproduced the refusal independently on the same evening. Logs: /tmp/muc-journeys.log and /tmp/muc-journeys2.log (lane machine), ~/cap-evidence for the retained copies.

WHY IT MATTERS: the obstacle is FLEET BUILD CONCURRENCY, not the machine and not any one branch. Any lane's esbuild bundle rebuild (a production build takes ~10s, and several lanes build all evening) can hold the journey gate closed for its whole 10-minute window, so the gate can be un-takeable while the fleet is working even on an idle machine. The reviewer hit the same wall on an unrelated branch, so this blocks landing, not one candidate.

WHAT A LANE MUST NOT DO (recorded so it is not rediscovered as a 'fix'): never kill, renice or otherwise interfere with another lane's processes to manufacture a quiet window — a lane that kills a peer's build to unblock its own test trades a real result for a convenient one and the peer only sees a failed build. Also do not raise CAP_QUIET_MAX_COMPILERS in a lane: running the journey under four builders tests a machine nobody ships on, and a green produced under conditions the declaration says are invalid is the defect class this repo spent the day cataloguing from the other direction.

OPTIONS (a policy call for the owner, per coord 2026-09-22): (a) serialise the journey and KAT legs across the fleet through a declared slot instead of competing for an emergent one; (b) raise the compiler cap deliberately and accept what such a run measures; (c) accept that the gate cannot be taken during fleet activity and schedule it for a quiet window — which may mean this leg never runs while the fleet is busy, and that is a real answer. Until it is decided, lanes sit on the window with a bound.

ACCEPTANCE for closing this bead: one of the three options is chosen and recorded with its rationale, and the chosen mechanism is verifiable — e.g. a declared slot the journey leg can actually acquire while other lanes build, or a stated schedule, or a documented threshold change with what it now proves. Evidence of the fix working: a journey run that STARTS (no exit 75) while at least one other build is in progress, or a recorded decision that says plainly this gate only runs on an idle fleet.

Related: chrome-agent-platform-muc (the candidate waiting on this leg), chrome-agent-platform-mkax/canon (the three-verdict rule and the load-sensitivity contract).

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND WHILE HOLDING THE WINDOW — and it is not fleet build concurrency. The gate counts a PARKED esbuild SERVICE DAEMON as a build.

MEASURED (holding the window for muc, ~/cap-evidence/muc/journey-window.log, sampled every 60s): machines went fully idle — load1 1.79-2.70, load/core 0.056-0.084 — while heavy=3[esbuild] persisted for 17+ consecutive samples, so builders_ok stayed 0 and the gate could never open. A 10-second CPU sample proves the three processes are NOT compiling: their accumulated CPU time did not move at all (0:41, 1:05, 0:33 across multi-day lifetimes).

The three, with ages and owners:
- pid 3569751, age 1d14h48m, parent `node ./node_modules/.bin/vite --host --port 5173`
- pid 1285365, age 2d00h34m, parent `isocan serve --foreground`
- pid 1438531, age 3d02h53m, parent `vite --port 5174 --strictPort --host`
All three are `.../@esbuild/linux-x64/bin/esbuild --service=0.28.2 --ping` — the long-lived esbuild SERVICE that Vite keeps open for its dev server. None is in this lane's tree, none is building anything, and none will exit on its own.

WHY: scripts/lib/quiet-window.ts:214-217 reads /proc/<pid>/comm and matches HEAVY_PROCESS_NAMES (line 44-47) — a NAME-ONLY match. It cannot distinguish an active compiler from a parked service that happens to share the binary name. The file's own comment (line 42) states the intent: a heavy process is one that 'starves CDP'. A daemon with flat CPU starves nothing, yet it holds the gate closed forever. The rule already knows how to exclude things that do not starve the browser (browsers and test workers are excluded deliberately) — a parked esbuild service belongs in that class.

CONSEQUENCE (supersedes the framing in the description): this is NOT 'the fleet is building so the journey cannot run'. While any lane leaves a Vite/dev-server esbuild service running — and the ones measured had been up for ONE TO THREE DAYS — the journey gate is permanently un-takeable on an idle machine, and waiting cannot help. Two independent lanes' refusals and both of mine are explained by one mechanism. It also means the load condition was never the blocker in the last two refusals: load_ok held; builders_ok never did.

OPTION (d), now the cheapest and most honest fix, to sit beside the policy options already recorded: count ACTIVE compilation rather than process-name presence — e.g. only count a HEAVY_PROCESS_NAMES process whose /proc/<pid>/stat CPU time advanced since the previous sample, or exclude `--service`/`--ping` esbuild servers the way browsers and test workers are excluded. Either keeps the declaration's intent intact (a real build still blocks the gate) and removes a blocker that is not doing any work. A lane must NOT do this unilaterally: it changes what a load-sensitive verdict means, so it needs the same policy decision as the other three options, with a mutant proving a genuinely compiling process still holds the gate closed (otherwise the fix would let the journey run under a real build — the exact condition the declaration exists to exclude).

EVIDENCE: ~/cap-evidence/muc/journey-window.log (full 60s series with load and builder counts), /tmp/muc-journeys.log and /tmp/muc-journeys2.log (the two gate refusals, exit 75, with CAP_ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL payloads).

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
IN_REVIEW — candidate pushed: fix/dnop-quiet-window-active-builds @ a2226ccd05015f5c2b1a4461236d627c065ef331 (remote verified). NOT landed; landing needs a verdict from someone who is not me.

CHOICE, stated as coord required: ACTIVITY, not names. The threshold counts name-matched processes whose accumulated CPU (utime+stime) advanced since the previous sample, or which were never seen before (fail closed — a build already running when the gate starts must still block it). A pid whose /proc/<pid>/stat starttime changed is a different process and counts active for the same reason. I deliberately did NOT add an esbuild '--service/--ping' special case: the activity rule is more faithful to the file's own intent and covers every parked compiler (a parked tsc/make/magick watch), while a name exclusion would fix exactly one binary. Name matches stay as evidence and the environment line now reports both: 'heavy-builders=4 active=0[esbuild]'. A sample with no activity information (hand-built/older caller) falls back to the name match — an unknown is never read as quiet.

LIVE PROOF, on the real box with the three parked daemons still running:
1. the gate WAITED while a real compile was active: 'quiet-window: waiting for a quiet box (bound 600000 ms) — active heavy-builders 4 > 1 (named: esbuild; compiling: esbuild)';
2. then it OPENED: 'quiet-window: box quiet after 10068 ms — load1=4.06 load5=4.86 cores=32 load/core=0.13 heavy-builders=4 active=0[esbuild]'.
Before this change the same box could never emit that second line. #1 is also the mutant coord asked for, live: with four esbuild named matches present, the moment one was genuinely compiling the gate still refused.

MUTANTS, both directions:
- a genuinely compiling process still holds the gate shut — the end-to-end test that used to copy /bin/sleep to rustc/esbuild/cargo (name-only load, i.e. the defect's own shape) now runs REAL esbuild compiles back to back and asserts exit 75 + CAP_ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL with activeCompilers >= 1;
- a parked daemon does NOT — the same test file drives the REAL sampler twice and asserts this test's own compiling pid is active via CPU advance while this test's own /bin/sleep-named pids are not. Every assertion is scoped to pids the test created, so another lane's build can neither pass nor fail it (p15i);
- pure-rule tests: advancing CPU → active, flat → idle, unseen pid → active, reused pid → active; and the /proc/<pid>/stat parse survives a comm with spaces and parentheses (a misparse there is the same defect in the arithmetic).

GATES, phases named: npm test at this tip — 16 serial (build/artifact) + 472 parallel files, 488 total, 4412 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored, wall 205s (serial 164s, parallel 40s). The quiet-window file itself: 18 passed / 0 failed.

CARRIED FINDING from the same run (recorded here because it is the next blocker, not this bead): with the gate fixed, chrome-journeys STARTED and reached 132/370 before aborting on 'cdp evaluate exceeded the budget under fleet load' — the qk7p environmental class, at load/core 0.13. So the quiet-window condition is necessary but was NOT sufficient for a full 370-check run under fleet load: the box measured quiet by this gate's predicate and the CDP cliff still fired ~8 minutes in. That strengthens the case for option (a) (serialise journey/KAT legs across the fleet through a declared slot) rather than for more threshold tuning.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
REVISE ADDRESSED — new candidate on the same branch: fix/dnop-quiet-window-active-builds @ 7efc78bd630889a93d3e149add181c68a514046d (remote verified; the previous tip a2226ccd is superseded). The sampler fix is untouched; only the two tests that prove it changed.

WHAT THE REVIEW FOUND IS ACCEPTED AS STATED: the mechanism was confirmed in source (activity not names, fail-closed on unseen processes, older callers falling back to the name count), and the two tests that PROVE it were measuring the machine as well as the code. A test whose result moves with the ambient daemon count or the box's compile speed is not portable, and the box is not part of the branch.

THE FIX, BY CONSTRUCTION RATHER THAN BY TUNING:
- calibratedBurner(dir, targetMs) measures a real compile on THIS box and scales the synthetic input until ONE compile outlasts the window the test needs; startCalibratedCompiler starts exactly one such process. The old fixed ~35 MB input was ~1.7 s here — and short enough on a faster box that the compile had already exited before the second sample (sampler test) or that a quiet gap opened BETWEEN two compiles (journey-gate test). Both tests now ASSERT the calibration covered the window (compileMs >= targetMs), so a box too fast to be covered fails loudly naming that reason instead of flaking.
- The sampler test asserts only about the pid IT started (the parked half already did) and its name-match assertions are LOWER BOUNDS over what the test created, never an exact count of the box.
- The journey-gate test keeps ambient parked daemons deliberately — the property is that a genuinely COMPILING process holds the gate whatever else the box runs — and with a calibrated burner that no longer depends on the box's speed.
- Both tests carry comments explaining the calibration and the pid-scoping, because the obvious simplification reintroduces a test that only passes at home.

PORTABILITY EVIDENCE (two ambient conditions, same result; the inputs no longer include the ambient count):
- 10 parked esbuild-named + 6 rustc-named idle processes (fixtures this session started): 18 passed / 0 failed, 15 s.
- after removing them (4 ambient esbuild, 0 rustc): 18 passed / 0 failed, 15 s.
npm test at the tip, phases named: 16 serial (build/artifact) + 473 parallel files, 489 total, 4422 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored, wall 202s.

HONEST LIMIT OF THIS REPAIR, so a re-review can judge it: I could NOT reproduce the reviewer's failure on this box, even with ~10 parked daemons and a completed /proc walk (a temporary truncation diagnostic never fired). So the calibration targets the most plausible mechanism — box speed — rather than a reproduced trace. If the two tests still red on the reviewer's box, their exact failure output is the next input and I will take it as the mechanism evidence rather than guessing again.

title: Curated agent templates suggest BACKGROUND recipes as skills, so the create dialog can only check part of the suggestion list
description:
Found while repairing scripts/kat-agent-templates.ts (chrome-agent-platform-za08) on the loaded extension.

Observed, measured in a real browser (fresh profile, create dialog): AgentTemplates' 'chief-of-staff' entry suggests five skills — daily-summary, weekly-digest, tab-hygiene, link-collector, meeting-prep — and the dialog checks exactly TWO rows. The other three suggest nothing and are silently absent from the selection.

Mechanism (source, not inference): the skills section can only CHECK a suggested id whose row exists in the profile's skill catalog (lib/agent-skill-rows.js checkTemplate → lib/recipes.js templateSkillMatches over the rows built from skill.list). In extension/lib/recipes.js those three ids are mode: BACKGROUND, and background recipes are scheduled templates — they are not rows in skill.list (measured: skill.list returned 34 entries; tab-hygiene and link-collector matched, the other three have no row). Result: a curated template advertises suggestions the owner cannot select, and the create dialog shows '2 selected' where the template's own data says five.

Why it matters: the template's suggested skills are a product promise (a starting point the owner can accept or edit). Three fifths of it silently does nothing, which is the same shape as the day's other defects — the UI reports success for a thing that did not happen.

Acceptance for done: either (a) the curated templates' suggested skills reference ids that exist as selectable skills, or (b) the create dialog renders a suggested-but-unavailable skill honestly (shown as unavailable with the reason, never silently missing), or (c) the template data and the claim are reconciled deliberately and documented. Whichever is chosen, a check in scripts/kat-agent-templates.ts must fail if a curated template suggests an id with no selectable row — do NOT weaken the existing mechanism check, which today asserts exactly the suggestions whose row exists are checked.

Evidence: ~/cap-evidence/za08-run6.log (NOTE line prints suggested/checkable/checked); the fixture's NOTE on every run reports the three lists. Related: chrome-agent-platform-za08 (the fixture repair that exposed it), chrome-agent-platform-l0r (recipes→skills rename, the same recipes/skills split).
close_reason: Landed on origin/main as v0.3.471 at commit 97a4f4261bdc0f72e9cef2d650b925ac87259eca. Unavailable template skill suggestions disclosed in agent config dialog; countLabel single-sourced; kat-agent-templates 43/43 passed in real browser.

The dialog (extension/ntp/ntp.js) mounts that host as a role="status" line under the skills list.

THE DATA PROBLEM IS NOT FIXED, and the bead says so in those words: the curated templates still name BACKGROUND recipes (daily-summary, weekly-digest, meeting-prep for chief-of-staff) that are not skills in the catalogue, so those suggestions still cannot be checked. Whether a template should suggest them at all is a data decision, unchanged here. Disclosure ≠ repair, and the two claims are kept apart.

TEST: tests/skill-catalog.test.ts (driving the real render path through the file's existing fake DOM) — two checkable skills + the chief-of-staff suggestion list → exactly two checked, the other three NAMED, count "3 suggested but unavailable"; an all-available template discloses nothing and adds no suffix; uncheckTemplate clears it. UPDATED TIP: feat/xiln-unavailable-suggestions @ 9f1885c63c0af362380f9260a5603d109ea8f349 (remote verified; 113902bd superseded), version 0.3.467. npm test at the tip: 4445 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored, 492 files, wall 231 s; worktree clean.

title: [bug] durable-root.test.ts mutates shared process env with /proc/cap-chp-impossible, racing dist-staleness-note in parallel suite
description: tests/durable-root.test.ts:69 sets CAP_DURABLE_ROOT=/proc/cap-chp-impossible as a process-global during its run. Because deno test --parallel runs test modules in a shared process, durableRoot() reads process.env live and causes racing tests (such as dist-staleness-note.test.ts) to fail with ENOENT: mkdir '/proc/cap-chp-impossible/...'. Reproducible ~1-in-3 running those two files in parallel. Isolate durable-root test env or restore cleanly with a lock/override.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
CANDIDATE: branch cap/m3a2-durable-root-env @ a51b739b5905ad7bb23d23741a2ea0ac9ee90700.
Root cause & Fix:
1. tests/durable-root.test.ts mutated process.env.CAP_DURABLE_ROOT in-process (e.g. to /proc/cap-chp-impossible, /tmp/cap-chp-must-refuse, /dev/shm/cap-chp-must-refuse), polluting shared process env under deno test --parallel and racing dist-staleness-note.test.ts and other suites.
2. Isolated all environment override test scenarios in tests/durable-root.test.ts into child processes via Deno.Command, ensuring parent process.env is never touched.
3. Verified race elimination: 50 consecutive parallel runs of tests/durable-root.test.ts and tests/dist-staleness-note.test.ts passed with 0 failures (previously failed ~1 in 4 runs).

title: test:changed fails closed to full suite for unimported scripts/** harnesses and unmapped bookkeeping JSON
description:
Root cause & measured behavior (reconciled across author measurements and independent review at 935ea3c2):

1. UNIMPORTED HARNESSES: Standalone harnesses under scripts/ (e.g. sidebar-parity.ts, a11y-audit.ts) are not imported by unit tests. Because scripts/select-tests.mjs uses static reverse-import reachability, unimported harness files trigger changedWithoutCoverage() fail-closed even though tree-inspecting guards (harness-registry, scripts-exit-codes, substring-pin-honesty, etc.) cover them. Directly imported harness libraries (like composer-target.ts) are covered.
2. UNMAPPED BOOKKEEPING JSON: The post-commit version hook bumps package.json, package-lock.json, and extension/manifest.json. These JSON files have no static importers in the reverse graph and are not covered by CONTENT_EXT_RE, triggering fail-closed on committed trees. (extension/lib/bundled-inventory-data.js is covered; the three JSON configs are not).
3. CONCURRENT TIP ADVANCE: changedFiles() compares against origin/main directly rather than the merge-base, so when origin/main advances, foreign landed files enter the working diff and contribute to fail-closed.

Acceptance:
1. Map unimported scripts/** harnesses to their inspecting guard suite (the dqc1 cross-cutting list) plus core instead of failing closed to 488 files.
2. Map version-only bookkeeping JSON diffs to the serial build/bootstrap/inventory suite.
3. Scope changedFiles() to merge-base so concurrent main landings do not pollute the changed set.
4. Fail-closed diagnostic message explicitly names which file/mechanism triggered the full suite fallback.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
CORRECTION FROM THE FILERS OWN SECOND MEASUREMENT — mechanism 1 in this bead's description is RETRACTED as stated, and the title was changed with it. I had labelled it 'derived from reading, not measured'; I have now measured a second change type and it does not hold.

RUN 2 (chrome-agent-platform-4vfj, worktree cap-4vfj-composer-hooks, base d0f01545, after commit + npm run build:production, /tmp/cap2-gates.log):

  select-tests: FAIL CLOSED - changed file(s) with no reachable test cannot be proved covered by a subset:
    scripts/a11y-audit.ts
  Running the FULL suite (npm test) instead.

ONE file. And .beads/interactions.jsonl
.beads/issues.jsonl
CHANGELOG.md
extension/lib/bundled-inventory-data.js
extension/manifest.json
package-lock.json
package.json
scripts/lib/harness-registry.ts
scripts/sidebar-parity.ts in that same worktree at that same moment returned CHANGELOG.md, extension/lib/bundled-inventory-data.js, extension/manifest.json, package-lock.json, package.json among others — i.e. all four of the version hook's bookkeeping files DID differ from origin/main and were NOT treated as uncovered. So the claim 'the hook bumps four import-unreachable files on every commit, therefore the subset is unreachable by construction after any commit' is FALSE. Those paths must resolve as covered (reachableTestFrom finds an importer, or CONTENT_EXT_RE/an earlier skip applies); I have not read which, and I am not going to assert a mechanism I did not verify twice.

WHAT BOTH MEASUREMENTS ACTUALLY AGREE ON:
- Mechanism 3 is the trigger, confirmed twice. Run 1 listed scripts/sidebar-parity.ts; run 2 listed scripts/a11y-audit.ts and NOTHING else. A harness under scripts/ is not imported by any unit test, so it can never be subset-covered, and scripts/** is what most lanes edit. Run 2 also proves the fix shape: scripts/lib/composer-target.ts, which a new test DOES import, was not listed — a harness lib with a test is subset-eligible.
- Mechanism 2 confirmed once, directly. Run 1 listed cap-evidence/constrained-width-layout.ts, which was bead cgei's landing and not my edit (coord confirmed filing it). changedFiles() runs  against the WORKING TREE, so when the base is behind the tip another lane's files enter your changed set. Run 2 was based on the tip, and its fail-closed list contained no foreign file.
- Mechanism 1's JSON listing in run 1 (extension/manifest.json, package-lock.json, package.json) is UNEXPLAINED and now conflicts with run 2. Same file class, opposite classification, different base. That instability is worth its own look: either the classification depends on the base in a way nobody intends, or run 1's tree state (two commits of version bumps plus a rebuild) put those files in a state run 2 did not. Labelled a hypothesis, not a finding.

RESTATED ACCEPTANCE, narrowed to what is measured: a scripts/** change with a tree-inspecting guard that covers it (the dqc1 list: harness-registry, scripts-exit-codes, substring-pin-honesty, durable-root, quiet-window, chrome-profile-isolation, machine-path-honesty, test-partition-guard) should select those guards plus the always-on core rather than the whole suite; the changed set should be scoped to the merge-base so another lane's landing cannot force your fail-closed; and the fail-closed message must name WHICH mechanism fired, because today 'no reachable test' reads identically for a harness nobody inspects, a config file, and a foreign landing. Cost of the status quo, measured twice in one evening on two-file harness repairs: 218s and 214s of full suite where AGENTS.md advertises 4-10s.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
THIRD MEASUREMENT, and it confirms the instability I had recorded only as a hypothesis — in the OPPOSITE direction from run 2, so the classification is now measured to be unstable in both directions.

RUN 3 (chrome-agent-platform-qdjn, worktree cap-qdjn-vacuity at cc2711fa, after commit dd83b990 + npm run build:production, /tmp/cap20-changed.log):

  select-tests: FAIL CLOSED - changed file(s) with no reachable test cannot be proved covered by a subset:
    extension/manifest.json
    package-lock.json
    package.json
  Running the FULL suite (npm test) instead.
  run-tests: 492 files total, wall 288s

The changed set here was ONE functional file, scripts/constrained-width-layout.ts, plus the post-commit hook's bookkeeping. The fail-closed list names ONLY the three bookkeeping files and does NOT name the scripts/** file — the exact inverse of run 2, where the list was scripts/a11y-audit.ts alone and the same three bookkeeping files differed from origin/main without being listed.

So, measured three times:
  run 1 (cwy2, base a3e35928 with main advanced): cap-evidence/constrained-width-layout.ts, extension/manifest.json, package-lock.json, package.json, scripts/sidebar-parity.ts
  run 2 (4vfj, base d0f01545 = tip):             scripts/a11y-audit.ts ONLY
  run 3 (qdjn, base cc2711fa = tip):             extension/manifest.json, package-lock.json, package.json ONLY

The same three release files are uncovered in runs 1 and 3 and covered in run 2, and the scripts/** file is uncovered in runs 1 and 2 and covered in run 3. My retraction of mechanism 1 was correct as a retraction of the STRONG claim ('every commit guarantees fail-closed'), but my run-2-based statement that those paths 'must resolve as covered' was too strong in the other direction: they resolve as covered SOMETIMES. The honest statement is that the classification of these paths is not stable across runs, and I have not established what it depends on.

Candidate explanations, all UNVERIFIED and listed so nobody adopts one as fact: the reverse-import graph may be built from the test files selected in the same pass, so which files are 'reachable' can depend on what else changed; a JSON file's reachability may depend on whether some test in the current selection imports it; or run 2's tree state (a rebuild plus a new test file that imports a lib) changed the graph enough to cover them. Distinguishing these needs reading buildReverseGraph in scripts/select-tests.mjs against all three trees, which I have not done.

What is unchanged and still the actionable part: the message does not say WHICH mechanism fired, so all three of these look identical to the lane reading them, and mechanism 3 (a scripts/** harness has no import-reachable test) is confirmed as the trigger in run 2 and as a non-trigger in run 3 — meaning a harness change does not reliably fail closed either. Cost measured again: 288s of full suite for a one-file harness change, against the 4-10s AGENTS.md advertises.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
Candidate pushed: branch cap-nco2-select @ 39314910d0238f86fc62a281663b65e5863073d4 (v0.3.476), based on origin/main 98cc8c8a. Main has since moved to 5e5fd815, which touches only .beads/issues.jsonl and CHANGELOG.md — zero overlap with my five files, so no rebase is owed.

THE TWO-SIDED MEASUREMENT IS NOW THREE-SIDED, AND IT SETTLES THE OPEN CONTRADICTION IN THIS BEAD. The description's mechanism-1 retraction, run 2's a11y-audit-only list, and run 3's bookkeeping-only list were read as the classification being UNSTABLE. It is not. Measured directly:
  • changedWithoutCoverage() is DETERMINISTIC at a given tree: three identical runs over the same probe set returned the same answer.
  • It is BASE-INDEPENDENT: at run 2's own tree (d0f01545) package.json, package-lock.json AND extension/manifest.json are all UNCOVERED — exactly as they are at 98cc8c8a. Run 2 did not see them classified differently; its CHANGED SET simply did not contain them at that moment.
So the instability was never in the classifier — it was in WHICH FILES ENTERED THE CHANGED SET, which is mechanism 3. That reconciles all three runs without any of them being wrong.

WHAT IS UNCOVERED, MEASURED AT 98cc8c8a (and the title's scope corrected): package.json, package-lock.json, extension/manifest.json, scripts/a11y-audit.ts, scripts/sidebar-parity.ts, scripts/constrained-width-layout.ts. COVERED: extension/lib/bundled-inventory-data.js, scripts/lib/composer-target.ts, scripts/lib/css-padding.ts, scripts/select-tests.mjs, scripts/test-partition.mjs. So it is NOT 'any scripts/** change' — it is precisely the files nothing imports. The reviewer's counterexample stands and the headline should say so.

WHY MAPPING THE HARNESS CLASS IS NOT A WEAKENING, measured: NO unit test EXECUTES those harnesses. For a11y-audit, sidebar-parity and constrained-width-layout, every test that so much as mentions them contains ZERO Deno.Command/spawnSync/execFileSync. The full suite therefore adds NOTHING for that class over the tree-walking guards — running 496 files instead of 28 was cost without coverage.

WHAT LANDED:
1. scripts/lib/changed-file-mapping.mjs — classifies an uncovered file and names what covers it. Version-only detection PARSES BOTH SIDES and compares flattened key paths; it never greps for lines containing "version", which is the mo2f.3 trap (that filter passes a nested dependency bump exactly as cleanly as a project bump).
2. scripts/select-tests.mjs — maps the two provable classes, scopes the changed set to the MERGE-BASE, and every fail-closed run now NAMES the file and the mechanism. Real output: 'select-tests: extension/manifest.json has no importer — version-only bookkeeping JSON (the post-commit hook's bump); selecting its 5 inspecting guard(s).'
3. tests/changed-file-mapping.test.ts — 9 tests.
4. AGENTS.md + docs/CHROME-TEST-CONTRACT.md updated.

MEASURED BEFORE/AFTER on a real commit: BEFORE (pristine picker at 98cc8c8a, same changed set) = FULL_SUITE, fail closed on the three bookkeeping files. AFTER = 22 files for a bookkeeping-only change, 28 for an unimported harness, 149 for my own multi-file commit — against a 496-file suite.

MY OWN TEST CAUGHT TWO UNJUSTIFIED MAPPINGS, and I removed the mappings rather than the assertion: changelog-shipping.test.ts references NO bookkeeping file (it reads .gitignore, build.mjs and the packaging scripts) and build-bootstrap.test.ts matched only on the 'dist-versions' directory name. A guard that does not read the file cannot be its coverage. The assertion now requires the exact literal path.

CAP-ASTRA'S CAVEAT (seq89) IS ASSERTED, NOT TRUSTED: root-only normalization must not suppress a real CSP or nested dependency change. Tested against the REAL manifest — version-only bump maps (true); version bump + weakened CSP does NOT (false); version bump + added 'debugger' permission does NOT (false); nested dependency bump does NOT (false).

FALSIFICATION — two mutants, each killed by its intended assertions: M1 replace the parse with a line-grep → 3 tests red, including 'a weakened CSP must force the full suite' and the nested-dependency case. M2 revert merge-base scoping to the moving tip → 1 red, 'uses the merge-base when git resolves one'. Both restored green.

A PROCESS ERROR I MADE AND FIXED, recorded because it is the same class the repo has been bitten by: I issued the commit and the mutant-plant in the SAME parallel block, so the commit captured the mutant — HEAD contained 'return base; // MUTANT' while my working tree had the real function. Caught by reading git diff rather than trusting the commit, fixed by amending with hooks disabled so the version did not double-bump. AGENTS.md's ady6 rule is 'commit first, THEN mutate'; running them concurrently violates it just as surely as running them out of order.

GATES at the pushed sha: full npm test 4472 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored, 496 files, exit 0, both phases GREEN — and all NINE nco2 tests verified BY NAME inside that run (the parallel phase prefixes each with its file path; my first grep for '^nco2' returned 0 and I checked that rather than reporting it).

HONEST GATE FAILURE TO DECLARE: npm run test:changed exited 1 TWICE before that, and I am naming the checks rather than absorbing them. Run 1: 4 failed — 'az4k detector honesty...' (bundled-tools-job-lane-tier.test.ts:90), 'gzip retained Worker...' and 'gzip admission census...' (gzip-preview.test.ts:196,209), 'Unix tools: all nine exact executable IDs...' (unix-tools-admission.test.ts:86). Run 2: 1 failed, the same gzip Worker check. ALL FOUR are 'NotFound: readfile extension/wasm/cas/<sha>.wasm' — missing binaries, never assertion failures. Attribution, measured: all 38 CAS blobs exist and are tracked; the exact requested hash resolves; each test passes in isolation on this exact tree (gzip 8/0) and on the canonical checkout (unix-tools 6/0); NONE of them comes from my mapping (all three are selected by the IMPORT GRAPH via bundled-inventory-data.js, so they were selected before my change too); and the CAS directory's mtime is 22:36:43 — INSIDE my parallel phase, with my build finishing at 22:34:33. So something regenerated the shared CAS tree mid-run. 4 → 1 → 0 across three runs is a race, not a deterministic red, and the full suite is green at the same sha. I am NOT claiming it is fully diagnosed: what is measured is the mtime overlap and the non-attribution to my change.

Needs a different-model-family verdict; merger owns landing.

title: No test executes ntp.js: source-scanning suites miss real UI regressions
description:
Systemic gap found during 7zf0 triage and review: no test in this repository executes ntp.js directly in a test environment. Over 68 test files source-scan ntp.js with Deno.readTextFile or regex matchers (e.g. task-inline-edit-and-panel.test.ts, route-focus.test.ts, agent-deletion-navigate.test.ts).

Two concrete examples of the failure mode:
1. agent-deletion-navigate.test.ts tests navigation state by re-implementing an inline simulation of the router logic rather than executing ntp.js, so ntp.js can regress while the test stays green.
2. 7zf0 regression test: when extension/ntp/ntp.js was reverted to main, 3 of 4 tests in agent-header-rename-reload.test.ts still passed because the 'behavioral' tests executed an inline simulation instead of the actual script, leaving the regex source-pin as the only failing assertion.

Demonstration: tests reading text can verify presence of tokens, but cannot falsify runtime behavior, race conditions, event ordering, or DOM state transitions in ntp.js. ntp.js needs real browser-driven harness or headless page execution tests for its core state machines and route transitions.

2. The BOOT ROUTE is executed too. ntp.js calls bootNtpRoutes() at module scope (:4991), which awaits applyCurrentHashRoute(false). The 'reload parity at #thread' test sets (globalThis).location = { hash: '#thread=<id>' } and history.state BEFORE the import, so the thread-route restore genuinely runs and is asserted (4 turns restored, title restored).

WHAT SURVIVES, and it is worth fixing: THE AGENT-ROUTE STATE MACHINE HAS NO EXECUTION COVERAGE THAT RUNS WITHOUT CHROME FOR TESTING. Measured: '#agent=' appears ZERO times in all three executing tests and twice in the browser test. openAgentSurface (:2705), openAgentChat (:2765), revalidateOpenAgent (:4342) and navigateNtpRoute are named ONLY by source-scanning tests. MY DEFAULT, proceeding unless redirected: add an EXECUTING test for the agent-route surface using the same house DOM + chrome-stub pattern the three existing executors use — set location.hash = '#agent=named:<id>' and history.state to a STALE name, execute the real ntp.js, and assert the boot route resolves the fresh persisted name into #thread-title and history.state. I am also correcting the title's scope in this comment rather than silently: the defect is 'the agent-route state machine is executed only by a skippable browser test', not 'no test executes ntp.js'.

title: scripts/sidebar-parity.ts crashes on main: the hub composer selectors drifted (#task-input/#run-task) and a null probe skips all 20 checks
description:
MEASURED on unmodified origin/main @ a3e35928 (worktree /home/paulkinlan/worktrees/cap-sidebar-parity, npm ci + deno install + build:production done):

  npm run test:sidebar
  error: Uncaught (in promise) Error: TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getBoundingClientRect')
      at <anonymous>:1:55   (scripts/sidebar-parity.ts:81 evaluate -> :156)
  exit=1, ZERO checks run, no SIDEBAR PARITY summary line.

The registry row still reads "18/2 at the re-inventory (two sidebar parity checks red); promote once green" (scripts/lib/harness-registry.ts:85). That is stale: the harness does not reach its checks at all today, so the hub's Tasks/Agents sidebar parity (expanded / collapsed / RTL / dark geometry, hover + keyboard delete, New-task focus) has NO running browser coverage.

ROOT CAUSE (measured with a read-only CDP probe on the loaded hub, ntp.html):
  agent-composer textarea#task-input -> false
  document.querySelector('#task-input') -> false
  document.querySelector('#run-task')   -> false
  #composer [data-composer-input]       -> true
  #composer [data-composer-send]        -> true
  the textarea's real id is "composer-input"
The composer renders per-instance ids (`${this.id}-input` / `${this.id}-send`) and exposes the stable hooks data-composer-input / data-composer-send for exactly this purpose (extension/shared/components.js:7035). The same drift was measured independently by the astra lane in bead chrome-agent-platform-b5q4 for cap-evidence/model-edit-still-refused-journey.ts; scripts/chrome-journeys.ts already carries a compat fallback in boxOf() (#task-input -> [data-composer-input], #run-task -> [data-composer-send]). sidebar-parity.ts never got it.

SECOND DEFECT, same class (found after the selector repair): the run then aborted with "TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')" at the `thread.list` probe (`.then(r=>r.threads.length)`). The dispatcher answers a throwing handler with {ok:false,error,...} (service-worker.js onMessage catch), which has no `threads` key. Reading `.length` off that is an anonymous crash that names neither the route nor the error. Sibling harnesses already defend with `?.threads?.length ?? 0`.

WHY THIS IS A CLASS, NOT A ONE-OFF: an uncaught TypeError in a probe aborts the whole harness, so every later check silently never runs and the printed output names no selector. That is the probe-null family this repo has already paid for twice (bead 4a44 "probes measure null/0 - the parity checks have never passed in a real browser run"; bead rfca "Settings browser gates assert visibility, not rendered content"). A harness that cannot see its element must record a NAMED red and say how much of it never ran.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. npm run test:sidebar reaches its checks and prints its SIDEBAR PARITY summary on current main. No uncaught TypeError.
2. The composer probes use the component's stable hooks, scoped to the hub composer (#composer [data-composer-input] / [data-composer-send]) - not the per-instance ids, and not a bare document-wide [data-composer-input] (ntp.html has a second composer, #thread-composer).
3. A missing/zero-sized required control is a recorded, named check failure AND an abort that names the selector; a non-array thread.list reply names the raw reply.
4. An aborted run still prints the summary line with the abort counted as a failure (exit non-zero) - the reader always learns how much ran.
5. Any check that is red AFTER the instrument is repaired is reported honestly as a product finding (or filed as its own bead), not quietly deleted. The harness must not be weakened to go green.
6. scripts/lib/harness-registry.ts:85 reason updated to the newly measured pass/fail count (docs never drift).

GATES: the harness run itself (transcript retained), npm run test:changed, npm test once before push, tests/scripts-exit-codes.test.ts + tests/harness-registry.test.ts still green (the script keeps a failure-derived Deno.exit and exactly one registry class).

FALSIFICATION: reverting the selector to #task-input must reproduce the crash; the new named check must go red when the composer hook is renamed.
close_reason: Landed on origin/main @ 983706df (v0.3.451). Migrated sidebar-parity to [data-composer-input]/[data-composer-send] hooks; 20 checks execute (19 pass / 1 fail owned by o1y1). Full two-phase suite green (16 serial + 471 parallel = 487 files, 4404 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored, wall 226s).

title: The changelog jargon filter does not cover the internal words that actually leak
description:
Measured 2026-09-22 on branch cap/mcp-harness-tools.

JARGON_RE (extension/options/changelog-filter.js, mirrored in scripts/bump-version.mjs as FILTER_JARGON_RE) is:
  /journey|KAT|assertion|CDP|harness|worktree|lane|tracker|splice/i

A changelog entry reading 'correct my own capability claim — NO pinned adapter implements client-hosted MCP' PASSED that filter and was written to CHANGELOG.md. It is first person, internal, and states no consequence for a person reading a release note. The words that leaked — 'capability claim', 'pinned adapter', 'client-hosted', 'MCP' — are none of them in the alternation, so the filter was green on a sentence no user could act on.

This is the mechanism that is supposed to catch internal vocabulary reaching a user-facing changelog, and it passed a first-person internal sentence. It was caught by a human reading the note, not by the gate.

Acceptance: the filter (or a check over it) rejects first-person engineering prose and the leaked vocabulary above, with a test that FAILS on the exact sentence quoted here. A refusal must NAME the offending word — the same defect was filed earlier for the filter's failure to name its cause.

title: check-reachability sees files with no importer, but not exported functions with no caller
description:
Measured 2026-09-22 on branch cap/mcp-harness-tools.

scripts/check-reachability.mjs failed the build on two shipped MODULES that no entry point imports:
  lib/harness-mcp-server.js: shipped but nothing reaches it (delete it, or add it to RETAINED with a reason)
  lib/harness-tool-provider.js: shipped but nothing reaches it
That is correct and it was right to fail.

But the same guard cannot see a FUNCTION that nothing calls inside a file that IS reached. scripts/acp-bridge.ts exported isBrowserLaunchingMcpServer with a full JSDoc block and 11 passing assertions in tests/acp-bridge-mcp-isolation.test.ts, and no caller anywhere in the repository. Its comment even claimed the load-bearing half was a symbol (capMcpServerEntry) that exists nowhere in the repo and had died with a deleted module, while a comment thirty lines below described a different and incompatible safety model. Two safety models attached to a function nobody calls, and the build was green.

Same shape as today's other findings: a check that reports on the class NEXT TO the one that matters. The file-level guard makes dead modules impossible and dead exported functions invisible.

Acceptance: either extend the reachability check to report exported symbols with no importer/caller (allowing a tested exemption list with reasons), or state in docs/TEST-COUPLING-INVENTORY.md that this class is uncovered and why. Prefer the first.

comments.text: IMPLEMENTED (v1) — branch cap/glm-kf3h-reachability @ 2e0a7483 pushed (off main a12f887ce). check-reachability.mjs gains scanExportedFunctionReachability() + exportedFunctions(): top-level export function / export async function declarations across the REACHED modules, caller scan over the shipped package only (tests/ is not shipped — a function whose only caller is its own test is dead by definition, the bead's exact example). RETAINED_EXPORTS is the explicit exemption inventory with reasons; rot (export returns/disappears) is reported like RETAINED's. Refinement (measured): same-file internal composition counts as use — the first scan produced 197 raw findings that were mostly internal-composition false positives (e.g. resolveSkillContext feeding runAcpTaskTurn); after the refinement a 17-module sample still shows 92 findings for triage (sample: ~/cap-evidence/kf3h-scan-sample.json). The v1 gate does NOT block — it is a scan for triage; promoting it to a blocking gate needs the 92 findings triaged (fix/cut/exempt with reasons) and the same-file-recursion limitation accepted (documented in tests). TESTS (reachability.test.ts, 10/0): declaration discovery (order/dedupe/comments/arrow-const scope), dead detection, another-file caller clears, exemption keeps + rot reports. The v1 limitation (same-file references including pure self-recursion count as internal use) is stated in the test name and comments per the honesty canon. title: Two latent checks that cannot fail: a once-taken non-vacuity guard reused per width, and an absent label reading as un-clipped
description:
Found by the independent review of cap/l3ts-check-strength (ac0a62d4), in cap-evidence/constrained-width-layout.ts. Both are the same "cannot fail" class as q264/qzae/cgei, stated as LATENT because the reviewer could identify the hole at the predicate level but could NOT reach it from the driver's current probes. Not fixed by that branch.

(1) THE NON-VACUITY GUARD IS TAKEN ONCE, AT ONE WIDTH, AND REUSED FOR ALL OF THEM.
  Line 422-430 computes panelHasButtons from panelResults["300"] ONLY:
    const panelHasButtons = !panelResults["300"].error && panelResults["300"].buttons.length > 0;
    check("side panel: the harness buttons rendered", panelHasButtons, ...);
    check("...guard...", panelHasButtons && panelResults["300"].containerVisible === true &&
      panelResults["300"].buttons.every((b) => b.w > 0 && b.h > 0), ...);
  That single boolean then gates the loop at line 480 (`if (panelHasButtons) { for
  const w of PANEL_WIDTHS) ... }`), while the checks INSIDE the loop iterate
  `r.buttons` unguarded, per width.

  CONSEQUENCE: a probe returning `buttons: []` at some width w yields THREE
  vacuous passes at that width - line 485 `.every(...)` on [], line 494
  `.every(...)` on [], line 497 `.every(...)` on [] - because the guard that would
  have caught it was taken at 300px and never re-taken at w. The guard reads as
  covering the loop; it does not.

  FIX SHAPE: take the guard PER WIDTH inside the loop, on `r.buttons.length > 0`,
  rather than once outside it.

(2) AN ABSENT LABEL IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM AN UN-CLIPPED ONE.
  Line 351: const labelClipped = label ? getComputedStyle(label).clip !== "auto" : false;
  If `.hq-label` is missing entirely, labelClipped is false. The new collapsed-rule
  check (line 494) asserts `b.labelClipped === expectClipped` with expectClipped
  = (w < 320). At 400px expectClipped is false, so a MISSING LABEL SATISFIES IT.
  It fails CLOSED at 260/300px (expectClipped true, so a missing label is RED), so
  this is SINGLE-DIRECTION ONLY: the 400px direction is satisfied by absence, the
  collapsed directions are not.

  FIX SHAPE: carry a `hasLabel` boolean in the probe and require it, so absence is
  RED in both directions rather than green in one.

ACCEPTANCE: for (1) a probe with an empty button list goes RED at every width, not
only at 300px; for (2) a chip with no .hq-label goes RED at 400px as well as at
260px. Both proofs recorded, and each shown passing when the defect is present so
the check is not itself vacuous.

The two post-loop 260px checks read collapsed.buttons from OUTSIDE the loop and carried the same hole, so they are guarded too — same defect, same fix, one line each.
(2) The probe now carries hasLabel: !!label explicitly and the collapsed-rule check requires it (b.hasLabel && b.labelClipped === expectClipped), so a missing .hq-label is red in BOTH directions instead of passing as "leaves the label visible" at 400px.

Evidence: ~/cap-evidence/qdjn-falsification/{run-mutants.sh,fixed-m1,prefix-m1,fixed-m2,prefix-m2}.{log,summary}.

  M1 — probe returns buttons: [] at 400px ONLY, leaving 300px intact so the outer panelHasButtons guard still opens the loop (this is the exact scenario the bead describes: the guard samples 300 and never looks at the width that broke):
    PREFIX (pre-fix): 46 passed / 0 FAILED, exit 0. All four .every() checks passed on an empty array at 400px. THE DEFECT, DEMONSTRATED — a green suite with nothing rendered at that width.
    FIXED:            44 passed / 1 FAILED, exit 1, and the one red is
      "panel 400px: the harness buttons rendered (per-width non-vacuity guard)" {"count":0,"error":null}
      — naming the width AND the count. The four downstream checks are skipped rather than recorded as vacuous passes, which is why the total is 45 of 49 and not 49.

  M2 — .hq-label never found (probe selector mutated to .hq-label-QDJN-MUTANT), so labelClipped falls back to false everywhere:
    PREFIX (pre-fix): 44 passed / 2 FAILED — red at 260px and 300px, and
      "PASS  panel 400px: the collapsed rule leaves the label visible" — THE SINGLE-DIRECTION HOLE, DEMONSTRATED: a missing label satisfied the 400px direction exactly as the bead predicted.
    FIXED:            46 passed / 3 FAILED — red at 260px, 300px AND
      "FAIL  panel 400px: the collapsed rule leaves the label visible (the container query does not fire)"
      So absence is now red in both directions, which is acceptance (2) verbatim.

Both acceptance proofs are therefore recorded, and each is shown PASSING when the defect is present.

GATES, stated exactly rather than rounded up:
  npm run build:production rc=0; npm run check:dist clean at HEAD; deno check on the harness clean.
  npm run test:changed and npm test BOTH EXIT 1 — but NOT from this change, and I verified that rather than asserting it. Three failures, all reproduced at a PRISTINE checkout of cc2711fa in a clean worktree with this branch's change absent:
    tests/components.test.ts: two diay segmented-control checks, "the activated tab must be scrolled into view exactly once, got 0" at components.test.ts:1147 — and GREEN at 61e4fdab, the commit before muc. Filed as chrome-agent-platform-0rw5 (P1) with the attribution: muc refactored extension/shared/components.js (+130) without touching components.test.ts, regressing the fix diay landed at c80b8abc two commits earlier.
    tests/agent-header-rename-reload.test.ts: the 7zf0 real-browser rename-then-reload check — verified pre-existing at pristine cc2711fa, NOT attributed (candidates: muc's +175 lines in ntp.js, or load sensitivity; distinguishing them needs a quiet window I did not have).
  This change cannot affect any of the three: it touches only scripts/constrained-width-layout.ts, and ZERO tests import that file (git grep for an import or new URL reference returns 0; the only mention is a comment at tests/css-padding.test.ts:4). So I am NOT claiming a green full suite — main is not green — and I am reporting the exact check names instead, as instructed.

NOT FIXED HERE, REPORTED INSTEAD: the "long registered name (stress)" loop does `if (!b) { console.log("(no button)"); continue; }`, so a width with no button silently SKIPS its three checks. Different shape from this bead's two — absent coverage rather than a vacuous pass — and it does print a line, so it is visible in the transcript rather than silent. title: Evaluate MCP Zod peer unification with schema parity tests
description: azlc audit found SDK1.30.0 peer contexts bind Zod3.25.76 and Zod4.4.3. zod-to-json-schema3.25.2 also binds these different peers; total emitted preminify converter contribution 2460 bytes, not the large source-input sum. EVALUATION COMPLETE (cap-gemini, 2026-09-25).
BRANCH: cap/gemini-mx1g-zod-peer, COMMIT: ac260948d (pushed to origin).
EVIDENCE: cap-evidence/mx1g-zod-peer-parity/EVIDENCE.md.
TESTS: tests/mcp-zod-peer-parity.test.ts (7 tests, all green).

FINDINGS & RECOMMENDATION: RETAIN SEPARATE PEER CONTEXTS (DO NOT UNIFY).
1. Emitted Converter Size: Despite 78 files / 108.5 KB source in zod-to-json-schema, tree-shaking in the production service worker bundle limits its emitted preminify contribution to EXACTLY 2,460 bytes. Deduplication yields negligible byte savings.
2. Silent Conversion Failure on Zod 4: zod-to-json-schema@3.25.2 only parses Zod 3 AST (_def.typeName); passed a Zod 4 schema it fails silently and emits an empty schema ({ "$schema": "..." }) with 0 properties.
3. Downstream Error Formatting Incompatibility: Zod 4 omits issue.received and issue.type; CAP's validationIssueDetail in extension/lib/lazy-tool-protocol.js relies on issue.received and degrades to 'must be string; received undefined' under Zod 4.
4. Mixed Shape Rejection: MCP SDK objectFromShape throws 'Mixed Zod versions detected in object shape.' when Zod 3 and Zod 4 are mixed.
5. Early v4-mini Constraint Drops: zod@3.25.76/v4-mini drops minLength/maxLength/minimum/maximum/description checks, whereas Zod 3 preserves them.

All gates clean: test:file (7/7 passed), test:changed (500 files, 4509 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored).

THE A/B, RUN FIRST AS THE BEAD REQUIRED ("Reproduce controlled A/B before attributing"): same real
adapter (claude-agent-acp), two arms, 60 s prompt deadline, with a DELIBERATELY INVALID key so no
secret is read or needed (cap-evidence/5f5u/ab-drill.ts):
  A_no_key:       promptAnswered=false timedOut=true callbacks=3 60002ms
  B_invalid_key:  promptAnswered=false timedOut=true callbacks=3 60001ms
IT DID NOT REPRODUCE THE DIFFERENCE — both arms stalled identically, and BOTH reported
`apiType=native baseUrl=native`, so in this harness the key never became the auth source at all. The
attribution therefore stays OPEN on the bead, and nothing here claims to fix a stall.

SO THE FIX IS JUSTIFIED BY THE WARNING THAT WAS ACTUALLY CAPTURED, not by the unreproduced story. The
adapter's own stderr says an auth source "takes precedence over your claude.ai login". Two consequences
follow whatever the stall's cause turns out to be, and both are implemented:
  1. SCOPE the overriding source out of the ADAPTER CHILD env (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY by default), never
     from the host, never from disk, reversible with CAP_ACP_KEEP_API_KEY=1 — the bead is explicit:
     "Preserve host settings/credentials; do not auto-delete user API keys." There is a test asserting
     the caller's environment object is NOT mutated, and one asserting the note never echoes a value.
  2. SURFACE the adapter's precedence warning as an actionable host-side line, because a precedence
     change visible only in a child's stderr is invisible in the surface the user watches.
Both spawn sites are covered: the WebSocket bridge (which spread the host env into the child) and the
native host (which passed NO env at all, so the adapter inherited everything).

AND THE INTEGRATION CHECK CAUGHT MY OWN FIX LYING. The bridge printed "CAP scopes it out of the adapter
child", while an adapter that prints its own environment reported `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: PRESENT` — the
note claimed a mechanism that was not happening, and the unit tests were green because they tested the
helper, not the wiring. Cause, MEASURED rather than assumed: Deno MERGES `env` over the parent's
environment by default, so omitting a variable does not remove it. `clearEnv: true` is what scopes a
child, and that is now asserted by a test that spawns a real child twice — PRESENT with the default,
ABSENT with clearEnv — so deleting the line reds a test instead of shipping a false claim again.

VERIFIED END TO END with a real bridge, a real WebSocket client and an adapter that reports what it
sees: default -> the host-side note AND `ADAPTER_SEES: ABSENT`; with CAP_ACP_KEEP_API_KEY=1 ->
`ADAPTER_SEES: PRESENT`, so a user who relies on the key keeps today's behaviour.

title: A client-supplied cwd that does not exist on the bridge host fails silently several machines from the cause
description:
Found by coord from Paul's Mac (2026-09-18), after the 7p7e fix was on disk and the error persisted: "Invalid params: `cwd` does not exist on the machine running the agent: `/Users/paulkinlan/journal`".

## The gap
7p7e stopped the bridge INVENTING a cwd ($HOME/journal only when the directory is really there). This is the other half: when the **CLIENT** supplies a cwd that does not exist on the bridge's own host, the bridge says **nothing**. The path travels to the adapter, the adapter reports an ACP-level "Invalid params", and the user is left to work out which of three machines disagreed. Same shape as the harness mismatch before `lpmv`: a real conflict reported far from its cause.

Paul's cwd most likely came from **our own instruction** — the journal's "launch all agent work from the journal root", which is right for agents on this box and wrong as a client setting on a laptop. Fourth time today a fleet assumption has landed on somebody else's machine.

## Wanted: a warning, not a rejection
When a session frame arrives with a cwd that does not exist on this host, print a line naming **the path, the host, and the fact that the client supplied it** — distinct from the bridge defaulting, which 7p7e handles by not inventing anything. **Never override the client's choice** (authoritative for its own session); make the disagreement legible where someone can act on it. `harnessCliWarning` is the model: same shape, same prominence, same refusal to guess, and emitted **once per path** rather than per frame.

## Precondition for the receipt (neither 7p7e nor its verification covered this)
A **client that sends a cwd the bridge host does not have** — constructed explicitly: drive the bridge with a frame carrying `/no/such/place` and assert (a) the warning names the path and host, (b) the adapter receives **the client's** path unchanged, (c) the warning is not repeated for the same path.

Acceptance: `clientCwdWarning(frame, { exists })` returns the warning for a nonexistent client cwd, `[]` for an existing one, `[]` for a frame with no cwd, and `[]` for non-session methods; the bridge prints it once per path at the frame-forwarding site; the client's cwd is never substituted.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
FIXED — branch `fix/acp-cwd-delete-journal-default`, two commits: `f3f5f4a4` (delete the default) + `87a9ef7d` (the sweep and the client-cwd diagnostic). v0.3.437. Independent verification wanted; I wrote the code and found the regression below.

## The diagnostic, as asked (warning, never a rejection)
`clientCwdWarning(raw, { exists, host })` prints, at the frame-forwarding site, once per path:

```
[acp-bridge] WARNING: the client asked for cwd "/no/such/place", which does not exist on THIS host (bridge-host-1) —
[acp-bridge]          the adapter will refuse it with "Invalid params". The client's choice is passed
[acp-bridge]          through unchanged (this bridge never substitutes one): fix it in the client's own
[acp-bridge]          settings, or install this service with --cwd if the host should declare it.
```

It carries **no knowledge of any directory convention** — only the fact that two machines disagree. Returns `[]` for an existing directory, for a frame with no cwd, for non-session methods, and for unparseable frames.

## The precondition, constructed explicitly
A **client that sends a cwd the bridge host does not have**: the drive test starts a real bridge on the fake adapter, opens a WebSocket, sends `session/new` with `cwd: "/no/such/place"` **twice**, and asserts (a) the warning appears **once**, (b) it names the path and the disagreement, (c) the fixture log shows the adapter received `/no/such/place` **unshanged** — the never-substitute half. Mutants, each run where its assertion lives: substitution → reds (UNSHANGED); the warning's own words removed → reds (`does not exist on THIS host`); per-frame instead of per-path → reds (count 2); no `exists()` check → reds (false-positive unit case).

## And the part that matters most: the sweep found a MACHINE-DEPENDENT PIN
Deleting the `$HOME/journal` default reddened `tests/acp-runner.test.ts`, because line 205 asserted the adapter received `${HOME}/journal`:

> `assertEquals(newSession.msg.params.cwd, \`${home}/journal\`, "the adapter received the host-side default cwd")`

So the harness's own suite **enforced this fleet's directory convention**, which means the guarded version's green gate was machine-dependent: it passed here, where `~/journal` exists, and **would have failed on Paul's Mac** — the same class as the bug. The fix is not to restore anything but to let the caller *declare*:

- `createAcpServer(port, adapter, env, hostCwdDefault)` — the host cwd is now a **declared argument** (the CLI's `--cwd` for the service, an explicit value for a test or probe). Detection is gone from the API, not only from the default.
- The runner test creates its own scratch directory, passes it, and asserts the adapter received **that** — the wiring stays pinned, the convention does not.
- `tests/acp-end-to-end.test.ts` now **requires** `CAP_ACP_CWD` instead of falling back to `$HOME/journal` — that fallback is literally the default that produced Paul's error.
- `cap-evidence/acp-multiharness-probe.ts` refuses with a message instead of guessing; the host-defaults test header no longer reads as a rule. (Left alone deliberately: `FALSIFICATION.md`, which is a historical record of the old behaviour, and `memory.get … key: "journal"` — the agent's journal, a product concept.)

## Verified
`test:changed` exit 0 on the committed bytes: **4392 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored**, parallel phase 470 files GREEN. Count went **up** by the two new tests, not down. ACP suites together: runner 22/0 (was 20/2 on this branch and 22/0 on main — the pin was inheriting the convention), host-defaults + end-to-end + harness-default + doctor 49/0.
