title: [bug] Hub agent header: a named-agent.list correction that lands before openAgentSurface's history await is overwritten by the stale name
description:
FOUND while building the 32yz execution coverage. NOT reproduced in a real browser — filed as an ordering QUESTION with its measurement, not as a confirmed product defect, and deliberately not asserted in tests/ntp-agent-route-execution.test.ts.

WHAT WAS MEASURED (Deno, house DOM + chrome stub, real extension/ntp/ntp.js executed):
openAgentSurface has TWO writers of the agent header.
  • :2714-2723 — the named-agent.list callback: if a.name differs from threadTitle.textContent it corrects BOTH the header and history.state.
  • :2752-2758 — after 'const history = await loadAgentSurfaceHistory(kind, id)', the function unconditionally assigns 'threadTitle.textContent = name || \"Agent\"', where 'name' is the value the CALLER passed in.
When the list reply arrives BEFORE that await settles, the callback's correction is applied and then OVERWRITTEN by the stale caller-supplied name. Measured with a microtask-speed stub reply: TITLE ended \"ZZZ Stale History Name\" while history.state.name was \"ZZZ Fresh Persisted Name\" — the two surfaces DISAGREED, header stale, history fresh. With a 40 ms reply the correction survives and both read fresh.

WHY THIS MIGHT NOT BE REAL, stated plainly: a microtask-speed sendMessage reply is a stub artefact. But 'impossible in a browser' is a claim I have NOT verified, and the ordering is not obviously unreachable: named-agent.list is issued FIRST (:2714) while the history read is issued later (:2752), so the list winning the race is plausible. Both are IPC.

WHY IT MAY BE UNREACHABLE ANYWAY: the divergence only matters when named-agent.get and named-agent.list DISAGREE about the name. In the product's own flow both read the same store, so a disagreement needs a stale cache or an in-flight rename landing between the two reads.

ACCEPTANCE (whichever way it resolves):
1. DECIDE by measurement, not by reading: drive ntp.html in a real loaded extension, rename a named agent so get and list can disagree, and observe whether the header can end stale while history.state is fresh. tests/agent-header-rename-reload.test.ts already has the browser harness and the rename flow to extend.
2. If reachable: the post-await assignment must not clobber a NEWER correction — e.g. skip the assignment when the header already holds a name the list resolved for this same agent id, or have the callback record the resolved name and have :2758 prefer it.
3. If unreachable: record WHY (the measured ordering that makes it impossible) and close. Do not 'fix' an ordering that cannot occur.
4. Either way the guard belongs in tests/ntp-agent-route-execution.test.ts, which already isolates the two paths and carries a listDelayMs knob for exactly this.

NOT A REGRESSION IN 32yz'S WORK: 32yz's tests pass on main and kill three mutants; this is a question its harness surfaced, held separately so a green suite does not imply the question was answered.

title: A stale extension/_emscripten_abi_probe from an interrupted run makes an unrelated change's test:changed red (the refusal is right, its message and leftovers are not)
description:
FOUND while validating an unrelated change (chrome-agent-platform-o3rx): `npm run test:changed` reddened on a check that has nothing to do with the change, and the cause was a STALE ARTIFACT, not a regression.

THE CHECK: `dqxa: prepareLoadedExtension refuses a pre-existing probe before destination copying or injection` — tests/emscripten-abi-loaded-harness.test.ts:252, asserting `Deno.lstat(extension/_emscripten_abi_probe)` throws NotFound. The refusal is CORRECT and worth keeping: the loaded-probe path must never clobber a real fixture or a dangling link.

WHAT HAPPENED: `extension/_emscripten_abi_probe` was present in a fresh worktree (left behind by an earlier loaded-harness run in that tree — the probe dir is created in `scripts/emscripten-abi-loaded.ts` and removed at the end; an interrupted or failed run leaves it). The check then failed for the NEXT run, on a change (scripts/lib/heavy-gate-slot.ts) with no connection to it. The exact check passed alone on re-run, and the whole gate was green afterwards — so the red carried no information about the change under test, which is precisely what test:changed exists to avoid.

WHY IT MATTERS: `test:changed` selects tests through imports, so this fires for any change whose dependency closure reaches chrome-launch → the loaded harness. A lane sees a red it cannot attribute, in a check whose name means "a fixture is in the way", and the true cause (someone's earlier interrupted run) is invisible.

ACCEPTANCE (keep the refusal, improve what it says and what it leaves behind):
1. The failure message distinguishes a leftover from a REAL fixture in the way, naming the path, its mtime, and the one command that clears it (or the marker that identifies it as the harness's own leftover).
2. A leftover created by this harness is either removed by the next run's setup (only when it proves it is its own, e.g. marker/tag/age) or reported as `LEFTOVER`, never as a bare NotFound assertion.
3. The check still refuses a pre-existing probe that is NOT provably a leftover — the mutation that must stay RED: place a non-empty directory (or a dangling symlink) at that path and confirm the refusal fires.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text: CLAIM: cap-ds-flash, worktree ~/worktrees/w6wo-probe-leftover, branch fix/w6wo-probe-leftover. Taking this as the cheapest false-red fix on the board (filed by me, unowned).

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
FIXED AND PUSHED — `fix/w6wo-probe-leftover` @ `79c69fe5`.

**THE DEFECT, as measured:** a run of `tests/emscripten-abi-loaded-harness.test.ts` that stages the reserved probe and is interrupted leaves `extension/_emscripten_abi_probe` behind, and the next run's FIRST line was a bare `assertRejects(() => Deno.lstat(probe), NotFound)` — so an **unrelated** change's `test:changed` reddened with no attribution (that is exactly what happened while I validated `scripts/lib/heavy-gate-slot.ts`).

**THE FIX — one governed rule, shared by the harness and the test's precondition:**
- A staged probe is recorded by an **ownership sidecar**, and the record had to live **outside the tree it describes**: my first version wrote the marker *inside* the probe directory, and the harness's own dist check refused it — `extension/` is an **indexed source authority**, so a file written there changes the closure and invalidates `dist.complete`. The record is therefore a lock-file-style sidecar under the durable scratch dir, keyed on the extension path.
- `probePathVerdict()` → `absent` | `leftover` (path **and** a matching record) | `foreign` (everything else, naming an mtime and, for a symlink, where it points).
- `assertNoExistingProbe()` **still refuses in both existing cases** — the harness never removes anything from a client's tree — but now says *which* it is: a LEFTOVER is named as safe to clear; a path with no record gets the path, its age, and the inspect/clear commands instead of a bare "unexpectedly contains".
- `clearProbeLeftoverIfProvable()` is what the test's precondition calls: it clears a provable leftover with a LEFTOVER line and throws the actionable refusal for anything else.

**MUTANTS AND END-TO-END, all run:** a planted leftover (dir + record) → the previously-reddening check **PASSES** with the LEFTOVER line; the same scenario with the leftover branch removed → **FAILS again** (so this change is what removes the false red); the record requirement dropped → the **"an UNMARKED path is never removed"** test REDs (the safety direction is guarded); and two new tests cover the provable-cleared and the foreign-refused cases (unmarked directory and dangling symlink, both still present after the refusal).

**GATE NOTE, with the exact failing check name per the standing rule:** `npm run test:changed` is GREEN (21/0, 26/0, 135/0), but **`npm test` has 1 failure: `mkax: a real sample from this box is finite, bounded and evidence-shaped` (tests/quiet-window.test.ts:410)** — and it is **not this change**. The parallel phase's own process churn makes 1io9's `/proc` scan exceed its 400 ms budget (verbatim: *"proc scan truncated after 912 entries in 404 ms … so this sample is NOT a quiet verdict"*), so the sample **correctly refuses**, and that test's `measurable === true` assertion reds. It passes alone in 54 ms with load1 63.93 and 1092 /proc entries — so it is the suite's *own* churn, not steady load, that trips it. Filed as **`chrome-agent-platform-2bli`** with that evidence and an acceptance that keeps 1io9's refusal intact.

title: Importing build-bundled-tool-packages.mjs regenerates extension/wasm/cas: isMain gates only the final exit, so the import is impure
description:
FOUND while fixing chrome-agent-platform-4lc0 (the test:changed CAS race). The 4lc0 fix CONTAINS this hazard by ordering and detection; this bead is the durable removal, which its acceptance does not require.

MEASURED: running `tests/tool-descriptions.test.ts` ALONE changes the per-file mtime fingerprint of all 38 files in extension/wasm/cas — and that test does nothing but import the generator for one constant:
  import { AGENT_DESCRIPTIONS } from "../scripts/build-bundled-tool-packages.mjs";
The generator HAS an isMain guard (scripts/build-bundled-tool-packages.mjs:34) but it gates only the final `process.exit(0)` (the tail). Its actual work is at module top level (REPO/WASM_OUT setup at :394-398, the generation loops at :230/:236/:247/:318, the write path at :482), so an importer runs the whole regeneration. In the nco2 subset that regeneration landed inside the parallel phase while tests/gzip-preview.test.ts was reading a CAS file, which failed NotFound — the false red 4lc0 was filed for, now traced to this line.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THAT ONE TEST: "import a constant" is a normal thing for a test to do, and today it silently rewrites the shipped CAS tree. Every future importer inherits a tree-mutating side effect, and the partition only catches it because 4lc0 taught the scan to look for this import shape; a driver imported from elsewhere (or a new build module) would have to be caught again by hand.

ACCEPTANCE: importing the module is PURE. The generation work runs only when it is the main module (wrap the effectful region in `if (isMain) { ... }`, or move it into a `main()` the guard calls) — importing then yields AGENT_DESCRIPTIONS and the other constants and writes nothing. Running `node scripts/build-bundled-tool-packages.mjs` (and `--verify`) must behave exactly as today, including the byte-identical VERIFY output and the deliberate `process.exit(0)` (pozs futex note). Once pure: drop the 4lc0 SERIAL declaration for tests/tool-descriptions.test.ts and return it to the parallel phase, with the EXEMPTIONS reason stating the purity (the scan class may stay — it is what would catch a regression).

NOTE ON SHAPE: a mechanical indent of the whole 900-line module is the wrong form (it buries blame and future merges); a `main()` that the effectful statements move into, or extracting the constants into a pure module the generator imports, is the reviewable version. This is a refactor, not a race fix, which is why it is separate from 4lc0.

title: DRIVER_REF_RE inherits hazards from any prose MENTION of a tests/*.ts file, not only from a spawn — its own comment says 'spawns', so explaining a test in a comment makes your file serial
description:
Found while reviewing cc18 (cap-cc18-treeshake @ bd181152), where it fired on the author twice and forced a workaround that made the code less readable. Not a defect in cc18 and not a blocker for it; it is a defect in the watcher.

THE MISMATCH BETWEEN DOCUMENTED INTENT AND IMPLEMENTATION.
scripts/test-partition.mjs:68-70:
    // A test that spawns one of these local drivers inherits the driver's hazard
    // classification (the hazard lives in the driver, not the test wrapper).
    export const DRIVER_REF_RE = /tests\/[\w.-]+\.(?:mjs|ts)/g;
tests/test-partition-guard.test.ts:46-62 (contentWithDrivers) reads a test file's text and, for EVERY match of that regex anywhere in it, reads the named file and CONCATENATES it before classifyHazards() runs. There is no spawn check: SPAWN_RE is defined at scripts/test-partition.mjs:72 and is not used to gate DRIVER_REF_RE. So the comment says "spawns" and the code implements "mentions" — a comment, a doc string, a TODO or an explanatory note naming a hazard-classified test file makes the mentioning file inherit that file's hazards.

OBSERVED, NOT HYPOTHESISED. The cc18 author's census comment named tests/wasm-tree-shaking.test.ts in prose; that file reads extension/dist, so tests/substring-pin-honesty.test.ts inherited a reads-dist hazard and the partition guard fired on it. The workaround, in the shipped source at tests/substring-pin-honesty.test.ts:~118, is this comment:
    (Its filename is deliberately NOT written here: the partition guard treats a
    `tests/*.ts` mention as a driver reference and would make THIS file inherit that
    file's reads-dist hazard, which is the same exemption-by-assembly reason the dist
    path above is built rather than spelled.)
That is the cost made concrete: a watcher that reads prose as a reference forces authors to OBSCURE which file they are talking about.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE AWKWARD COMMENT. AGENTS.md requires every lane to keep docs/TEST-COUPLING-INVENTORY.md current — "what each watches, the literal grep a re-anchor owes it" — and cc18's own new section 18 does exactly that, naming files in prose. The inventory is a document whose entire purpose is to name watchers and their subjects. A guard that penalises naming a test file is in direct tension with the doc the repo tells everyone to write, and it will fire on every future comment that explains a test.

SEVERITY, STATED PLAINLY SO IT IS NOT OVERSTATED: it FAILS CLOSED. The over-classification moves a file into the SERIAL phase, which is the conservative direction, so it cannot let a real build-artifact hazard through into the parallel phase. The cost is phase placement, suite wall time, and authors writing evasive comments — not correctness. P3, not P1.

FIX SHAPE: gate the inheritance on an actual reference rather than any mention. The narrowest version uses what is already there — only walk DRIVER_REF_RE matches when the file also matches SPAWN_RE, since the documented intent is spawn-scoped. The more precise version requires reference syntax around the match: `from "tests/…"`, `import("tests/…")`, or the path appearing as an argument to a spawn/exec call. Either keeps the real behaviour (a wrapper that spawns a dist-writing driver inherits its hazard, e.g. package-extension-freshness) and stops a sentence from doing it.

ACCEPTANCE: a test file whose ONLY reference to a hazard-classified tests/*.ts is inside a comment classifies as parallel (or keeps its own classification unchanged), while a file that genuinely spawns or imports that driver still inherits it; tests/test-partition-guard.test.ts gains both cases so the distinction is pinned rather than implied; and the evasive comment in tests/substring-pin-honesty.test.ts can be rewritten to name the file it is talking about.

NOT VERIFIED: I did not run the guard with a synthetic comment-only mention to watch it fire — the cc18 author's experience is the observation, and the code path is read from contentWithDrivers. Reproducing it deliberately is the first step of the fix, not a precondition for filing.

title: [bug] The partition guard treats a tests/*.ts mention in PROSE as a driver reference, so a comment explaining a test inherits its hazards
description:
FOUND while landing cc18 (coord ruling seq964 asked for this to be its own bead). Not a blocker today: measured ZERO live false-inheritance cases. Filed because the mechanism guarantees more, and the next one will look like a mystery red.

THE MECHANISM, source-referenced:
scripts/test-partition.mjs:70 DRIVER_REF_RE = /tests\/[\w.-]+\.(?:mjs|ts)/g, and tests/test-partition-guard.test.ts:52 contentWithDrivers() CONCATENATES the full text of every match into the classified text. The intent is correct and load-bearing: a wrapper that spawns a local driver must inherit the driver's hazards, because the hazard lives in the driver (measured: tests/package-extension-freshness-driver.mjs classifies as all three hazard classes while its wrapper tests/package-extension-freshness.test.ts classifies as none, so without inheritance the wrapper would run in the parallel phase and race the rebuilders).

THE DEFECT: the regex matches anywhere in the file text, including comments. A sentence that NAMES another test file is therefore a dependency. PROSE IS A DEPENDENCY.

THE LIVE INSTANCE (2026-09-23, cc18): a comment in tests/substring-pin-honesty.test.ts explaining why its skippedBuildArtifact count moved from 2 to 5 named tests/wasm-tree-shaking.test.ts. That file legitimately reads extension/dist, so substring-pin-honesty inherited 'reads extension/dist' and the guard failed:
  'build-artifact hazard(s) would run in the PARALLEL phase: tests/substring-pin-honesty.test.ts - reads extension/dist'
This is particularly wrong for that file: it deliberately ASSEMBLES its dist path (scripts, line 418: new RegExp with distPath()) precisely so its own text never matches a dist literal, and its section-19 note calls that 'exemption-by-assembly'. A comment undid a deliberate design property. Worked around in cc18 by not writing the filename, with the reason recorded inline; the underlying scanner is unchanged.

BLAST RADIUS, MEASURED at 913d7e80 (this is why it is P3 and not P1):
- 50 test files whose ONLY tests/* references are in comments (examples: acp-fixture-env-guard -> tests/acp-runner.test.ts; agent-worker-loop -> tests/agent-abort.test.ts + tests/agent-worker-host.test.ts; artifacts -> tests/memory.test.ts).
- 4 files with both code and comment references (chrome-test-contract, composer-selector-migration, select-tests-r3, select-tests).
- ZERO of those 50 currently inherit a hazard, because none of the files they name is itself a hazard. So there is no red on main today and no lane is blocked.
- The trap: the moment ANY of those 50 named files gains a hazard (reads extension/dist, writes under extension/, spawns build.mjs), its 50-strong prose referrers start inheriting it. The failure will name the REFERRING file, which will contain no dist literal and no spawn, so the next lane will read a guard bug rather than a comment.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. A tests/*.ts mention inside a comment does NOT contribute hazards. A mention in a CODE position (a string literal, an import specifier, a Deno.Command argument) still does.
2. The true-inheritance case keeps working: tests/package-extension-freshness.test.ts must still classify as a hazard through tests/package-extension-freshness-driver.mjs. That is the positive control and a fix that loses it is worse than the defect.
3. FALSIFICATION, both directions, run not asserted: (a) plant a comment naming a hazard test in a clean file - guard stays GREEN after the fix, and is proven RED before it (the cc18 instance is the recorded instance); (b) plant a CODE-position reference to the same file - guard goes RED. Without (b) the fix is a hole rather than a repair.
4. State in the fix whether the 4 mixed files change classification; none should.

SHAPE (not prescriptive): strip comments before matching, or match only in code positions. Cheapest honest option is a comment-stripping pass in contentWithDrivers() plus the same in classifyHazards()'s caller, keeping the regex. Do NOT solve it by adding referring files to SERIAL or EXEMPTIONS - that hides prose as a dependency instead of removing it, and grows the serial phase for no reason.

RELATED: cc18 (found here), and docs/TEST-COUPLING-INVENTORY.md section 18 which records the same trap from the cc18 side.

title: The pozs descendant assertion flaps: removing the process-group kill only sometimes reds it, so a lost kill can pass
description:
FOLLOW-UP FOUND WHILE FIXING htl8: the descendant-survival assertion in the pozs fixture does NOT reliably notice a lost process-group kill — it FLAPS.

EVIDENCE (same mutant, same tree, repeated runs): removing `process.kill(-r.pid, "SIGKILL")` from the ETIMEDOUT branch of scripts/lib/serial-phase.mjs gives, for the SAME edit:
- run 1: fixture PASSES (exit 0) — the mutant survives, i.e. the check does not notice a surviving descendant;
- run 2 (two mutants in one script): exit 1, no diagnostic printed;
- run 3: fixture PASSES again;
- run 4: exit 1.
So whether the assertion sees the orphan is timing-dependent, and a lost group kill can pass the fixture. That makes the check unreliable for the property it names: "a timed-out serial file leaves no descendant processes behind (process group kill)".

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED, so the next lane does not repeat it:
- An orphan CAN outlive a SIGKILLed parent in this environment: probed directly, both a bash chain (setsid bash -c 'sleep 300 & …' killed with -9, the sleep survived) and the fixture's exact Deno shape (Deno.Command("sleep").spawn() inside a Deno process SIGKILLed; the child survived). The kernel is not reaping orphans, and Deno does not tie a spawned child to its parent's lifetime here.
- The assertion's instrument is `Deno.kill(grandchildPid, "SIGCONT")` inside try/catch: a success means "alive". A ZOMBIE (killed but unreaped) also returns success, so the instrument can only ever report "alive" or "gone", never "gone but not reaped" — worth knowing when reading it.
- The fixture's own `finally` SIGKILLs the recorded pid, so a survivor from a FAILING run is cleaned up by the fixture (no orphan is left behind by the drill).

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: who (if anyone) kills the descendant in the runs where the mutant passes — the fixture's own cleanup runs AFTER the assertion, the harness's group kill is the thing under mutation, and nothing else in the chain was observed to do it.

ACCEPTANCE: make the property deterministic. The shape I would try first: have the fixture prove its own premise BEFORE asserting the kill — i.e. (1) spawn the grandchild so that it demonstrably survives a direct-child kill (a double-fork or an explicit new session, verified by a probe run), then (2) assert that runSerialFile's timeout path removes it. A check whose premise is asserted cannot flap, and a lost group kill must red it every time. Secondarily: print the instrument's reading (pid, /proc existence, kill result) on failure so the next red is attributable.
close_reason: Landed on origin/main at commit 913d7e80eac2348abf07f5187e6ac4f448de5b36. Documented dual mechanism of pozs descendant process kill (spawnSync group kill vs residual group kill) with premise assertion and normal-exit orphan tests (6/6 green).

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
FIXED AND PUSHED — with the bead's central claim corrected by measurement. Branch `fix/iypw-premise-asserted-descendant` @ `a297c35c` (test-only; no version bump, the hook's user-facing filter is right that this ships nothing to users).

THE BEAD SAID "the assertion flaps". IT DOES NOT FLAP — MEASURED:
1. **The timeout path cannot be reddened by that mutant.** `spawnSync`'s own `timeout` + `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` is GROUP-WIDE in this runtime: a bash that backgrounds `sleep 300` and execs a long sleep leaves the sleeper GONE after spawnSync's timeout, with no explicit group kill anywhere. Control: killing ONLY the direct child pid by hand leaves the same sleeper SURVIVED. 6/6 mutant runs passed, and with the branch's own kill instrumented it reports **ESRCH — the group is already cleared before it runs**. So `process.kill(-r.pid, "SIGKILL")` in the ETIMEDOUT branch is redundant belt-and-braces, and the historic 2-of-4 reds were most plausibly htl8's pid-file race firing the OTHER assertion — which the original drill did not distinguish. (The premise half of the original acceptance was therefore necessary but not sufficient: the check was not passing vacuously, it was passing correctly on a property provided twice.)
2. **The residual path is falsifiable, but only for a real orphan.** A Deno process kills the children IT spawned when it exits normally (measured: a `deno run` and a `deno test` that spawn `sleep` and exit leave it gone; plain bash and a plain spawnSync normal return leave it alive), so the fixture's "grandchild" — a direct child of Deno — could never show what the runner's group kill does.
3. **The liveness instrument was itself lying.** SIGCONT succeeds for a ZOMBIE, so a kill that landed and had not yet been reaped read as "survived": the new test reddened a healthy run IN THE PARALLEL PHASE (group kill returned OK, orphan was a zombie). The assertion now reads /proc/<pid>/stat state with a bounded wait — gone/Z = killed; only "still running" fails.

WHAT SHIPPED (tests/serial-phase-resilience.test.ts):
- One probe source for both pozs tests that leaves an ORPHAN (intermediate bash exits) and RECORDS ITS PREMISE: orphan pid, child pid, and both process groups read from /proc. The premise is asserted before any outcome assertion, so a run where the orphan was never in the child's group says PREMISE FALSE instead of passing.
- NEW TEST: "a serial file that EXITS while its orphan lives leaves no descendant (residual group kill)" — the first falsifiable test of the explicit group kill, because in that scenario no timeout kill happens and Deno's exit cleanup cannot reach a grandchild.
- The timeout test keeps its property claim with the redundancy documented in the file, rather than pretending to pin a line it cannot falsify.

MUTANTS (scripts/lib/serial-phase.mjs), all run: **M1** ETIMEDOUT kill removed → BOTH GREEN (the measured redundancy, now documented); **M2** residual kill removed → residual test **RED** ("must not survive a NORMAL exit", 3 s budget) — it could not red before; **M3** premise mutant (orphan escapes the group via setsid) → **PREMISE FALSE** in both tests, so the premise assertion is not vacuous either.

GATES: `npm run test:changed` GREEN twice (141 passed / 0 failed; the same command failed once before the instrument fix), `npm test` at the tip: serial phase (16 files) GREEN in 154 s, parallel phase (477 files) GREEN in 43 s, plus rebuild + check:dist clean. Evidence: ~/cap-evidence/iypw/ (mutant matrix logs, /proc witness timeline, mechanism experiments A–G).

STATE: in_review. Landing is the merger's; a reviewer from another family should check the two claims that carry the bead — that the residual test reds on M2, and that the timeout test's redundancy is the honest reading rather than a weakened assertion.

title: serial-phase-resilience fixture assumes a grandchild pid gets recorded inside a fixed window (load-sensitive timing)
description:
Third red from the same busy-box npm test run (rshb tip, load1 20.9 / load5 43.4), NOT reproduced on the green zeew-tip run minutes later (same suite, load had dropped) — recorded so it is not lost, with the evidence that distinguishes it from a product defect:

OBSERVED: tests/serial-phase-resilience.test.ts "pozs: timed-out serial file leaves no descendant processes behind" (tests/serial-phase-resilience.test.ts:74) → AssertionError: grandchild pid must have been recorded (line 104).

WHAT IT IS: the fixture spawns a serial file that is expected to time out, kills it by process group, and then asserts on a RECORDED grandchild pid. The assertion says the recording did not happen. On a box at load1 20.9 / load5 43.4 the grandchild may not have been observed/written before the kill window closed; on the next run, on a quieter box, the test passed with no change to the tree. So the precondition (a grandchild pid recorded within a fixed window) is ambient-load dependent.

ACCEPTANCE: the fixture establishes its own recording precondition rather than assuming the window is enough — e.g. wait (bounded) for the grandchild's pid to be recorded and fail CLOSED with a diagnostic naming the load and the elapsed window if it is not, or record the pid synchronously at spawn time from the fixture's own process tree rather than relying on an observation race. Do NOT relax the assertion that no descendant survives (that is the property the cgei class cares about).

title: a11y-audit leaks its Chrome profile directory on every run: 13 residue dirs / 71MB in /tmp, and the script has no Deno.remove for it at all
description:
Found while confirming that no browser processes of mine were left running after a test:chrome drive. MEASURED, not inferred:

  ls -d /tmp/cap-a11y-* | wc -l   -> 13
  du -sch /tmp/cap-a11y-*         -> 71M total (8.0M each)

MECHANISM, read from the source. scripts/a11y-audit.ts:49 does:
    const tmp = await Deno.makeTempDir({ prefix: "cap-a11y-" });
and passes it to launchChrome as the profile. The script's teardown (the finally at the end of main()) closes the CDP client, SIGKILLs the browser and closes the docs server — and there is NO Deno.remove(tmp) anywhere in the file (grep for 'Deno.remove(tmp' and 'remove(tmp' both return nothing). So each run leaves a complete Chrome profile directory behind permanently, cleared only by a reboot or a manual sweep.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN 8MB: a11y-audit.ts is class "gate", npm "test:a11y" (scripts/lib/harness-registry.ts:71) and runs inside test:all. A gate that leaks on every invocation accumulates residue across every lane's every full-suite run, on a box where /tmp is shared and where this repo's own conventions exist to prevent exactly that. It is also the same class as bead 2ypf/f99r (a harness that cleans up its browser but not the state the browser wrote).

CONTRAST, which is why I am confident this is a gap and not a deliberate choice: scripts/sidebar-parity.ts DOES remove its profile in its finally block (await Deno.remove(profile, { recursive: true }).catch(() => {})), and AGENTS.md specifies chromeProfileDir(name) from scripts/lib/chrome-profile-dir.ts for exactly this purpose — a per-instance directory under the durable root (~/cap-evidence/cap-chrome-profiles/<name>-<pid>-<ms>-<rand>) with stale dirs self-pruned by pruneChromeProfileDirs() once per kat-runner run (6h threshold, so a live browser is never touched). a11y-audit uses neither: it makeTempDirs into /tmp and never removes it, so it gets no self-prune either.

Note the location itself is probably fine — the rule is that profiles live OUTSIDE the repository, and /tmp satisfies that (tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts scans launch sites and passes today). The defect is the missing cleanup, not the directory choice. Adopting chromeProfileDir would fix the leak AND bring the profile under the existing self-prune, which is the lazier correct answer than adding a remove call.

FIX SHAPE: use chromeProfileDir("a11y") from scripts/lib/chrome-profile-dir.ts instead of Deno.makeTempDir, so residue self-prunes with every other harness's; or, if the /tmp location is wanted, add Deno.remove(tmp, { recursive: true }).catch(() => {}) to the existing finally block alongside the browser kill. Then sweep the 13 existing dirs.

ACCEPTANCE: two consecutive npm run test:a11y runs leave zero cap-a11y-* residue in /tmp (or leave it under the durable root where pruneChromeProfileDirs owns it); the existing 71M is swept; tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts and tests/durable-root.test.ts still green (the latter has an allowlist of scripts permitted to call mkdtemp, so moving to chromeProfileDir may need that entry removed rather than added — check before editing).

ALSO OBSERVED, NOT ATTRIBUTED: 6 cap-sidebar-parity-profile-* dirs survive in /tmp even though that harness removes its profile in a finally block, which suggests runs killed before the finally executed (mine were killed once, deliberately, during the nweh work). And 62+9 cap-fake-browser-lock-* files, which are unit-test fixture lock files governed by tests/chrome-lock-fixture-scope.test.ts and may be entirely intentional — I did not investigate either, and neither is claimed as a defect.
close_reason: Landed on origin/main as v0.3.478 at commit 51f640461608028f19165f635706def256d3ddfd. a11y audit switched to chromeProfileDir('a11y') with group-kill teardown, bounded removal, self-prune, and removed from ALLOWED_FILES. Independent review PASS by cap-gemini (40/0 a11y, 11/11 profile guards).

**WHAT LEAKED, and why the guard permitted it:** the audit created its Chrome profile with an uncleaned temporary directory and had **no removal anywhere** — thirteen directories, 71 MB of residue in a 46 GB RAM-backed mount that suites have already exhausted once (chp). `scripts/a11y-audit.ts` was in `ALLOWED_FILES` in tests/durable-root.test.ts as "ephemeral … script-lived scratch" — and **a file on that list is not guarded**, so the leak was allowed by construction. It is now removed from the allowlist (writing that removal's comment with the old path literal tripped the guard itself, which is the behaviour a text scan should have).

**WHAT CHANGED:** `chromeProfileDir("a11y")` from the house API (durable root, outside the repo, attributed, refusing RAM-backed or in-repo paths); the profile is removed in the audit's own teardown `close()`, which every exit path runs; `pruneChromeProfileDirs()` once per run as the backstop for a killed run (6 h threshold, never touches a live profile).

**TWO ORDERING BUGS IN MY OWN FIX, both found by measuring:** (1) removing the profile while the browser still held it left it half-deleted — swallowed by the removal's catch, so it survived a GREEN run; (2) killing only the DIRECT child left Chrome's helper processes writing into it, and `Deno.remove(recursive)` then failed with **"Directory not empty (os error 39)"** — the pozs lesson: kill the process **group**. The teardown is now group-kill → wait → remove with a bounded retry, and a failure after that **speaks** instead of being swallowed, naming the pruner that takes it later. Without the "speaks" change I would have shipped a silent leak.

**VERIFIED:** audit green (40 passed / 0 failed / 1 expected-red), **zero new temporary directories** (13 before, 13 after) and **zero leftover profiles** in the durable root; then the **thirteen stale directories were swept** (71 MB back). tests/durable-root.test.ts + tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts 11/11.

**GATES, with the three failures named:** `npm test` **GREEN** — 4472 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored, serial phase 17 files. `npm run test:changed` had three failures, **none of them this change** (which touches only the audit and the allowlist): `dnop: the REAL sampler counts this test's compiling process and not its parked ones` (quiet-window.test.ts:181), `mkax: the launcher refuses to START the browser when the box is not quiet` (quiet-window.test.ts:424), and `86gg: the SAME slow file is killed by the flat bound and survives the scaled one` (serial-phase-timeout.test.ts:80, which passes 6/6 alone).

**AND THIS RUN CONFIRMS THE `r2ai` MECHANISM with a second independent occurrence** — the quiet-window failures carry the refusal text verbatim: *"load could not be measured: proc scan truncated after 796 entries in 406 ms (budget 4096 entries / 400 ms)"*. That is an **unmeasurable** sample, not a loaded box, which is exactly what `2bli` and `r2ai` describe: the suite's own concurrent churn trips the /proc scan budget, 1io9's fail-closed refusal fires, and tests that assume a measurable box redden for a reason invisible in their names.

title: A truncated /proc walk in the quiet-window sampler reads as 'no builders' — i.e. as a quiet box
description:
Found while fixing the dnop portability revise (chrome-agent-platform-dnop). Not the cause of that failure — I could not reproduce it — but it is a real hole in the same reading.

THE HOLE: scripts/lib/quiet-window.ts walks /proc under two bounds (MAX_PROC_SCAN = 4096 entries, MAX_PROC_SCAN_MS = 400 ms) and breaks out of the loop when either is hit. The partial scan's count is then returned as the sample's compilers count (and, since dnop, as activeCompilers), and quietReasons treats a low count as a quiet box. So on a box with enough processes (or a slow /proc read) a REAL compiler that the walk never reached is reported as zero builders — the gate opens under a build, which is the exact condition the gate exists to exclude. The same shape as tonight's other findings: a truncated measurement read as a complete one.

WHY IT IS NOT the dnop test failure: on this box with 10 parked esbuild-named and 6 rustc-named processes the walk completed (a temporary diagnostic never printed), so the reviewer's two red tests must have another cause; those tests are now hermetic by construction regardless (calibrated workload duration + pid-scoped assertions).

ACCEPTANCE: a sample whose /proc walk was truncated is NOT a quiet verdict. Either mark it measurable: false with the reason (the module's own contract is 'FAIL CLOSED: if the box cannot be measured, the verdict is a refusal'), or carry an explicit scanTruncated flag that quietReasons treats as a refusal reason naming the truncation. Plus a test that drives a truncated walk (inject the bound through the sampler's own seam) and asserts the verdict is a refusal rather than quiet — and, per the review lesson of 2026-09-23, an assertion whose inputs do not include this box's ambient process count.

NOT IN SCOPE for the dnop branch: that branch is a narrow portability repair; this is a behaviour change to the sampler and belongs in its own review.

CORRECTION NOTE (same session): the first write of this description went through a double-quoted shell string and its backticked identifiers were command-substituted away; it was rewritten from stdin with a quoted heredoc. Recorded rather than silently edited — the second time tonight that shell quoting, not reasoning, damaged a record.
close_reason: Landed on origin/main as v0.3.467 at commit 0a0fb402f85616f9630ecaf38cdb74c3841a2d8f. Truncated /proc walk marks load sample unmeasurable rather than falsely claiming quiet. tests/quiet-window.test.ts 19/19 passed.

title: Static pairing guard: chrome-journeys check() literals must match the EXPECTED ledger at commit time
description:
we0m root cause: the chrome-journeys assertion ledger (EXPECTED at scripts/chrome-journeys.ts:561) is a HAND-MAINTAINED literal array; nothing pairs it with the executed check() literals at commit time — only the runtime finalizer catches a drifted pair, and the full-suite finalizer only fires at the end of a ~370-check browser run, so a rename can leave one half behind for a whole review cycle (it did: we0m).

Build a static pairing guard that fails FAST: extract every check()/report() first-argument literal (including const-bound names: report(name,...) via consts like STEP1_NAME, and the dual happy/catch call sites) and compare against EXPECTED as sets + order; fail the build/test on missing, extra, duplicate or order drift. Reuse the sweep approach proven in ~/cap-evidence/glm-l0r/we0m/l0r-ledger-sweep.mjs plus the const-name resolution it still lacks. Known artifacts to encode, not false-positive on: the about:* catch-handler duplicates (identical names, guarded by ordering), and the catch-only playbook tripwire that deliberately sits outside EXPECTED (check(name,false) at :8025). Same class of ledger exists in scripts/agent-access-journeys.ts — cover it too.

Acceptance: reverting the we0m fix (or renaming any check() literal alone) fails the guard in seconds with the offending file + name; a clean tree passes; the guard itself is falsified by a planted pair fault.

title: Finish the composer-selector migration: the ledgered sites in chrome-journeys, component-gallery-smoke (a gate), 11 KATs, 12 named harnesses, 2 evidence drivers and 4 unit tests to audit
description:

The prior description was written before the first slice was reviewed and corrected two of its numbers; the changes are itemised in the CORRECTION comment on this bead rather than edited silently.

Follow-on to chrome-agent-platform-4vfj, which landed the RESOLVER (scripts/lib/composer-target.ts) and the GUARD (tests/composer-selector-migration.test.ts) on main @ 5d51debf and is closed. This bead owns the remaining migration, which the guard makes mechanical and monotonic: the ledger can only shrink, and any new retired-id site anywhere in scripts/, cap-evidence/ or tests/ fails the build.

CURRENT STATE
- Candidate: branch cap/4vfj-journeys, latest sha 544de67f, based on origin/main 225c7e06. Awaiting review plus a quiet-window npm run test:chrome drive.
- Already landed from this family: test:a11y 36/4 exit 1 -> 40/0 exit 0 (5d51debf); test:security FAIL exit 124 at 120 s reaching 17 of 19 -> PASS 21/0 in 15 s (7770dc89), with the cookie-redaction check now able to fail and proven to by a production mutant (225c7e06, bead nweh).

WHAT THE FIRST SLICE DOES
1. Migrates the chrome-journeys sites that MATTER: :2688 and :2721 bypassed boxOf() and read the retired id directly, coercing an absent element to '' so two multi-slash checks failed on an empty string that looked like a parser regression; plus the sendTask trio at :6262-6264 (:6263 read it directly for a debug line, so it logged on EVERY call and never said why) and the multi-slash Run-task click. All now go through composerInput / composerSend / composerPopup scoped by HOST, because ntp.html carries two composers.
2. Wires the diagnostics. check() was `function check(name, cond)` — two parameters — so a detail argument was discarded and the {error: "composer input not found: <selector>"} payload was never read. It now takes an optional detail and prints it on FAILURE ONLY (truncated to 400 chars), leaving PASS lines and the results element shape untouched so no verdict can move. The detail path is throw-safe: JSON.stringify REJECTS on a cyclic structure, and a diagnostics line must not be able to take the run down.

Adds tests/journey-check-detail.test.ts, which EXECUTES the real check() (source-extracted and compiled with new Function(), the house pattern from tests/journey-cdp-timeout.test.ts) rather than pinning its text — a substring pin on `detail?` would pass with the printing removed. 4. Corrects the ledger's criterion. 38 is a count of matching LINES, not call sites, and boxOf coverage is the real test of what still resolves.

- TS2554 is SEVEN on this branch, NOT zero. All seven are "Expected 2 arguments, but got 1" at fetchJson() call sites (1154, 1206, 1225, 8528, 8534, 8885, 8891), pre-existing on pristine (16 there = 9 "got 3" + 7 "got 1") and unrelated to arity at any site touched here. - deno check differential, deno's own summary: pristine 627 -> branch 618. A differential, never a pass/fail gate.

- M1 detail parameter present but nothing prints it (the original defect): 6 passed / 2 failed, reddening exactly "a failing check PRINTS the detail it was handed" and "a detail that is not JSON-serialisable still reaches the output"; the six safety assertions stayed green.

- Restored: 8 passed / 0 failed. The fix is committed BEFORE the mutants are run, because a `git checkout --` restore against uncommitted work discards the fix along with the mutant and invalidates the differential (that happened once here and is recorded in the CORRECTION comment).

comments.text:
# Independent review — REVISE

Candidate: `36802738775578c52242d05d5f1585b6d93decf9`
Tree: `5726e142ebd2d97853983690bc7bf95022d5ab82`
Base: `5d51debf`; fetched origin/main matched that base when review began.
Worktree: `/home/paulkinlan/worktrees/ady6-independent-review` (detached exact candidate).
Reviewer environment: PI_PROVIDER=openai-codex, PI_MODEL=gpt-6-astra, PI_SESSION_ID=01a0cb65-f67b-74fd-86d8-7c244af8c81a. This is environment evidence of a different family from the reported Qwen author, not a provider-side model attestation.

## Blocking findings

### R1 — P2: neither missing-input diagnostic reaches the reported check

`scripts/chrome-journeys.ts:2703-2705,2738-2740`, reporter at `:547-563`.

The first new `{error: 'composer input not found: ...'}` payload is parsed into skillResolved, but the check receives only its boolean condition. The second check passes `{multiValue}` as a third argument, but `check(name, cond)` neither accepts nor reads that argument. It records `{name, pass}` and logs only `FAIL: <name>`. Both diagnostics are lost. The advertised improvement, distinguishing missing input from a multi-slash product defect, does not happen.

Executable evidence: `node source-probe.mjs` extracts the exact before/after evaluation statements, assertions and check function and runs them in a Node VM with a fake DOM/CDP. With both inputs absent, both checks fail but neither their console output nor result rows contain the error or sentinel. This is source execution, NOT browser evidence. The same probe proves absent legacy inputs fail before the change, and matching stable input values satisfy the candidate checks.

Smallest required revision: carry each error/value into a reporting channel that actually exists, and add an executing missing-input regression check against the real reporting path. If extending check(), ensure the change does not unintentionally expose sensitive details from existing ignored third arguments; there are other such call sites. No evalIn change is required.

The added third argument also produces a NEW TS2554: Expected 2 arguments, but got 3 at :2740. On Deno 2.9.6 / TypeScript 6.0.3, exact `deno check scripts/chrome-journeys.ts` gives **627 errors on base, 628 on candidate**, not the claimed 25/25. Baseline is genuinely already red; this is a count differential plus a specifically identified new error, not a useful absolute gate. Retain/correct the author's command/environment provenance rather than silently replacing their numbers.

### R2 — P2: the ledger's mechanism claim is false

`tests/composer-selector-migration.test.ts:66` and the ady6 bead description/comment claim all remaining 42 mentions resolve through typeInto → clickSel → boxOf, and that only the migrated two bypass it. Counts 44 → 42 are correct **matching-line counts**, not 44 → 42 executable selector sites.

Candidate's remaining 42 lines classify as:
- 32 boxOf/clickSel/typeInto call lines (the compat chain is real).
- 4 lines implementing the boxOf compatibility mapper itself (:378-382).
- 1 legacy-id alternative in a focus assertion (:1442).
- 4 direct DOM queries with their own stable-hook fallbacks (:2779,7928,7953,7974).
- 1 direct stale DOM query with NO fallback (:6263): `document.querySelector('#thread-composer #task-input')?.value ?? null`.

The last is a diagnostic read inside sendTask, followed by logging only; it does not itself veto sending or make an assertion fail. Therefore this review does NOT claim a third broken journey assertion. Nevertheless it is false that every remaining read resolves, or that all remaining lines pass through boxOf. Correct the ledger and bead description, classify that stale diagnostic explicitly, and keep the 'exactly these two red checks' statement scoped to an unmeasured hypothesis.

## Confirmed properties

- The author's self-correction is RIGHT: each original assertion requires a nonempty skill-reference match, and the second also requires a tab-reference match. Empty values fail, not silently pass. The source-extracted execution independently reproduces this.
- Host-scoped stable selectors are correct for the hub; resolver outputs `#composer [data-composer-input]` and `#composer .popup`.

title: diay: the End/keyboard KAT check does not discriminate, though its comment claims it does
description:
Found in independent review of cap-diay-tab-scroll @ f1172e18 (chrome-agent-platform-diay).

WHAT IS WRONG (claim accuracy, not coverage). In scripts/kat-providers-tabs.ts the keyboard block carries the comment:
  // Keyboard: End jumps to the LAST tab, which is off-screen at 360px — this
  // discriminates, unlike a Home check (the first tab is already visible at
  // scrollLeft 0, so Home passed vacuously on the un-fixed tree).
The check is 'at 360px End scrolls the jumped-to tab into the strip's viewport'.

MEASURED: it PASSES on the pre-fix tree. Driven the real KAT in real headless Chrome at 360px against two independent pre-fix builds (a clean d0f01545 build and the canonical a3e35928 build) — both give 16 PASS / 3 FAIL, and the End check is a PASS in both. It is a non-discriminating regression guard, NOT a discriminating check.

MECHANISM: the same one the author correctly identified for click. _onKey -> _select(..., {focus:true}) -> _focusSelected() -> el.focus(), and Chrome's native focus scroll brings the focused tab into view on its own. So the check is satisfied with no component scroll at all.

FULL DISCRIMINATION CENSUS of the 19 checks (branch vs two pre-fix builds): exactly 3 discriminate —
  - 'at 360px the stored default's tab loads scrolled into view (the original bug)'  (this is the strong one)
  - 'a silent re-activation with a visible tab scrolls nothing (nearest no-op)'
  - 'revealing a vertically off-screen tab scrolls the page MINIMALLY (nearest), never a full alignment (block-start)'
The other 16 PASS on both trees. Checks 13 (click) and 14 (page-move guard) are already labelled as regression guards in the driver; check 15 is the one whose comment overclaims.

FIX SHAPE: one comment change — label the End check a regression guard for the same reason the click check is labelled, or assert the keyboard activation on the strip's own scrollLeft in a way that does not depend on focus. Nil urgency: check 16 asserts the same property more strongly and does discriminate, so no coverage is lost.

ACCEPTANCE: the comment no longer claims discrimination the check does not have (or the check is reworked to discriminate and the rework is shown red on a pre-fix build).

title: Migrate persisted recipe: task identities to skill: (alarms + KV re-key + OPFS memory-dir rename)
description:
Follow-on from chrome-agent-platform-l0r (the recipes-to-skills rename): the CODE vocabulary is one vocabulary now, but three PERSISTED identity formats still carry the retired term, and renaming them without a migration would orphan user data.

1. cap:scheduledTasks keys + chrome.alarms names minted as recipe:<id> (service-worker background-agent.set/delete, skill.run run ids). Minting sites + every startsWith("recipe:") match site.
2. Background-agent OPFS memory dirs: backgroundAgentMemory(id) slugifies the schedule name, so dirs are memory/background/recipe-<id> (memory.js backgroundAgentSlug; SW 1382/1390/1457 pass alarm.name). Renaming the identity orphans every background agent's memory/journal/run history — the migration must RENAME OPFS DIRECTORIES (copy+delete, no OPFS rename), fail closed on partial copies, and keep legacy dirs readable.
3. hooks subscription field recipeId (cap:hooks persisted records + hooks.subscribe/unsubscribe tool schema + management-tools.js + pure.js parseOmniboxContent "recipe:" content kind).

Design sketch: one idempotent SW-startup migration (versioned marker), re-key KV map + recreate/clear alarms, rename OPFS dirs with verify, legacy-accept reads retained for one release, falsification fixtures: pre-migration store fixture proves continuity (memory + enabled state survive), interrupted-migration fixture proves fail-closed, no double-fire between alarm recreate and clear.

Acceptance: a profile with enabled background agents scheduled under recipe:<id> upgrades with zero user-visible change (same next-fire times, same memory, same journals); grep shows recipe: only in the migration/legacy-accept layer.

title: check:dist is named and worded as a gate but is deliberately a note that exits 0 - the mismatch is what makes an honest instrument read as a check that cannot fail
description:
FOUND BY the independent review of d0f01545, which observed that dist.complete reports stale in the canonical checkout while `npm run check:dist` exits 0 - and graded that as "a check that cannot fail".

I MEASURED IT, AND THE FRAMING NEEDS CORRECTING BEFORE ANYONE ACTS ON IT.
Driven: `npm run check:dist` prints "[dist] the built extension is stale against this tree: dist.complete validation failed: marker indexed source authority is stale ..." and exits 0. So the observation is true as stated.

BUT THE SCRIPT DOCUMENTS THIS AS DELIBERATE, in its own header (scripts/dist-staleness-note.mjs:12):
  "A NOTE, never a gate: it exits 0 whatever it finds, prints nothing when the build is current or absent, and never touches the tree. It validates the recorded target so a developer/enterprise build is judged against itself."
The file exits 0 at line 26 (no marker) and line 41 (after printing), in both cases on purpose. Its stated job is to name a stale build at the moment it goes stale, because `dist.complete` binds the exact commit - including the post-commit hook's own version bump - so ANY commit invalidates a built tree, and lanes were meeting that as three red serial-phase tests whose message named a marker rather than the cause (chrome-agent-platform-1mz2).

SO THIS IS NOT THE FOURTH INSTANCE OF THE "CHECK THAT CANNOT FAIL" CLASS, and it should not be filed or counted as one. The enforcement is real and lives elsewhere: the serial phase of `npm test` asserts the built tree is current at HEAD and DOES fail on a stale dist.complete. A note that exits 0 is not a check that fails to fail; it is a note doing exactly what its header says.

WHAT IS STILL WORTH FIXING, and it is a real trap even so: the command is NAMED `check:dist` and its output reads as a failing verdict ("validation failed: ..."), while it deliberately gives no verdict. That mismatch is what led an independent reviewer - reading the name and the message as anyone would - to conclude the project has a gate that cannot fail. A reader can make two opposite errors from the same output: treat exit 0 as "clean" when a note printed, or file a defect against a note for behaving as designed. Both happened today.

FIX SHAPE (small, and a naming/wording change rather than a behaviour change): either rename the script to `note:dist` so the name states what it is, or keep the name and make the output unambiguously a note - open with "NOTE (not a gate)" and say where the real enforcement is (the serial phase of `npm test`). Do NOT make it exit non-zero: its documented contract is that a post-commit hook runs it and it must never fail a commit. A test asserting the note never sets a failing exit code would pin the contract so a later lane cannot "fix" it into a gate by accident.

NOTHING PAUL LOADS IS AFFECTED, stated because the observation could be misread as an owner-visible problem: the canonical bundle carries the wiring, and the driver scored 46/0 against it. At the time of measurement the canonical checkout's dist.complete WAS stale (the note printed); it has since been fast-forwarded to the landed tip d0f01545, and the note's own advice is to rebuild.

title: The post-commit version hook infers user-facing from the commit subject — wrong in both directions, and it costs a manual amend each time
description:
Found by ds-flash-2 while landing two ACP fixes (2026-09-18), routed here by coord as "a finding, not a grumble".

## What happens
`.git/hooks/post-commit` runs `node scripts/bump-version.mjs patch --skip-if-no-note --message "$MSG"`. The script derives a "user-facing note" from the commit message and:
- **accepts** it (no jargon word detected) → bumps the version and writes a changelog entry;
- **rejects** it (jargon detected) → prints "does not pass user-facing filter — NOT bumping" and stays quiet.

Both directions are wrong in practice:
- A **bookkeeping** subject with no jargon word passes → consumes a version and writes a changelog entry for work the user will never see. Seen tonight: `0.3.437 → 0.3.438` with the changelog line *"delete the $HOME/journal guess instead of guarding"*, and earlier *"mark the user-visible fix ()"*.
- A **genuinely user-facing** subject that happens to name a component (`harness`, `bridge`) is declined → the user-visible change ships with no note unless the author bumps explicitly.

## Cost
Three rounds of manual amend in one evening: remove the junk changelog block, revert the version in four files (package.json, package-lock.json, extension/manifest.json, extension/lib/bundled-inventory-data.js), then amend with a subject containing a jargon word so the hook declines. Each round is also a chance to leave version drift behind — merger had to resolve `version_name`/release 0.3.437 drift from an earlier round of exactly this.

## Suggested fix, owner's call
- **(A) Stop inferring.** Bump only when the author passes `--user-note "<what the user gets>"`; without it, the hook never bumps. Removes the guessing entirely, and matches the message the hook already prints when it declines.
- **(B) Make it idempotent per branch.** Skip when the branch already carries a bump that is not on `origin/main` (or when the changelog's top entry is not on `origin/main`) — a second commit on the same branch should be free. This alone kills the double-bump.
- **(C) An explicit trailer**, e.g. `Bump: none|patch|minor`, honoured over any heuristic.

A+B together is the smallest change that makes both observed failures impossible; C is optional belt-and-braces.

## Evidence
- `f3f5f4a4` and its first form of `87a9ef7d` (`f57c3387`) both landed as amended commits at **0.3.437** with one plain-language entry after manual cleanup.
- Hook output on each occasion: `[bump-version] commit note "…" does not pass user-facing filter — NOT bumping version (treating as non-user-facing bookkeeping)` when defeated, and `Bumped 0.3.437 → 0.3.438 (changelog: fix(acp): … )` when not.
- Filter: `isUserFacingEntry()` in `scripts/bump-version.mjs` (~line 111/122).

title: Infinity reaches typed-array/count APIs and crashes with RangeError (tool-exec preview bounds; mis-filed as bfbd evidence)
description:
Found while measuring chrome-agent-platform-bfbd (agent-board gates). The phase-2 dptw evidence the bfbd bead points at is not an OOM of the board: `area1-suite.log` shows

    error: RangeError: Invalid typed array length: Infinity
        "overbound": { value: Array.from(new Uint8Array(EXECUTOR_BOUNDS.maxWasmBytes + 1)) },
                                         ^
    at tests/tool-exec-preview.test.ts:98

So the "naive removal" sweep reached a path where `Infinity` became a **typed-array length**. That is a real, small defect in its own right, and it is currently mis-filed as evidence for the agent-board caps:

- `EXECUTOR_BOUNDS.maxWasmBytes + 1` with `maxWasmBytes` unbounded/Infinity → `new Uint8Array(Infinity)` → RangeError, not a controlled refusal.
- The same log records `RangeError: Invalid count value: Infinity`, i.e. a second site where Infinity reaches a count/length API.

Why it matters beyond the sweep: any bound that can be driven to a non-finite value should fail as a **bounded, named refusal** rather than a RangeError from inside an allocation, and a crash-on-Infinity also hides the real bound question behind a crash. Acceptance: with the bound set to a non-finite value, the code path returns a named error (or clamps) instead of throwing from `Uint8Array`/`String.prototype.repeat`; a test pins the non-finite input.

Evidence: /home/paulkinlan/logs/cap-dptw-gates/area1-suite.log (and area1-suite2.log for the count-value variant).
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
FIXED — branch `fix/cqhq-unbounded-bounds-pin` @ `991285c5` (pushed). Two defects, one shape: **a check that cannot see what it claims**.

## 1. A live vacuous case in the suite (not the historical crash)
`tests/wasm-host-gate2.test.ts:1362` claimed an "over-budget" case as `EXECUTOR_BOUNDS.maxResponseBytes + 1`. The byte ceilings are **Infinity by design** (dptw, `wasm-executor-bounds.js`), and `Infinity + 1 === Infinity` — so the fixture was **never over budget**. It is rejected by the **finiteness** clause at `wasm-executor.js:148` (`!Number.isSafeInteger(raw.stdoutBytes)`) while the byte clause it names (`> maxResponseBytes`) is unreachable. Green, for the wrong reason, since the ceilings went infinite. The case is renamed for what it actually exercises, with the reason inline.

## 2. An Infinity bound SILENTLY DISABLES its check
Every `x > bound` comparison against Infinity is false, so a stray non-finite bound removes a refusal without failing anything. The unbounded set is now **pinned**: exactly the eight declared byte ceilings (`maxWasmBytes`, `maxRequestBytes`, `maxResponseBytes`, `maxBinaryResponseBytes`, `maxBase64ResponseChars`, `maxTransportErrorBytes`, `maxFileOpBytes`, `maxWorkspaceRpcBytes`) may be non-finite; every other bound must be finite.

## Falsified before committing
- finite-expected bound → Infinity (`maxSessionIdBytes`) → pin **fails**: `a non-finite bound silently disables its check`;
- a field dropped from the declared set → pin **fails** too.
Both mutants restored byte-exact.

## Class sweep — the answer is "these, and no others"
The `RangeError: Invalid typed array length: Infinity` in `area1-suite.log` came from a **test fixture** doing `new Uint8Array(EXECUTOR_BOUNDS.maxWasmBytes + 1)`, not from product code. Swept the class:
- **no product consumer uses a bound as an allocation length** (`new Uint8Array(BOUND)`, `.repeat(BOUND)`, `Array(BOUND)` — empty);
- every product consumption is either a comparison (`> bound`, safe with Infinity) or `String.prototype.slice(0, bound)` (safe: Infinity clamps to length);
- the only **arithmetic on a bound** anywhere in the repo was the one vacuous fixture above;
- the old log's second site (`Invalid count value: Infinity`) does not exist in the current tree.

So the current tree cannot reproduce the crash; the defect was the *test-shaped* use of a non-finite bound, and the durable guard is the pin (a future accidental Infinity now fails loudly instead of removing a refusal). This change touches **no product code** — 80 passed / 0 failed before and after, on `tests/wasm-host-gate2.test.ts` + `tests/tool-exec-preview.test.ts`, so finite-bound refusals are unchanged rather than clamped away.

title: Acceptance scripts copy the built tree with GNU cp -r and keep a source-relative dist symlink (54k5's sibling class)
description:
WHAT: four acceptance/evidence scripts copy a checkout into an owned directory with GNU `cp -r` (or an equivalent copy) and keep a SYMLINK for the built tree instead of materializing it. Measured on origin/main 0c387326 by name+line in chrome-agent-platform-54k5's sweep: scripts/webmcp-realsite-probe.ts:56, scripts/webmcp-acceptance.ts:185, scripts/kat-webmcp-honest-errors.ts:65, scripts/read-page-host-grant-acceptance.ts:190. The same class was fixed for the permission-variant builder in 54k5 (fs.cp re-bases a copied symlink to an ABSOLUTE path inside the SOURCE tree for BOTH relative and absolute source links: the copied tree then loads the source's bytes, dies when the source is GC'd, and a link-blind attestation still calls it clean).

WHY IT MATTERS: these are the harnesses that produce ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE. A copied tree that reads the source's bytes can report a result about a tree that was never copied — the same 'check that cannot fail' family the fleet spent 2026-09-18 killing. The 54k5 sweep recorded these as not-changed deliberately ('6854 separate' was written in the bead, but 6854 is a closed, unrelated loaded-probe bead), so nothing currently owns them.

WHAT TO MEASURE FIRST (reproduce before fixing): for each script, execute its copy step with a source whose built-tree entry is (a) a relative symlink (the dev-checkout shape) and (b) an absolute symlink, then assert whether the copied tree's runnable path is a symlink, where it resolves, and whether the copy survives the source's build GC. Record the link text before and after, not just 'it worked'.

ACCEPTANCE: every copy these scripts load from is materialized (no symlink escapes the owned copy) or the script refuses to run; the copy is self-contained across source rebuild/GC; and an executed regression proves the prior failure (link text copied verbatim / target inside the source). If a copy is never loaded (evidence-only), say so with the line that proves it and close the finding without a change.

RELATED: chrome-agent-platform-54k5 (fixed the variant builder; its comment records this residual), chrome-agent-platform-gab8 (where the copy defect was discovered).

title: A fresh worktree's serial-phase gate reds on a stale dist.complete marker after the commit hook bumps the version
description:
WHAT: Setting up a worktree exactly per AGENTS.md (npm ci; deno install; npm run build) leaves extension/dist built at version N, then the post-commit hook bumps package.json/manifest/bundled-inventory-data to N+1 inside the same commit WITHOUT rebuilding dist. The next npm test / npm run test:changed serial phase then reds 3 unrelated build-artifact tests with 'dist.complete validation failed: marker indexed source authority is stale' (tests/bundled-tool-packages.test.ts x2, tests/emscripten-abi-loaded-harness.test.ts x1). Observed on cap/u0cc-resume-truth @ 7623b590 (base origin/main 0c387326) after the fix commit's own version bump 0.3.414 -> 0.3.415.

REPRO: fresh worktree off origin/main; npm ci; deno install; npm run build; commit anything (the hook bumps the version); npm test -> serial phase 3/15 failed with the marker error, all three unrelated to the committed change.

WHY IT MATTERS: the red names a build-artifact marker, not the cause (a version bump), so it reads like the candidate broke the build. It cost a full gate cycle here; every lane that commits and then gates hits it.

FIX DIRECTION: either the version bump step rebuilds/refreshes the dist marker (or bumps it as part of the same bookkeeping), or AGENTS.md's setup line and the gate docs say the build must be re-run after any version-bumping commit before the serial phase. Note also that tests/emscripten-abi-loaded-harness.test.ts specifically requires a STORE build (expectedTarget: 'store' in scripts/emscripten-abi-loaded.ts), so 'npm run build' alone is never enough for the full suite; npm run build:production is the one that satisfies both.

ACCEPTANCE: on a fresh worktree, setup + one commit + npm test has a green serial phase without an extra manual build, or the setup/gate docs name the exact rebuild command and the failure message names the version bump as the cause.
acceptance_criteria: On a fresh worktree, setup + one commit + npm test has a green serial phase without an extra manual build, OR the setup/gate docs name the exact rebuild command and the failure message names the cause. SETUP REQUIREMENT (read before wondering why check:dist never fires): the post-commit note lives in .git/hooks/post-commit — OUTSIDE the repo — so landing scripts/dist-staleness-note.mjs does NOT wire it up on a fresh clone or another machine; install the hook pair from the primary checkout (cp scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit scripts/git-hooks/post-commit .git/hooks/ && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/post-commit), and until then npm run check:dist is the always-available check.
notes: SETUP REQUIREMENT (prominent): machine-local hook + tracked script. Landing the script alone wires up NOTHING on another machine. A fresh setup runs: cp scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit scripts/git-hooks/post-commit .git/hooks/ && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/post-commit (from the primary checkout; one install serves every worktree).

title: ACP without a bridge process: Chrome Native Messaging transport
description:
Owner ask (2026-09-12): 'ideally I would like not to have to run a CLI to get acp bridge working'. Partly answered: node scripts/acp-service.mjs install runs the bridge as a launchd LaunchAgent (macOS) or systemd --user unit (Linux) — starts at login, restarts on crash, nothing to babysit. The endgame that removes the process entirely:

- chrome.runtime.connectNative + the 'nativeMessaging' permission; a host manifest (macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/NativeMessagingHosts/<name>.json) with allowed_origins: ['chrome-extension://<ID>/'] — which needs a STABLE extension id (add a 'key' to extension/manifest.json) or the allowlist breaks on every load.
- The host itself is tiny: read 4-byte length-prefixed JSON on stdin, write it out — then proxy to the adapter's newline-delimited stdio. That shim is what scripts/acp-bridge.ts already does, minus the WebSocket.
- The client gains a transport: extension/lib/acp-client.js already takes an injectable transport, so this is a new NativeMessagingTransport + a runtime choice, not a rewrite.
- Wins: no port, no origin guard question (Chrome enforces allowed_origins), no service to supervise, and the 'bridge is not running' error class disappears because Chrome spawns the host per connection.
- Costs: an installer step (a manifest file + a launcher path), a per-OS host path, and CI/browser tests need the host installed (the fixture adapter can back it).

DIRECTION: keep the WS bridge as the dev/headless path; add native messaging as the packaged path, with the same ACP client and the same tests pointed at the new transport.
acceptance_criteria: The extension can drive an ACP adapter with NO bridge process running and no listening port: install one native-messaging host manifest, then a turn works; the existing WebSocket bridge stays supported and tested.

title: The quiet-window harness pins are satisfied by their own import bindings — re-anchor the refusal handler they name
description:
Carved out of chrome-agent-platform-wzez (CLOSED, census delivered and independently verified) as the
audit's actionable tail. Coord assignment 2026-09-07 21:59Z: "take the 3 DEFEATABLE quiet-window
re-anchors as your bead (small, closes the class)". Owner: qwen (01a07d6e). Sequenced AFTER
chrome-agent-platform-c9y8's verdict — this bead touches tests/quiet-window.test.ts only, so there is
no file overlap with c9y8, but the guard extension is what makes these three pins visible to the
committed guard, so landing order matters for the story even if not for the merge.

THE FINDING (census row, mutation-confirmed as mutant W2). Three source-text pins in
tests/quiet-window.test.ts, inside the loop at :327 that walks the harnesses declaring themselves
load-sensitive:

    const src = Deno.readTextFileSync(`${ROOT}scripts/${file}`);
    assert(src.includes("QuietWindowRefusedError"),      `${file} must handle the refusal`);        // :328
    assert(src.includes("ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_EXIT"),   `${file} must exit with the environmental code`); // :329
    assert(src.includes("ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_MARKER"), `${file} must print the marker line`);     // :330

The loop currently has exactly ONE member: `declared` is
`Object.entries(HARNESSES).filter(([, e]) => e.loadSensitive !== undefined)` over
scripts/lib/harness-registry.ts, and only `"chrome-journeys.ts"` declares loadSensitive (verified by
hand at 4c89bd9d — harness-registry.ts:65 is the single occurrence). So all three pins judge
scripts/chrome-journeys.ts, where each token occurs exactly TWICE: once as an import binding at
:34-36 and once in live code at :136-139.

That makes all three DEFEATABLE on the census ladder: live > 0 and shadow > 0, so deleting the live
construct leaves the import behind and the pin stays green.

PROVEN, NOT INFERRED (mutant W2, house discipline, restored + re-hashed + empty git status):
delete the five-line refusal handler at scripts/chrome-journeys.ts:136-140 —

    if (e instanceof QuietWindowRefusedError) {
      console.error(e.message);
      console.error(`${ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_MARKER} ${JSON.stringify(e.sample)}`);
      Deno.exit(ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_EXIT);
    }

leaving `throw e;` and the three imports. Each token drops from 2 occurrences to 1 (import only).
`deno check --no-lock scripts/chrome-journeys.ts` reports 625 errors both at baseline and with the
mutant, i.e. no new syntax or type error (esbuild is unusable in this environment — rc=1 at baseline
too — recorded rather than hidden). Result: tests/quiet-window.test.ts went 13/0 -> 12 passed / 1
FAILED.

THE IMPORTANT HALF: the kill came from :347 "mkax: the REAL journey gate refuses with exit 75 under
artificial load" — an EXECUTING gate that runs the real harness under artificial load and asserts the
environmental exit code. The test that HOLDS the three substring pins, "mkax: load-sensitive harnesses
DECLARE themselves, and the declaration is honoured in source", PASSED with the handler deleted. So the
property is NOT a live hole, and this bead is hygiene, not firefighting: three pins that name a safety
property (an environmental refusal must reach a THIRD exit code with a greppable marker, never be
re-read as a product red) cannot see the deletion of the construct they name, and are backstopped only
by a slower, load-dependent, Chrome-launching gate.

Lesson recorded on wzez and worth repeating here: DEFEATABLE means "a shadow can satisfy this pin",
NOT "this feature is deletable". Only a whole-suite mutant separates those, which is why this bead
exists at P3 and not P2.

WHAT TO DO. Re-anchor the three pins on the CONSTRUCT, parsed rather than grepped, following the shape
ecke landed for bundled-inventory-data (816aae8e) and uodl landed for recordServerToolUsage /
buildTemplateSelect:

1. Pin the handler SHAPE, not the three words: the refusal must be caught by type, must print the
   marker, and must exit with the environmental code — e.g. a single anchored regex over the catch
   body covering `instanceof QuietWindowRefusedError` … `ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_MARKER` …
   `Deno.exit(ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_EXIT)`, or three assertions each anchored on its own construct
   (the instanceof test, the marker print statement, the exit call) rather than on the bare identifier.
2. KEEP IT GENERIC. The assertion runs once per member of `declared`, and a second harness can declare
   itself load-sensitive at any time, so the anchor must describe the required shape (catch the typed
   refusal, print the marker, exit with the code) and must not hardcode chrome-journeys.ts's
   surrounding lines. A pin that only matches today's single member is a pin that silently stops
   covering the next one.
3. Decide explicitly whether the three bare-word pins stay as provenance (the ecke/template-cards
   precedent) or are replaced. If they stay, they stay DEFEATABLE by construction and the committed
   guard will not flag them (live > 0), so say which it is in a comment rather than leaving both nets
   ambiguous.
4. Note for whoever implements: regex literals carrying a backtick or a quote are safe here — the
   guard tokenises regex literals properly (that was the audit's defect #5, and 222 regexes across 21
   target files depend on it).

ACCEPTANCE.
* Mutant W2 RE-RUN and killed BY THE PINS: with the five-line handler deleted, the test that holds
  them — "mkax: load-sensitive harnesses DECLARE themselves, and the declaration is honoured in
  source" — must FAIL, not merely the executing exit-75 gate at :347. Name the killing assertion and
  its message in the report, per house discipline.
* The restored tree must go green again (13/0), with the pristine hash of scripts/chrome-journeys.ts
  re-verified (4f8c205f2e1862d67c1c57799e58e9e3ed38fc9f33dc373865038f4d2aec1272 at 4c89bd9d) and an
  empty `git status --porcelain`.
* Generality proven, not asserted: a second mutant that adds a FAKE harness member declaring
  loadSensitive without the handler shape must be caught by the re-anchored pin, or the pin must be
  documented as single-member-only with the reason. Otherwise the re-anchor is a pin on today's file
  rather than on the declaration rule.
* Repo gates: `npm run build:production` BEFORE `npm run test:changed` in a fresh worktree (the
  store-map tests read the STORE dist.complete marker; a developer-only build leaves it stale and they
  fail with "marker indexed source authority is stale" — environment, not coverage), then `npm test`
  once before push. Post-commit, re-run `npm run check:changelog` and
  `npm run test:file -- tests/changelog.test.ts` — the bump hook writes the changelog entry AFTER the
  gates.
* CAUTION for stage 2: this file's own suite launches Chrome (the exit-75 gate at :347), and
  tests/security-suite-custody.test.ts flocks the machine-global
  /tmp/cap-serialized-chrome-acceptance.lock on a 20s self-timed budget, so a concurrent lane running
  Chrome KATs can red it for everyone. Its failure is NOT a kill. Re-run at rest before believing it.
* Independent review by a different model; push an explicit SHA, never the local main ref.
* NO mass rewrite: three pins in one file. The census's WEAK-STRING rows, build-artifact class and
  interpolated-token class are DECISIONS batched to coord/Paul and are explicitly not part of this bead.

EVIDENCE. cap-evidence/uodl/census-4c89bd9d/CENSUS.md §6 (adjudication + W2), mutation/
mutation-results.json (both mutants, full discipline record), census-attribution.json rows for
tests/quiet-window.test.ts:328-330 (DEFEATABLE, live=1 shadow=1 each, with occurrence lines). The
extended guard from chrome-agent-platform-c9y8 now attributes these three pins, so after this bead
lands they should stop appearing as DEFEATABLE in any future census re-run.

THE CHANGE. The three bare-word pins are replaced by three anchored pins that must be satisfied INSIDE the refusal handler:
  /instanceof\s+QuietWindowRefusedError\s*\)/                                                  -> "must catch the refusal BY TYPE — an import binding is not a handler"
  /instanceof\s+QuietWindowRefusedError\s*\)[\s\S]{0,400}?ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_MARKER/        -> "must print the greppable marker from inside the refusal handler"
  /instanceof\s+QuietWindowRefusedError\s*\)[\s\S]{0,400}?Deno\.exit\(\s*ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_EXIT\s*\)/ -> "must exit with the environmental code from inside the refusal handler"
The import block cannot satisfy any of them (no `instanceof`, no `Deno.exit(`), and the 400-char bounds mean a marker printed in an unrelated statement cannot either. title: Decode filesystem file-URL roots in Chrome acceptance harnesses
description: During nwhc/browser preparation, scripts/chrome-journeys.ts:13 and scripts/kat-wasi-tranche2.ts:7 were read and still derive ROOT via new URL("..", import.meta.url).pathname. URL.pathname retains percent encodings; the source-pinned nwhc same-expression Node counter demonstrated /cap%20checkout/ != decoded /cap checkout/. These unchanged harness expressions are susceptible to the same filesystem-root problem with spaces/nonASCII paths. No Chrome run from a spaced checkout has been performed; this is a source-level portability finding, not an observed browser gate RED or execution escape. Existing current379 checkout has no such characters. Scope: use standard fileURLToPath for these filesystem roots and add persistent spaced/nonASCII path controls. Preserve canonical launcher, port0, waitForServiceWorker, registered lock/semaphore/quiet-window settings, exact behavior/assertions, evidence/cleanup boundaries, and WASI caller arguments. Do not modify the active admission candidate for this follow-up; no blocking dependency on woem or current Chrome set.
